News.title: Kids face daily limits and nighttime blocks on Instagram & Facebook as Meta agrees $17bn payout in teen addiction trial
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

META BLOCK Kids face daily limits and nighttime blocks on Instagram & Facebook as Meta agrees $17bn payout in teen addiction trial

TECH giant Meta has agreed to pay out $17 billion in a landmark trial that will see the social media giant slap stricter limits on kids using its platforms.

A bombshell lawsuit accused Meta-owned sites Instagram and Facebook of deliberately hooking kids and teens on harmful content.



Lawyers representing 49 US states said Meta designed its platforms to keep kids addicted, fueling a mental health crisis.

The lawsuit also alleged that Meta lied to the public about its addictive design features and unlawfully collected data from kids under 13.



The tech firm runs platforms like Facebook, Instagram, Threads and Whatsapp.

In a watershed moment, Meta agreed to a range of sweeping measures to tackle social media addiction in children.

The firm will impose a two-hour daily cap on its apps and block teens from using Instagram and Facebook at night.

“For years, Meta intentionally deceived the public about the addictive and harmful design features that have wreaked havoc on youth mental health”, said Attorney General Jay Jones.

He hopes the settlement “will put an end to these dangerous practices and deliver meaningful relief that will protect children from online harm”.

Meta clapped back and said that creating a safe online environment was “imperative” to the firm.



The trial kicked off last week in California and CEO Mark Zuckerberg was due to appear in court – but the proceedings were cut short after a deal to settle was agreed.

The $17 billion settlement is a fraction of Meta’s 2025 revenue of $201 billion.

The company has now urged other tech giants to follow suit.

News.title: Sara Sharif’s killer dad ‘throttled then slashed with tuna tin lid by two lags who left him “bloodied” on cell floor’
News.content:
JAIL HORROR Sara Sharif’s killer dad ‘throttled then slashed with tuna tin lid by two lags who left him “bloodied” on cell floor’

SARA Sharif’s killer dad was allegedly throttled then slashed with a tin lid by two lags who left him “bloodied” on the ground, a court heard.

Urfan Sharif, 43, was said to have been attacked at HMP Belmarsh, South London, on New Year’s Day last year.



Two inmates, Steven Sansom, 47, and Adam Watson, 39, have been charged with attempted murder.

Westminster Magistrates’ Court was told Sharif was targeted in a “planned and co-ordinated attack”.



Prosecutor Jack Wadsworth said the killer dad was invited into Sansom’s cell where Watson was waiting.

The court heard Watson allegedly “took hold of him and punched him repeatedly”.

Sansom is then said to have grabbed Sharif by the neck and “applied sustained pressure to his throat”.

Prosecutors claim Watson then passed an “unidentified object to Sansom” which he allegedly used to “make repeated cutting motions towards Sharif’s throat”.

The court heard prison officers entered the cell and found Sharif “bloodied and distressed” on the floor, with injuries to his face, mouth and neck.

Both Sansom is further charged with unauthorised possession of an offensive weapon – a tin lid bent to make a weapon, according to the charge sheet.



The two men, who appeared separately by video link from HMP Wakefield, are serving prisoners, the court heard.

They were both remanded into custody to next appear the Old Bailey on September 23.

Tragic Sara was hooded, burned and bitten by Urfan Sharif and her stepmum Beinash Batool as they dished out sadistic “punishments”.



She was found bludgeoned to death with at least 71 internal injuries at home in Woking, Surrey, on August 10 2023.

Sharif, 42, his wife Batool, 30, and brother Faisal Malik, 29, were at the centre of a global manhunt after fleeing the UK after her death.

Once he landed in Pakistan, the evil dad called police to confess his daughter was dead after he beat her up “too much”.

Sharif wept as he and Batool were jailed for life with a minimum of 40 years and 33 years after being convicted of murder.

Sara’s uncle Malik was also jailed for 16 years after being cleared of murder but found guilty of causing or allowing her death.



It later emerged authorities missed at least 15 opportunities to save Sara before her brutal death.

News.title: Boy, 15, arrested after teenager stabbed to death in daylight attack at council HQ near Wembley
News.content:
KNIFE TRAGEDY Boy, 15, arrested after teenager stabbed to death in daylight attack at council HQ near Wembley

A 15-YEAR-OLD boy has been arrested on suspicion of murder after a teenager was allegedly stabbed to death near Wembley Stadium.

Cops had launched a manhunt after David Wynter, 17, was allegedly attacked at a council HQ in broad daylight yesterday.



Officers cordoned off the Brent Civic Centre in Wembley, North West London, after the horror unfolded yesterday afternoon.

Metropolitan Police and London Ambulance Service (LAS) crews rushed to the HQ on Engineers Way at around 2.30pm.



Cops arrested a 15-year-old man yesterday and he remains in custody.

A Section 60 order has been authorised, granting officers enhanced powers to stop and search people and vehicles.

Superintendent Chris Clarke, lead for emergency response policing in the area, said: “This was a tragic incident, and we are aware of the significant concern the stabbing has caused in the local community.

“A police presence remains in and around the crime scene.



“We would like to reiterate that officers do not believe there is any wider risk to the community.”

Images taken from outside the building show a number of emergency vehicles, including ambulances and police cars, parked outside.

Other photos show the entrance inside the building cordoned off with police tape while another shows forensic officers heading into the library.

Some staff, residents and visitors saw the alleged stabbing take place, according to Brent Council leader Muhammed Butt.

Eyewitnesses reported seeing someone “on the floor” after the alleged attack as one said on social media: “I was in the library on the mezzanine level when it happened.



“From what I could see from the balcony was somebody on the floor and splatters of blood. I have no more information than that.”

Another wrote: “I was at the exact same place where the stabbing happened and had gone up to the first floor about ten minutes earlier.

“A staff member walked into the meeting room and told us to evacuate because someone had been stabbed.

“What I witnessed on the way down was unreal.”

The civic centre was evacuated and has been shut down until further notice.

News.title: Stourbridge fire which destroyed 19 houses and left 25 in hospital was started accidentally in field
News.content:
A HUGE fire, that burned down nineteen homes and left 25 people in hospital, was started accidentally in a nearby field.

Families were forced to evacuate as the fire spread across Stourbridge, West Midlands, on August 13.



Investigators have now established that the inferno was sparked by farming equipment.

The fire first broke out near Racecourse Lane in the afternoon with equipment being used in the fields nearby just before the blaze erupted.



Doorbell footage captured by one heartbroken family revealed the extent of the devastation.

Richard and Rose-Anne Vinten only moved into their home five months before the fire broke out.

But, their new house is one of dozens that was destroyed or damaged by the wildfire.

Shocking video released by the couple showed their garden catching alight with just a few flames.



Moments later an inferno was in full force as their house was engulfed by the blaze.

West Midlands Fire Service chief fire officer Simon Tuhill said the fire spread over more than 500 acres in Stourbridge.

He confirmed 19 properties were gutted, with drone footage showing homes completely destroyed and covered in ash.

Speaking today, he added: Chief Fire Officer Simon Tuhill said: “Our thoughts remain with everyone affected, whether directly or indirectly, by events on August 13 in Stourbridge and beyond.

“Many people in Stourbridge face having to rebuild homes and lives and, understandably, have questions as part of that process.



“That’s why we are confirming that both fires were not started deliberately. They were accidental.

“I know that many are still struggling to comprehend the scale of damage and personal loss. I’m also acutely aware that this information will not bring back those homes, livelihoods or cherished memories.

“I remain immensely proud of the response from our firefighters, staff and officers, who worked tirelessly in incredibly challenging conditions to protect lives and property.”

Horrifying aerial footage shows the blaze ripping through a 40-acre residential area, destroying homes and gardens.

Local resident Jane Baxter said she could see the flames from her “bedroom window” and described the “horrendous” choking smell in the air.



She and neighbours were given a few minutes to gather their belongings before fleeing, with the blaze just 200 yards away.

A rescue centre was set up nearby for the families who were forced to flee their homes.

Stourbridge councillor Andrew Tromans said at the time: “The apocalyptic scenes in Norton and across Stourbridge are sadly just a taste of what is to come if we don’t act.

“It is my view, and it has been for a while, that Dudley councillors must have an emergency meeting about [how] we protect our borough from the impacts of climate change.”

Dozens of firefighters were scrambled to fight the blaze, which took hours to bring under control.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Police launched an investigation into the cause of the Stourbridge inferno, with reports of it starting in a nearby grassland before spreading to homes.

West Midlands Fire Service has now confirmed that the blaze was started by farm equipment.

News.title: Woman who killed husband & dismembered his body before dumping remains in bags across city reveals why she did it
News.content:
‘HAD ENOUGH’ Woman who killed husband & dismembered his body before dumping remains in bags across city reveals why she did it

A WIFE has confessed to killing and dismembering her husband before scattering his body parts in bin bags across Sydney.

Nirmeen Noufl, 55, pleaded guilty to manslaughter and revealed that her 30-year marriage had been riddled with abuse and infidelity.



Nirmeen revealed the grim series of events which led up to the death of her husband Mahmoud Noufl’s death in May 2023.

She claimed they had a violent argument with Mahmoud, 62, chasing her from room to room before pinning her to the kitchen floor and trying to choke her.



Fearing for her life, she grabbed a nearby tool lying around from the house renovation and stabbed him in the chest.

Two months later Mahmoud was reported missing – and in October 2024 Nirmeen was charged with one count of murder.

She had been due to appear in court for a mammoth 40-day murder trial – but at the 11th-hour Nirmeen pleaded guilty to manslaughter.

She confessed to killing her husband in their Greenacre home sometime between May 3 and May 4, 2023.

The couple’s more than 30-year marriage had reportedly been turbulent – with multiple counts of alleged violence and infidelity.



Days before his death, Mahmoud had revealed that he was having an affair – and planning to marry his mistress.

Nirmeen initially demanded a divorce – but then resorted to more desperate measures, unable to ignore “the voices in my head”.

A witness had spotted Nirmeen with a cut to her forehead, bleeding lip and a swollen jaw on the night of the killing.

The same witness, who cannot be named, also said they had seen a “large round saw” beneath plastic tarp on the floor of the house.



She later dismembered the body and scattered the remains across suburbs in Sydney.

His strewn corpse is yet to be found – making it difficult to establish how he was killed.

Acoording to court docs, Nirmeen told a friend that she “had enough” of being treated “like sh*t”.

“We had a fight and he was laughing at me”, she told a witness who cannot be identified.

“He just treated me like sh*t, spat at me. I had enough.



“I have been trying to ignore the voices in my head.

“I’m sorry and that I regret it, but I genuinely believe it didn’t happen, and I don’t know how I did it.”

Documents suggest that Mahmoud – who held conservative Islamic views – had been “controlling of his wife”.

He refused to divorce her – even after telling her he planned to elope to Egypt with another woman.

The mistress had been sent around £8,000 (550,000 Egyptian pounds) to buy a new home abroad – but two weeks after Mahmoud’s death, she received a Facebook message demanding the money back.



Unaware that her lover had been killed, she asked for a voice message from the sender.

The unidentified messenger replied: “You have no shame. You know that this money belongs to my wife Nirmeen. So even if she is the one sending the message, she (has) the right to demand it from you.”

Nirmeen had access to her husband’s Facebook account – but court docs do not confirm whether she was the sender.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

For two months Nirmeen kept up the ruse that her husband was still alive, sending messages from his phone and turning away relatives who tried to visit by saying that he was tired and did not want to see anyone.

She said he “did not want to talk to anyone because he was embarrassed and ashamed about his affair”.

News.title: New hosepipe ban is announced for first time in over 30 years for 1.2million Brits – and it’s coming into force TOMORROW
News.content:
A NEW hosepipe ban is being introduced for over a million Brits for the first time in 36 years.

This is the tenth supplier in England and Wales to introduce restrictions as nearly three-quarters of Brits face drought conditions.

Bristol Water has confirmed that a temporary hosepipe ban will come into force tomorrow to protect the River Severn’s water resources as a result of drought.



This is the first hosepipe ban the supplier has introduced because of drought since 1975 and generally since 1990, with around 1.2million Brits set to be affected.



Richard Stanbrook, director for drinking water services at Bristol Water, said: “Introducing a hosepipe ban is never a decision we take lightly, and we fully appreciate the inconvenience it will cause.”

Large parts of the South West of England will be affected, with the ban covering Bristol, Weston Super Mare, Portishead, Glastonbury and other locations.

Bristol Water has confirmed that the restrictions will be enforced in its supply area from 0.01am on Thursday, August 27.



Under a temporary use ban, customers cannot use a hosepipe, sprinkler, or pressure washer for various activities, such as watering plants or filling up hot tubs.

Anyone caught breaking the rules can face a £1,000 fine, unless an approved exemption or loophole is in place.

The supplier joins around half of the UK’s water companies have introduced hosepipe bans throughout the summer, including Thames Water, Wessex Water and Southern Water.



This follows a summer of prolonged dry conditions and five heatwaves, with drought declared across 70 per cent of England and the entirety of Wales, with Bristol and the South West affected.

During this period, Bristol Water says that half of its water has come from river sources, resulting in a significant impact on the River Severn’s resources.

The South West of England currently has the lowest reservoir capacity in the entire country, according to Defra, as resources continue to be stretched.

Wimbleball reservoir, about an hour’s drive south of Bristol Water’s supply area, is considered to have exceptionally low water levels for this time of year.



If your water supplier is affected, it is important to check their website to find out if your postcode has been impacted by temporary use bans.

Blue Badge holders, and those on the Priority Services Register, are exempt from the rules as well as those who require the use of a hose for a medical purpose.

News.title: Bizarre truth behind the haunting Cat in the Hat ‘serial killer’ terrifying Brit kids… and the even scarier paedo threat
News.content:
“I’M COMING… LOCK YOUR DOORS” reads the sinister caption on a viral TikTok video of someone dressed as Dr Seuss character The Cat in the Hat dancing robotically.

The clip, which racked up a million views, joins a legion of others showing the children’s book favourite in similarly menacing scenarios – and it is leaving UK kids and teens terrified.



Some have claimed an individual in the costume carried out assaults, stalked them while walking home at night and sent “threatening messages” warning of a plan to carry out “violent acts”.

Youngsters in every corner of the country have been terrorised by TikTok footage and photos of the creepy cat.

But it is all a hoax. Artificial intelligence is behind the creepy creations – all made for online clout, followers and money.



In just over a week, the wild speculation about this mythical ‘attacker’ has caused such concern that police in Wexford, Ireland, were forced to share a post debunking the theories and outing the clips and photos as fakes.

They claimed to have received a number of distressing reports of the cat “causing havoc in neighbourhoods and towns across the country”.

A spokesperson added: “To be clear, the Cat in the Hat was not in your driveway while you were out and he is not currently hiding out in [the village of] Curracloe.”

Similarly, South Yorkshire Police had to denounce a fake online account pretending to be them, which wrongly claimed there was “suspicious behaviour” in the Meadowhall area.

The phony post urged homeowners to lock all windows and doors, insisted that extra police patrols had been ordered and said they were taking the incident “seriously”.



An SYP spokesperson encouraged the public not to believe everything they see online and jokingly added: “We can also confirm no recent sightings of his associates Thing One and Thing Two.”

While the claims of a Cat in the Hat killer may seem laughable, teenagers and children around the UK believe and fear it.

Multiple clips showing the eerie lifelike character alongside the locations he will strike in next have spread like wildfire. And, worryingly, some parents are adding fuel to the flames.

In response to Wexford police’s statement, one person claimed: “He was in Coolcotts last night chasing kids with a knife. My daughter showed me the video.”

Another insisted “it’s not AI” because their daughter “saw him in Ashford the night before last”. Hysterical fear has spread among young people.



Ellie, 16, from the Scottish Borderlands, told the BBC: “I was so scared of him when I was little. Now it’s like he’s actually come to life to haunt me.”

Another, Skye, 16, decided to leave a friend’s sleepover at 3am because she was so worried after watching clips of the freaky feline.

“I wanted to go home,” she said.

“When I started walking down my friends’ driveway, I got totally freaked out that the Cat in the Hat was going to jump out. I had to call my mum to pick me up.”

More concerningly, one account observed by Lily, 14, claimed they would be arranging a “meet and greet” for TikTok followers in the woods near Galashields, near Scotland.



Thankfully, she spoke to her mum, who rightly warned her there could be a predator, paedophile or attacker waiting for anyone who attended.

She told Lily: “You are not going to meet anyone in the woods in the middle of the night!”

No police force so far has expressed any concern about a Cat in the Hat ‘attacker’ – but it’s clear from posts seen by The Sun that some people on social media have their concerns.



On an Essex Facebook community group, one person anonymously posted that their younger siblings had received “threatening messages” on Snapchat and TikTok.

They wrote: “This was from a user called the ‘cat in the hat’, messaging them that they will be committing violent acts and to lock their doors and windows as they are ‘coming to Loughton.’”

The individual, whose claims are unverified, said one sibling, who has a learning disability, was “panicking” and they feared the kids would be “scared to leave the house”.

They claimed they had contacted the police and urged parents to ensure their children’s social media accounts had the location feature disabled and to warn kids about the hoax.

One mum in St Helier, Jersey, claimed on a community board that she had seen an individual dressed like the character “running around quite erratically”.



She admitted being uncertain if it was “teenagers messing around” or a genuine threat, before adding: “It really scared my six-year-old.”

Another lady in Mansfield, Nottinghamshire, shared screenshots of an exchange with her daughter where she begged her to lock all windows and doors.

The message read: “There’s a cat in the hat lurking [a]round Mansfield and police have even sent a warning on Facebook… it’s so scary, people are getting chased.”



The hoax comes a decade on from a viral ‘killer clown’ trend, where individuals would dress as clowns and lurk near schools, dark roads and forests to scare people.

Often they would film the reactions of the spooked strangers to upload online. The phenomenon spread from the state of Wisconsin across the US and then to the UK, Europe and Australia.

Other iterations, all attempting to recreate the posts’ viral success, have followed, including someone who dressed as Stephen King’s Pennywise the clown from IT.

Now these hoaxes are more easily spread because AI can create lifelike people and scenarios for videos and photos. It’s easily achievable with a few clicks on a smartphone.

Last year, an AI prank saw a daughter trick her “extremely concerned parent” into believing she was home alone with a homeless man she had taken in.



The mum was so scared that she called Dorset Police, who attended the scene and discovered it was fake. They then urged people to conduct research before calling 999.

It’s likely police forces across the UK are cautious to give oxygen to this new Cat in the Hat attacker hoax and will want to ensure already-stretched police time isn’t wasted.

The trend’s origins are unknown, but one theory pointed to a viral post on X, formerly Twitter, about the original costume from 2003 film The Cat in the Hat being listed for auction.



The furry outfit, which is tipped to sell for £17,500 under this hammer on Wednesday, was labelled “genuine nightmare fuel” and “scary as f***” by commenters.

On the August 8 post, which received 10 million views, one person wrote: “This is a horror movie in the making.”

Another clip that showed someone dressed in the original Cat in the Hat costume was captioned “Help, what do I do?” racked up 15 million views.

Seeing the viral popularity achievable may have inspired people to turn to AI to create their own creepy clips for online clout or to make money.

“An AI image costs seconds to make but ‘buys’ millions of views,” Ruth Azar-Knupffer, Co-Founder at VerifyLabs.AI, tells The Sun.



“The platforms also pay in reach, followers and sometimes in money, for exactly the emotions this material produces.”

In addition to this, Ruth suspects that for some people “frightening teenagers has some kind of pay-off” for them. Others like sharing conspiracies without thinking about the consequences

She believes the public at large needs to have access to deepfake detecting technology to avoid falling for these types of hoaxes again.

She tells us: “The lesson is that the public is unarmed. Verification is currently a service sold to institutions while the people actually being targeted are left to squint at their screens and guess.

“Until everyone has access to a deepfake detector, they will continue to be the victims of other people’s imaginations, however dark those imaginations get.”

News.title: Will the lunar eclipse be visible from my area? UK weather forecast for the Blood Moon – and best time to see it
News.content:
STARGAZERS across the UK are gearing up for a spectacular celestial show this week as a stunning “Blood Moon” takes to the skies.

Those who set their alarms for the early hours of Friday, August 28 will be in for a treat as the UK experiences a partial lunar eclipse – with over 93% of the Moon’s face plunging into the darkest part of Earth’s shadow.



It will look almost identical to a total lunar eclipse, and you can even leave the specialist eyewear at home.

A lunar eclipse occurs when the Earth positions itself directly between the Sun and the Moon, stopping sunlight from directly reaching the lunar surface.



During a near total lunar eclipse, the Moon is bathed in a dramatic red, copper-like glow caused by the Earth’s atmosphere – hence the nickname “Blood Moon”.

It’s a sight you won’t want to miss, but to fully appreciate it, you’ll need a decent break in the clouds.

When is the best time to see the lunar eclipse?

The eclipse is an hours-long event, but the action kicks off at 2.23am on Friday, August 28, as Earth’s outer shadow first touches the Moon, causing a subtle dimming.

The partial eclipse officially begins at 3.33am, when a distinct dark “bite” will appear across the lunar disk as it enters the Earth’s main shadow.

The peak of the eclipse will arrive at 5.12am, when maximum coverage will cause the Moon to glow in dramatic reddish-orange hues – the “Blood Moon” effect.

Around 6.15am, the Moon dips below the horizon, wrapping up visibility across the UK.



How to get the best views of the eclipse

Getting a good view of peak eclipse will require some forward planning, due to how low the Moon will be in the sky – roughly eight degrees above the west-southwest horizon.

Your primary goal is securing an unobstructed line of sight.

Seek out high ground like a local hilltop, an open park, or a west-facing coastline to ensure tall buildings, trees, or hills don’t block your view.

While the red glow of the Moon will be bright enough to spot from suburban back gardens, stepping away from light pollution and city streetlights will make the spectacle more vivid.

Unlike the solar eclipse seen earlier this month, you can leave the specialist eyewear in the drawer and look directly at the Moon with the naked eye.



You don’t need to bring any special gear, but if you’re lucky enough to own a pair of binoculars or a camera with a zoom lens, you should be able to get a closer look at the crimson-lit craters.

What is the weather forecast where you live?

Your best-laid eclipse plans may be scuppered if the Great British weather refuses to play ball, and cloud cover is the ultimate threat to skygazers.

The Met Office has issued its latest update, but says that “weather conditions are expected to be challenging for many hoping to see the eclipse.”

If you live in the South or East of England, you may have drawn the lucky ticket, at least to start with.

The Met Office says: “The best initial viewing opportunities are… likely to be across southern and eastern England.



“These areas are expected to remain relatively cloud-free from around 2am, potentially allowing observers to see the opening stages of the eclipse.”

But for many others, the start of the eclipse is going to be hidden behind a blanket of grey.

“At the beginning of the event,” says the Met Office, “cloud is forecast across Cornwall and Devon, Wales, the Midlands, parts of northwest England, and most of Scotland and Northern Ireland.”

But “cloud amounts are also expected to build elsewhere across the UK, meaning conditions may become increasingly unfavourable before the eclipse reaches its maximum at 5.12am.”

There is slightly better news if you live in the North East of England, where “patchier cloud is expected,” meaning you might just get lucky and spot the red Moon peeking through the gaps.



The Blood Moon weather forecast where you live:

Cornwall & Devon: Cloudy from the start of the event, creating generally challenging early viewing conditions.

Cloudy from the start of the event, creating generally challenging early viewing conditions. Midlands & Northwest England: Overcast skies expected early on, with cloud amounts building as the night progresses.

The Met Office says that though “the greatest chance of seeing something is likely to be across southern and eastern England during its earlier stages… there may not be one location offering ideal conditions throughout.”

“Cloud cover can vary over relatively short distances,” it says, “so those planning to watch should check the latest local forecast before setting out.”

News.title: UEFA to drop World Cup boycott after FIFA promise over Gianni Infantino plan
News.content:
UEFA to drop World Cup boycott after FIFA promise over Gianni Infantino plan

UEFA had pledged to boycott FIFA competitions in response to Gianni Infantino's controversial plan to sell stakes in tournaments such as the World Cup to private investors

View 2 Images UEFA remain the biggest threat to Gianni Infantino (Image: Nicolò Campo/LightRocket via Getty Images)

UEFA is set to drop its boycott of FIFA competitions. It comes after football's European governing body was given guarantees that FIFA will not repeat Gianni Infantino's plan to sell stakes in the World Cup.

‌



UEFA and its 55 member associations are due to meet on Thursday ahead of the Champions League draw in Monaco where further discussions are likely to take place. UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin has been outspoken on FIFA's ill-fated plan and the English FA joined the rest to promise a boycott of future competitions which could even threaten the participation in future World Cups.

‌



That could have affected the under-20 Women's World Cup which is first on the horizon next month but that threat now appears to have passed. UEFA sent a letter to FIFA with support from the 55 member associations threatening legal action after Infantino's sell-off plan and made it clear they would boycott competitions.

‌



They made two conditions for the boycott threat to be lifted which was for FIFA to withdraw the sell-off proposal and the second was for 'assurances' that it would never happen again. UEFA clearly feel they have got those guarantees and the action is on hold but that has not changed the position that the European nations still want to remove Infantino as president.

News.title: King Charles and Camilla to travel 10,000 miles across three Caribbean countries for next major royal tour
News.content:
King Charles and Camilla to travel 10,000 miles across three Caribbean countries for next major royal tour

King Charles and Queen Camilla are set to travel a total of 10,000 miles for their next royal tour to Antigua and Barbuda, The Bahamas and Guyana

View 5 Images King Charles and Queen Camilla will travel to the Caribbean for their next major royal tour

The King and Queen are to embark on a huge 10,000 mile journey across three countries for their next major royal tour.

Charles and Camilla will travel to Antigua and Barbuda to coincide with their attendance at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) 2026. Palace officials will be hoping the King and Queen are welcomed to the country, following the last major royal tour of the Caribbean in 2022 by the Prince and Princess of Wales being marked by several controversies.

The then Duke and Duchess of Cambridge were criticised for the way in which they greeted locals during one event in Jamaica, shaking the hands of children through a wire fence, and not engaging with protestors demanding reparations for Britain’s role in the Transatlantic slave trade.

View 5 Images The Prince of Wales wears a native head dress whilst joining in on a traditional dance during a visit to the Iwokrama rainforest, in Guyana, during his Caribbean tour in 2000 (Image: PA)

Queen Camilla will be key figure in Harry and Meghan return to royal life READ MORE :

Antigua and Barbuda has in the past signalled its intension, along with Jamaica, to follow in the footsteps of nearby Barbados to ditch its historic association with the British Crown. As yet, no new legislation has been passed apart from a constitutional amendment approved by Parliament in December 2025, which formally removed the requirement to pledge loyalty to King Charles III, his heirs and successors.

View 5 Images The Prince of Wales gets a warm greeting from Carlton Pickering, a local man who insisted on being phototgraphed, with the Prince during a walk-about in Linden, Guyana in 2000 (Image: PA)

When Antigua and Barbuda’s new cabinet was sworn in May, following prime minister Gaston Browne securing an unprecedented fourth consecutive electoral victory, for the first time, elected officials pledged allegiance directly to the country, ending a more than 40-year tradition of swearing loyalty to the British sovereign. Royal sources said the King and Queen were “immensely looking forward to the Autumn tour”.

Prior to CHOGM, the King will undertake a visit to The Bahamas, of which he is also head of state. Charles will then undertake an official State Visit to Guyana, at the invitation of the President of Guyana and at the request of the UK Government.

View 5 Images The Prince of Wales standing near the Kaieteur Falls, in Guyana, the highest continuous single drop waterfall in the world, where he visited in 2000 (Image: PA)

Buckingham Palace said the visit “will mark 60 years of bilateral relations between the UK and Guyana.” The King and Queen’s Autumn Tour “will celebrate communities, cultures and Nature within the Commonwealth family”, a statement from the palace added.

The Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) will be held from November 1-4 in St John’s, Antigua and Barbuda, and will bring together leaders from the 56 Commonwealth countries, as well as representatives from business, civil society, and youth organisations. Charles, 77, is expected to deliver a keynote address at the gathering - in his role as Head of the Commonwealth.

View 5 Images The King, as Prince of Wales met displaced Barbudans as he visits the National Technical Training Centre to meet residents of Barbuda who were displaced by the Hurricanes of September 2017 (Image: Getty Images)

The theme of this year’s meeting is 'Accelerating Partnerships and Investment for a Prosperous Commonwealth'. The King, when Prince of Wales, visited Antigua and Barbuda in November 2017, following the widespread devastation caused by Hurricanes Irma and Maria.

He has also previously made official visits to Guyana in February 2000 and The Bahamas in July 1973. The upcoming visit will be the first official visit to Antigua and Barbuda by the Queen.

News.title: Landline users urged to take action as switch-off deadline looms - what you need to do
News.content:
Landline users urged to take action as switch-off deadline looms - what you need to do

The UK's traditional phone network is being switched off in January 2027 as services move to digital technology, meaning households with landline phones need to make the transition to internet-based calls before the deadline

View 3 Images Households will need to switch to a digital landline (Image: PinPep)

Almost half of UK landline users are unaware of the analogue phone switch-off, despite the January 2027 deadline fast approaching. The country's traditional phone network is being decommissioned as services move over to digital technology, meaning households with landline phones will need to make the shift to internet-based calls.

‌



A survey of 2,000 adults with a landline telephone in their home revealed that 53% use it on a weekly basis, yet 45% don't fully understand what steps they need to take ahead of the switch-off to ensure their phone continues to work.

‌



Landlines remain essential for many, with one in three relying on theirs to stay in touch with friends, family and healthcare providers. The majority of those surveyed said their landline is still a crucial part of their household, with 17% stating it's cheaper for overseas friends or family to call them on a landline rather than a mobile.

‌



View 3 Images TV Chef Rustie Lee (R) has teamed with Community Fibre to raise awareness of the switch off (Image: PinPep)

The research was commissioned by Community Fibre, which provides broadband and calls packages enabling customers across London and the south-east to seamlessly switch to a full fibre home phone service.

TV chef Rustie Lee, who regularly uses her landline, has teamed up with the broadband provider to help raise awareness of the upcoming change. She said: "The landline switch-off is one of the biggest changes to our home phones in years, so if you haven't switched yet, there are a few things you need to do.

‌



"My top tip is this: don't just accept the first deal you're offered by your current provider. Take a moment to shop around, especially look at the newer fibre broadband providers as they will often save you a lot of money.

"The extra good news is that switching to a new fibre provider is also simple and risk free. You can keep your telephone number, and your new provider can handle the switch on your behalf with your current provider so you won't have any break in service."

View 3 Images The landline may be connected to other devices such as alarms (Image: PinPep)

‌



The landline transition could also affect other devices in the home. These include alarms designed to help elderly or vulnerable people live independently by connecting them to a 24/7 emergency response centre, as well as some home security systems.

Rustie added: "If you use a telecare alarm or other devices that use a phone line, check with the providers of those services if they'll be affected too, rather than your phone company."

Peter Rampling, a broadband expert at Community Fibre, said: "The switch from analogue to digital phone services is a nationwide change that is affecting millions of households.

Article continues below

"But unfortunately, many of those needing to switch may not be offered the best available full fibre service by their existing provider, so it's important to explore what else is out there before committing.

"Whether you're sorting your own line or helping someone else to do it, shopping around and switching provider makes absolute sense with the cost-of-living crisis and can save money and effort in both the short and the long run."

News.title: Shameless couple 'dine and dash' from Tenerife restaurant – even taking leftovers in boxes
News.content:
Shameless couple 'dine and dash' from Tenerife restaurant – even taking leftovers in boxes

Traditional Spanish eatery El Cañonazo in Santa Cruz de Tenerife, posted a video on Instagram of a couple with blurred faces seemingly exiting the restaurant without paying

View 3 Images Traditional Spanish eatery El Cañonazo posted the video on Instagram (Image: @guachincheelcanonazo/Instagram)

A shameless couple who allegedly “dined and dashed” from a Tenerife restaurant reportedly even had the audacity to take their leftovers with them. Traditional Spanish eatery El Cañonazo in Santa Cruz de Tenerife posted a video on Instagram of a couple with their faces blurred, seemingly exiting the restaurant without paying.

‌



The incident took place on Saturday, August 22, with the El Tablero eatery's CCTV capturing footage of the alleged "dine and dash" . In the clip, the couple appeared to depart the restaurant calmly.

‌



Adding to the staff's fury, the man could be seen carrying their leftovers out in a silver container, having just enjoyed lunch at the restaurant. El Cañonazo's managers expressed their anger in the post's caption.

‌



They said: "We’re so angry, and to make matters worse, there’s nothing we can do about it; we can’t publish their faces or report them because nobody’s helping us… It’s so infuriating! What would you do?"

View 3 Images The man could be seen carrying leftovers out in a silver container (Image: @guachincheelcanonazo/Instagram)

It marks the latest in a reported rise in "dine and dash" incidents across the Canary Islands’ hospitality industry. Local newspaper Diario de Avisos reports that it's fuelled both frustration and financial losses.

‌



Data protection laws prevent the release of the alleged offenders' faces publicly without court approval. And it appears to have left El Cañonazo feeling powerless.

Merely 10 days prior to the incident, the Japanese restaurant Aiko Sushi, situated in the centre of Santa Cruz de Tenerife, disclosed that they'd been lumbered with an unpaid bill totalling 144.50 euros (about £123) from August 12.

Two women left the establishment without paying, but had left a phone number for the purposes of making the reservation. Aiko Sushi tried to call the number but was allegedly blocked, so it had to resort to legal action.

‌



Similarly, La Vespa restaurant in La Matanza de Acentejo experienced a dine-and-dash in June, this time by a family of four. A couple and their two minors enjoyed a large meal, but claimed their card wasn't working.

View 3 Images The El Tablero eatery's CCTV captured footage of the alleged "dine and dash" (Image: @guachincheelcanonazo/Instagram)

Having pledged to return with cash that day, staff spotted them waiting at a bus stop - allegedly to leave the area. Traditional eatery El Fogón in La Laguna saw a group of young people dashing on a 200 euro (around £170) tab in March.

Article continues below

However, in an unexpected turn, the father of one of the alleged culprits went to the restaurant to settle the entire bill after the incident surfaced on social media. He also apologised for his son's behaviour.

One incident in the Cruz Chica area involved two customers who left without paying. They left a mobile phone behind in the restaurant and were quickly identified.

And in yet another case at Arepera 23 in Caletillas, diners reportedly walked out on a €120 bill (about £100). It came after a dispute over an item on the bill.

News.title: Terrified mum claims to have photographed a PANTHER prowling through her Northampton estate
News.content:
Terrified mum claims to have photographed a PANTHER prowling through her Northampton estate

The mum-of-eight says she fears for children living nearby after photographing the mysterious creature, weeks after another suspected big cat was spotted in Northamptonshire

View 3 Images The photo shared by Clare Hodges which she claims she took near her home (Image: Clare Hodges / SWNS)

A terrified mum says she ran for her life after coming face-to-face with a huge black animal she believes was a panther prowling near her home.

‌



Clare Hodges, 51, had stepped outside to put her bins out when a noise behind her caught her attention in the Ryehill area of Northampton. Expecting to see a fox known to visit the neighbourhood, the mum-of-eight instead spotted a large black creature with a long tail just yards from nearby homes.

‌



Clare managed to take a photograph before racing back inside, where she showed the startling image to her partner Joseph. The full-time carer, who looks after her autistic 11-year-old daughter, said: “It was terrifying. I was putting the bins out when I heard a noise behind me.

‌



View 3 Images Clare believes the animal may have made its way from Harlestone Firs Forest (Image: Tony Kershaw / SWNS)

Wild beavers could return to UK area in bid to reduce flood risk and protect against drought READ MORE :

Fox found hiding in cupboard in MP's Westminster office before being escorted out READ MORE :

“ The neighbours had been leaving out some raw lamb for a lovely vixen we have in the area at the minute and we’d been trying to get a photo of it for some time so I had my camera ready already. So I thought it was the fox and turned to get a quick image and then within a second or so I thought ‘oh s**t, what is that?’.

"It was very big and I just ran quicker than I have ever done in my life into the house, shut the door and showed my partner Joseph. I thought it could be a big dog at first, like a Dalmatian with no spots, but then we saw the tail was not like a dog at all.”

‌



Clare says she is now frightened about what could be roaming so close to families’ homes. She told Sell Your Story: “It’s actually terrifying how close to homes it has decided to get. Panthers can be extremely quick and could have got either one of us if it had wanted. I’m worried for the safety of my daughter and other children in the area now.

“She lives in her own little bubble due to her autism so it’s really aware of danger. The other weird thing is that all the cats in the area hadn’t been out for a few days before it happened. So I wonder if its been the area for some time. I think it must have been attracted to the meat which had been laid out in the street for the fox.”

View 3 Images People are questioning whether Clare used artificial intelligence (Image: Tony Kershaw / SWNS)

‌



Clare believes the animal may have made its way from Harlestone Firs Forest, a large area of woodland a couple of miles from her home where she says there have previously been rumours of big cat sightings. She added: “There have been rumours of big cat sightings up there before but what is worrying is how far it came into a built up area. Its a quiet area here but there’s still lots of houses and flats so it’s extremely worrying.”

But not everyone was convinced by Clare’s extraordinary picture after she shared it online, with some questioning whether the image had been created using artificial intelligence. Clare insists the photograph is genuine. She said: “Afterwards I posted the image on my Facebook page and while some people were amazed others didn’t believe me.

"Some said it was AI but it really isn’t - I wouldn’t know how to do that anyway and I don’t have the time to looking after my daughter. Put people can think what they like, but we know what we saw. A lot of people have pointed out the panther like features. Some said they had never seen a clearer picture of a big cat before and never before so close to homes.”

Article continues below

Big cat expert Tim Whittard said: “If authentic then this shows a very large feline animal alarmingly close to people’s homes.” The apparent sighting comes just weeks after another large cat was reportedly spotted elsewhere in Northamptonshire.

There have been a number of possible big cat sightings across Northamptonshire and neighbouring Rutland over the years, including tales surrounding the so-called Beast of Rutland. Northamptonshire Police confirmed they received a report on August 6 of a large cat seen in fields in a village near Corby but said Clare’s latest reported sighting had not been reported to the force.

News.title: Mum-of-four, 37, died in horror house fire as husband 'climbed up drainpipe' in desperate bid to save her
News.content:
Mum-of-four, 37, died in horror house fire as husband 'climbed up drainpipe' in desperate bid to save her

Kate Mulcahy's desperate husband tried to save her by scaling their Middleton, Manchester property and attempting to enter the attic room where his wife was sleeping

View 4 Images Kate Mulcahy, 37, died in a horror house fire (Image: Facebook)

A beloved mum-of-four died in a horror house fire as her husband clambered up their home's drainpipe in a desperate bid to save her, an inquest has heard.

‌



Kate Mulcahy, 37, died in a "ferocious" blaze that ignited early in the morning at her home in Middleton, Greater Manchester, in November 2024. Rochdale Coroners' Court heard that Mrs Mulcahy's husband became aware of a fire at their property at around 4am on November 10, just over a couple of hours after Mrs Mulcahy returned home from a baby shower at 1.30am.

‌



Her young children were led to safety thanks to the help of her neighbours and husband, bricklayer Mr Mulcahy, but he was unable to reach his wife before she died in the blaze.

‌



View 4 Images Mrs Mulcahy's husband scaled a pipe to the roof of their home in Middleton and attempted to gain entry in a desperate bid to save his wife (Image: MEN Media)

The court heard that Mrs Mulcahy had been sleeping on the top floor of the family's five-bedroom detached property, where the fire is believed to have started. When he became aware of the flames and their location, desperate Mr Mulcahy scaled the side of their home and reached the roof, where he smashed a skylight window and even removed roof tiles.

Despite his heroic efforts, the flames were too intense for him to battle, and he was forced to retreat. Pictures from the aftermath of the fire show the damaged skylight and exposed roofing from where he tried to remove the tiling.

‌



Firefighters raced to the home, where they were able to extinguish the flames, and they tragically discovered Mrs Mulcahy dead inside. Coroner Michael Salt concluded her death was an accident, adding that the cause of the fire was undetermined. Mrs Mulcahy's heartbroken sister, Emma Cropper, paid a tribute to the "best mum, sister and auntie" following her death, and remembered "her kindness, laughter and warmth touched so many lives".

The "outstanding mum", she said in a public post on Facebook, will be "missed deeply". The post read: "She really was the best, and I will miss her until my last breath.

View 4 Images Firefighters raced to the scene but were unfortunately unable to save Mrs Mulcahy, who they confirmed had died (Image: MEN Media)

‌



"She really was the best Mum, Sister & Auntie, and I can't imagine a world without her in it. I’m so lucky as we have so many memories shared, but so sad we won’t make anymore." Tim Ainsworth, a neighbour, said he had heard "loud bangs" and dogs barking next door before Mr Mulcahy dropped his children on his doorstep.

The neighbour added that the dad was "screaming in panic" and appeared in a state of "sheer terror" as he watched him climb the drainpipe to his roof.

He recalled seeing "really large" and "intense" flames, and was met by an impassable "all of fire" as he attempted to enter the property himself to help. He said in a statement: "I thought if anyone was in that room, they wouldn't have survived." As he tried to help, he witnessed Mr Mulcahy throwing tiles off the roof and shouting "Kate" at the "top of his voice".

‌



Mrs Mulcahy died as the result of "burns and the inhalation of fire fumes", a post mortem confirmed, with forensic pathologist Dr Jamie Robinson unable to find evidence of an assault, injury, or underlying disease.

View 4 Images Investigators have been unable to conclude what caused the fire (Image: MEN Media)

Investigators found a vape and cigarette lighter in Mrs Mulcahy's handbag, which was in the room. The court heard the "careless use of smoking materials" could not be ruled out as a potential cause of the fire. It was, however, "just a possibility" that they were involved in the incident.

Article continues below

The court also heard that specialists could not exclude the "incendiary failure of an electrical appliance" or "naked flame ignition of combustible materials by one of the occupants".

Detective Inspector Kim Tallis-Hines said she was satisfied there was no evidence of any suspicious circumstances or third-party involvement. Coroner Mr Salt, concluding Mrs Mulcahy's death was accidental, said: "These are circumstances that have been thoroughly investigated. Sadly, for various reasons, we don’t know 100 percent what took place."

News.title: Brit mum hails Dolly Parton's 'legacy' after Imagination Library helped son develop 'amazing literacy skills'
News.content:
Brit mum hails Dolly Parton's 'legacy' after Imagination Library helped son develop 'amazing literacy skills'

EXCLUSIVE: A British mum has told how Dolly Parton's Imagination Library helped her young son develop a love of reading, as the star's remarkable book-gifting legacy continues after death

View 4 Images Dolly Parton launched the Imagination Library in 1995 (Image: ABC via Getty Images)

Dolly Parton has left a lasting legacy for millions of children across the world through a book-gifting scheme she set up more than 30 years ago.

‌



The country music legend, who died aged 80 after a brief battle with cancer, founded the Imagination Library to help children develop a love of reading from an early age. The scheme sends youngsters a free, age-appropriate book addressed personally to them every month from birth until they turn five.

‌



The Imagination Library was initially launched in Dolly’s native Tennessee in 1995 in honour of her father, who could not read or write but who she considered the smartest man she knew. The scheme stretched across the globe, with children in the UK also receiving the books. The mum of one of those children has spoken to the Mirror about the huge impact the programme has had on her children.

‌



View 4 Images Christina Partington reading a gifted book with her children (Image: Christina Partington)

CHRIS BUCKTIN: Dolly Parton was the Queen who united America when almost nothing else could READ MORE :

Christina Partington, 37, who shares family content on Tiktok, is mum-of-two to Louis, four, and Penelope, one, enrolled in the library two years ago after a local councillor invited the family to join. She has noticed significant growth in Louis since he began receiving the books.

She said: “He is excited for his present from Dolly every month when he sees it on the door mat. We have read to him every day and he’s starting school in September and is starting to read and write some simple words. Having access to books from an early age has given him the foundation to develop these amazing literacy skills.”

‌



She told the Mirror: “I know the charity gives kids from deprived areas access to books that they might overwise get. What a legacy she has left.”

Christina has since spoken to her son about Dolly’s death, and he said he is sad he never got to meet her. She said: “He said he loved the books and hopes he still gets his monthly present from Dolly.”

View 4 Images The Imagination Library has gifted more than 300 million books across the world (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Louis also said his favourite books are the ones with dinosaurs and looks forward to night time for his bedtime story. The library later expanded around the world, with Dolly launching the programme in the UK in 2007 and the first books sent to children the following year.

Since then, she has gifted more than 300 million free books to children across the world, including in the UK, US, Canada, Australia and the Republic of Ireland. The Imagination Library operates through around 100 local partner organisations in the UK, including local authorities, councils and charities.

Among those to benefit is Essex Virtual School, a team of education experts and advisers which tracks and champions the education of vulnerable children. The virtual school has been signed up to the scheme for four years and has noticed a “huge” difference.

‌



Sharon Halsey, PEP and virtual school operational lead, said: “On average the charity has provided around 100 books a month for children in care and those known to social care under the age of five... It’s been very positive, the families that have had the books have said it’s been lovely to get a new book each month, to be able to share that with the child. It creates bonding and conversation.”

“Nationally every body saw libraries have seen a decline for visits from families, because the pressures from lives. It was an additional offer for our younger cohort. It goes through the post marked for the young person themselves, it’s really personal to them. The books are focused on the age of the child, and if there is a young person that has special needs there can be a request that their books are aimed at a lower age group.”

View 4 Images The Imagination Library was close to Dolly's heart (Image: NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty Images)

‌



The library has also expanded to include bilingual and braille books and is funded through her Dollywood Foundation and local community programme partners. Dolly set up the Dollywood Foundation in 1988 with the aim of helping children in her home county of Sevier County, Tennessee, succeed at school and improve graduation rates.

Three years later, she launched the Buddy Program in a bid to tackle the number of youngsters dropping out of school. Pupils were asked to pair up with a fellow student, with Dolly promising each of them $500 if they both went on to graduate. The initiative was credited with helping cut the local dropout rate from 35 per cent to just six per cent.

Dolly’s philanthropy stretched far beyond the foundation and Imagination Library. In 2000, she launched the Dolly Parton Scholarship, which awards $15,000 to five graduating students in Sevier County each year. Over the years, the star also raised and donated money to causes including hospital maternity units, women’s services, families who lost their homes in wildfires and hurricane relief efforts.

Article continues below

But Jeff Conyers, president and vice chair of the Dollywood Foundation, said the Imagination Library was particularly close to the star’s heart. He said: "A lot of people know Dolly in a lot of different ways. She was so talented, you know, as a songwriter and a musician and an actress. But, I think one of the most special things about her was just how big her heart was for all people and humanity and especially for this program, inspiring children.”

Jeff said the Imagination Library was particularly close to the star’s heart. He said Dolly was a “huge dreamer” from a young age who grew up with little but had faith she would go on to “do something big in the world”. He added: “And so when she got the opportunity to build something like the Imagination Library and give that gift to millions of children and families around the world and do that in a way that honored her father and her mother, I just really can’t think of anything that was more important to her.”

The Imagination Library will continue following Dolly’s death, with the Dollywood Foundation saying the programme was built to “last for generations”.

News.title: Murder probe as two people dead in house fire in Middlesbrough
News.content:
A murder investigation has been launched after two people died in a house fire.

The blaze in Grangetown, Middlesbrough, broke out just before 05:30 BST and also left a woman in hospital in a critical condition, alongside a further three people who suffered non-life threatening injuries.

Cleveland Police said it was investigating what had happened but was "keeping an open mind and cannot rule out any links to wider organised crime at this time".

The fire happened about two miles from the A66 crash that killed five young men and two police officers on Saturday morning.

Redcar and Cleveland Local Policing Commander Supt Emily Harrison said the force was working to "establish the circumstances of exactly what has happened".

"We will have a high visibility presence in the Grangetown area as this investigation progresses, and to provide reassurance to local communities, who will no doubt be impacted by this tragic incident."

Patrols have been increased in the local area to "reassure the local community", the force said.

News.title: Prince Harry and Meghan land in UK days after announcing move
News.content:
The Duke and Duchess of Sussex have arrived back in the UK, BBC News understands.

Prince Harry, Meghan and their children Archie and Lilibet are believed to have flown into the country privately from California, and landed in Birmingham shortly before midday.

A spokesman for the Duke and Duchess of Sussex said "this is not something we would comment on".

There did not appear to be a police presence as Harry and his family left the airport, a source told the BBC.

Last week, it was reported that the couple would be relocating to the UK in August. They will not return to official duties but will live in Britain as non-working royals.

It is thought the family will base themselves at a private property outside of London in the Cotswolds area.

Archie and Lilibet have been enrolled in school and the new term is due to start next week.

The Sussexes left the UK and stepped back from their royal duties in early 2020, before settling in California in March that year.

King Charles was told of the move earlier this month. The family visited the King at his Highgrove home in July this year, but it is understood the move was not discussed.

Before that visit, Prince Harry and Meghan had not been in the UK together since they attended the funeral of Queen Elizabeth II in 2022.
