Sports.title: Forest in talks with Celta Vigo over Javi Rueda as Axel Disasi joins Palace on loan
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest are in talks over the €15m (£12.8m) signing of the Celta Vigo right-back Javi Rueda, which would probably be their final incoming of the window after Liam Delap from Chelsea.

Oliver Glasner has been seeking someone who can play right wing-back and the 24-year-old former Real Madrid academy player fits the desired profile.

The former Spain youth international joined Celta three years ago from Madrid, who will receive half the fee. He made his first-team breakthrough last season, playing 26 La Liga games and 11 in the Europa League, helping his side to reach the quarter-finals.

Forest confirmed on Wednesday that the wing-back Eric da Silva Moreira will spend the season on loan to the Dutch side Excelsior to aid his development.

Chelsea have agreed to sell Delap to Forest in a deal worth £50m and have loaned Axel Disasi to Crystal Palace for the season. Disasi has also been borrowed by Aston Villa and West Ham since he signed for Chelsea from Monaco.

The defender said: “I know that it’s very tough to play against Palace at Selhurst Park – so I’m looking forward to being on the other side now.”

Brentford have struck an agreement with West Ham to sign El Hadji Malick Diouf for £35m plus up to £5m in add-ons. The left-back has been keen to leave West Ham since their relegation.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 5: Charlton Athletic
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 14th (NB: this is not necessarily Sophie Downey’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 3rd (WSL2)

Prospects

Just under 20 years since Charlton’s successful women’s team were disbanded after the men’s team’s relegation from the Premier League, they are finally back in the limelight and ready to make a name for themselves again.

Karen Hills’s side impressed for much of last season, going on a 27-game unbeaten streak and possessing the meanest defence in WSL 2. A mid-season blip harmed their race for the title, however, and they lost out to Birmingham City on the final day of the season, ultimately going through a playoff to achieve their goal of promotion. Beating Leicester in that game will have given Hills and her players confidence that they can compete. There will be no complacency, however, having seen how newly promoted sides have fared in recent history.

Six players have departed since last season, including the influential Katie Bradley But they have been replaced with a blend of knowhow and exciting young talent. The arrival of Ashleigh Neville and Emily van Egmond will bring experience to Hills’s dressing room. Leah Davidson’s and Grace Johnston’s arrivals from Australia are intriguing moves. Meanwhile, Sophie Whitehouse was the hero of the previous campaign and Charlton will be looking to the goalkeeper to again lead from the back. It is the attacking side of the game that perhaps causes the most concern. Charlton managed only 31 goals last season, the lowest of the WSL2’s top six.

Preparations got under way with a pre-season trip to Cádiz, a chance for a new-look side to come together. There is no doubt that the task to stay up is a challenging one, but a club that have defied the odds on more than one occasion will believe they can do it again.

Off-field picture

A record-breaking partnership has seen haircare brand Sofnfree become the women’s team’s official sleeve partner. The branding will feature on all playing and replica shirts this season, while content creation will be a focus as Charlton hope to access new and existing audiences. The club have also launched their first women’s-centric TikTok channel. The news, however, that ownership group Global Football Partners have put the club up for sale could cause a bit of instability in the short term.

The manager

Reaching the Women’s Super League was part of the five-year plan Hills had when she was appointed in 2021, bringing a club close to her heart back into the limelight. The 51-year-old represented Chartlon for six years as a player, winning the FA Cup in 2005. This is the second time in Hills’s coaching career she has guided a team to the top flight, having previously done so with Tottenham in 2019, and watching Charlton walk out at the Valley against Liverpool on 6 September will inevitably be an emotional moment for her.

View image in fullscreen Karen Hills has guided a club into the top flight for the second time after have done so with Spurs in 2019. Photograph: Tiego Grenho/Alamy

Star signing

Only three months ago, Neville was lining up against Charlton in the promotion playoff. Now she is a fully fledged Addick, joining from Leicester on a two-year deal. The full-back brings with her a wealth of experience having made more than a century of appearances in the WSL. The majority of those were under Hills at Tottenham after arriving there from Coventry United. A tough-tackling, intuitive defender, Neville never shirks a challenge and has the ability to push forward. She will also be a strong leader in the dressing room.

Stat attack

Despite finishing third in WSL2, Charlton kept the joint-most clean sheets and conceded the fewest goals in the division. No club saved as high a percentage of their shots on target faced, with Whitehouse playing every minute. She saved four penalties in the playoff shootout, too.

Set for a breakthrough

Johnston was named Charlton’s first signing of the summer during a transfer window that has seen many A-League players depart for Europe. The versatile young full-back arrives at the Valley hoping to make her mark on English football after three seasons with Perth Glory. She impressed during her time with her home town club, played every minute of last season, winning the club’s 2026 best young player award. Johnston’s form led to her being called up to the Young Matildas in 2023, representing the under-20s and now the under-23s. She was an integral member of the squad that won the Asean Women’s Championship last year.

What they say …

“I know what Karen’s about and vice versa; she knows what I bring. I’m really looking forward to working with her again” – Ashleigh Neville

Where are they playing their home games?

Charlton will play their home games at the Valley for a third consecutive season. Season-ticket sales started almost immediately after their successful promotion push. Alcohol will also still be allowed in the stadium, with an alcohol-free section established. Other fan activations include giving supporters the opportunity to sponsor a player.

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Jean-Philippe Mateta to Aston Villa?
Sports.content:
Liam Delap may not have broken any records during his time with Chelsea but he is setting one on his way out the door. The England youth international is thought to be breaking Nottingham Forest’s transfer fee record with Oliver Glasner bringing him in for an expected £50m. The fee comes despite a disappointing 2025-26 season with the 23-year-old striker scoring only one Premier League goal.

Injury problems with his shoulder and hamstring did not help but the lack of return means the Blues were open to selling the striker and Forest have taken the bait. If Delap does sell for £50m it also means Chelsea will make a £20m profit on the player after buying him from Ipswich for £30m in 2025.

Delap isn’t the last deal Forest want to get over the line before Monday’s deadline day either as they are interested in Corinthians and Brazil midfielder André.

One story that is gathering momentum like a ball in snow is Jean-Philippe Mateta moving to Aston Villa. The Villans have made Crystal Palace an offer for the France striker but it is a long way off what the London club would like.

A departure that could finance Mateta’s move could be that of Ollie Watkins, though it is one that has shocked Villa. It has been extensively reported the English international has interest from Saudi club Al-Hilal with his signature set to be worth about £59.8m. Villa are close to agreeing the move and it is understood Watkins would have an annual salary of £12m.

With deadline day approaching, last-minute signings will come out of the woodwork at every turn. Let’s rattle through some. Manchester United are interested in Stuttgart defender Finn Jeltsch, Newcastle have submitted a bid for Lille winger Matias Fernandez-Pardo, West Ham defender El Hadji Malick Diouf may play in the Premier League again with Brentford close to a deal for the Senegalese player, newly promoted Hull have agreed a move to sign Ilyas Ansah from Union Berlin in a deal worth £20m and Tottenham are pushing to sign Omar Marmoush from Manchester City.

If Spurs did get that move over the line for the Egypt forward then the club’s spend this summer would be close to £400m. It is no wonder fans looked lost for words at Tottenham’s 3-0 loss to Brentford last weekend.

We started with Chelsea so let’s end with the Blues. Enzo Fernández, who was met with a wall of boos when Chelsea played Fulham in their opening fixture, may not play in London for much longer. Manchester City will submit a bid for the Argentina midfielder before deadline day. If they do, it could be the biggest transfer of the summer so far with Chelsea reportedly wanting £120m for the 25-year-old.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

So Fernández may travel up the M1 and M6 but the boos are likely to follow him after he scored and showboated in England’s defeat to Argentina in the World Cup semi-final.

Sports.title: Steve Bruce was sacked at EFL club for subbing new Premier League star for £15m transfer
Sports.content:
Steve Bruce was sacked at EFL club for subbing new Premier League star for £15m transfer

Steve Bruce has told talkSPORT how delighted he is to see one of his ex-EFL stars finally make his Premier League debut last weekend.

The legendary former Premier League boss has overseen the careers of hundreds of players across the 12 clubs he has managed.

5 Thomas-Asante made his Premier League debut against the reigning champions Arsenal Credit: Getty

The 65-year-old, who is now a talkSPORT regular, hasn't been in the dugout since October 2025, when he was let go by Blackpool.

Bruce, who has been tipped for a management return at the top level, admitted poor recruitment led to him being axed at Bloomfield Road.

The same can't be said of his West Brom tenure, in which he plucked Brandon Thomas-Asante from Salford City for £300,000 in 2022.

The 27-year-old has enjoyed a meteoric rise to make his Premier League debut for Coventry City in their 3-0 defeat to Arsenal.

Thomas-Asante scored 13 goals and registered four assists under Frank Lampard to help the Sky Blues win the Championship title.

He was part of Ghana's World Cup squad this summer, coming off the bench to set up the Black Stars’ winner against Panama - although he was an unused substitute in their goalless draw with England.

Only four years ago Thomas-Asante was playing alongside Bruce's son Alex at Salford, having embarked on a non-league tour before that.

Steve Bruce opens up on Brandon Thomas-Asante

Speaking to talkSPORT.com on behalf of Free Bets, home of the best UK betting sites, the Manchester United legend said: "When I was out of work I watched a bit of Salford with my son being there, and I always thought, 'He's got something.'

"You'd give him the ball, and something can happen."

5 Salford City co-owner Neville had mixed emotions when getting the call from his old Manchester United teammate about Thomas-Asante

The reason Bruce got the West Brom sack

Thomas-Asante, who joined West Brom on deadline day 2022, scored a last-gasp equaliser on his debut to earn a 1-1 draw against Burnley.

He followed that up with another goal on his second appearance for the club, but their partnership ended a month later when Bruce was sacked following a goalless draw at home to Luton Town.

The ex-Sunderland and Newcastle gaffer even admitted that his decision to hook Thomas-Asante against the Hatters led to his demise, with the Hawthorns crowd turning against him.

Bruce added to talkSPORT: "I remember saying to him at West Brom, and it was a big, big occasion for him with all his family, and you could feel that hunger and desire.

"I think after half an hour at West Brom, he became a cult hero all of a sudden. In fact, the reason why I got the sack really at West Brom was I took him off.

5 Thomas-Asante applauding the West Brom fans after he was withdrawn against Luton in Bruce's final game in charge Credit: Getty

5 He ultimately scored 18 Championship goals over two seasons for the Baggies

"I took them off, and the crowd shouted, 'You don't know what you're doing.'

"I brought on Karlan Grant, who was 15 million quid's worth.

"But yeah, I mean I'm delighted. Look, that's the nice part of management when you've given somebody a chance, and I believe there's still some younger players in and around the EFL who need a break.

"He's certainly one who proves the point. He went on, and now he's playing in the Premier League. I'm delighted for him.

"He's a good kid with a big heart, and I hope he does well."

5 Bruce watched his old West Brom side against his son Alex's Rotherham United in the Carabao Cup earlier this month Credit: Getty

Steve Bruce still misses management

Having managed over 1000 games in his post-playing career, Bruce told talkSPORT: "Look at how blessed I have been.

"I've been very fortunate, I think somebody up there, though, to have both Sheffield clubs, both the Northeast clubs, three clubs in the Midlands.

"I've managed big clubs and managed their rivals, but look now I've been blessed that I've had the opportunity to manage over a thousand games.

"Especially when I was younger, I always thought I'm not going to be able to do this... I had three, four clubs within two years.

"It took me a while to settle down. I still miss it to this day.

"Still miss it to this day, the day-in and day-out of preparing the team and getting the team ready for the weekend."

Sports.title: ‘Not OK’ – Ally McCoist questions decision to boo new Premier League manager after two games
Sports.content:
‘Not OK’ – Ally McCoist questions decision to boo new Premier League manager after two games

Ally McCoist has defended football fans' right to boo their team after Nottingham Forest were jeered during their loss to Leeds United.

However, the talkSPORT co-host has questioned whether such a reaction from supporters helps the situation.

3 Oliver Glasner's Forest were booed after their second defeat to Leeds in three days Credit: Getty

His remarks follow Forest's 2-0 Carabao Cup second round defeat to Leeds at the City Ground on Tuesday night.

The reverse marked a second loss in three days to the same opponents in front of their own fans.

It leaves new Forest boss Oliver Glasner with two defeats from his first two matches in charge.

The former Crystal Palace manager was appointed on a three-year deal in July.

Glasner booed by Forest fans

McCoist reacted to the jeers during Wednesday's talkSPORT Breakfast show.

Asked by Alan Brazil if he is ok with the fans booing Glasner already, he replied: "The answer to that would be no. No, I’m not ok with him getting booed.

"Fans are entitled to voice their opinion. They pay their money, but the first thing you’ve got to say is, booing does not help anybody.

"It doesn’t help the players, it doesn’t help the management, doesn’t help the feeling within the stadium, the atmosphere, but I’ll stand by their right to do it.

"They’re well within their rights to do it if they pay their money, but after two games, new manager, no (it is not ok).

"I think it was only a very, very small element. It only happened once or twice.

3 McCoist believes it is 'not ok' for Forest fans to boo Glasner after two matches Credit: Getty

"So in answer to the question, I’ll fight for the right to do it, but I don’t think it does anybody any good."

Forest's cup exit follows a 1-0 defeat to Leeds in the Premier League on Saturday.

They travel to Anfield to face Liverpool this weekend before hosting Tottenham Hotspur on September 5.

Matches against Aston Villa and Coventry City follow ahead of the first international break of the season.

Glasner became the club's fifth permanent manager in 10 months when he was named as Vitor Pereira's successor earlier this summer.

His arrival came after the Austrian left Palace following almost two-and-a-half years in charge at Selhurst Park.

3 Forest have lost their first two matches under Glasner after their Carabao Cup exit Credit: PA

During that time, he won the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League.

Those trophies represent the only major honours in the club's 120-year history.

As for his new club, Forest's last piece of significant silverware came in 1990 when they lifted the League Cup for a fourth time.

Last season saw the club finish 16th in the Premier League as well as reaching the semi-finals of the Europa League.

Sports.title: Why Liverpool cannot play European powerhouse in Champions League due to new UEFA rule
Sports.content:
Why Liverpool cannot play European powerhouse in Champions League due to new UEFA rule

Liverpool can still be drawn away at the Bernabeu but will not be able to host Real Madrid at Anfield in the Champions League due to new UEFA rules.

The European giants have visited Merseyside during the continental competition for the past two campaigns running.

3 Liverpool have used Anfield as a fortress against Real Madrid in previous campaigns Credit: Getty

The Reds have been successful both times, with Alexis Mac Allister and Cody Gakpo sealing a 2-0 victory in the 2024-25 season and the Argentine scoring the only goal of the meeting in the following encounter.

However, UEFA has introduced a regulation preventing the exact same fixture from being repeated at the same venue for three consecutive campaigns.

Despite this restriction, Los Blancos could still play Andoni Iraola's men in the league phase in Madrid.

The rules state: "Uefa administration may determine alternative conditions for the draw in accordance with the principles set by the Club Competitions Committee,

"And may adapt any of the conditions of the draw to avoid deadlock situations and/or take into account any relevant constraints in light of decisions taken by the UEFA Executive Committee.

"This means that if any teams that already played against each other in the league phase of the Uefa Champions League in the 2024/25 season are again drawn against each other, with the same home team, in the league phase of the Uefa Champions League in this 2025/26 season,

"Those teams will not be able to be drawn against each other with the same home team in the 2026/27 season."

Liverpool last visited the Bernabeu in March 2023, when a place in the quarter-finals was up for grabs.

Karim Benzema netted the only goal in a 1-0 win for the Spanish giants.

Arsenal face similar restrictions

Arsenal will also not be drawn away to Inter Milan in the league phase of the competition tomorrow.

3 The fixture is still allowed to play at the Emirates Credit: Getty

The Gunners travelled to the San Siro to face the Serie A champions in both 2024/25 and 2025/26.

Mikel Arteta's side secured a impressive 3-1 victory in Milan last term thanks to strikes from Gabriel Jesus and Viktor Gyökeres, whereas the Italian outfit won 1-0 on home turf the previous year.

The draw for this season’s Champions League league phase will be made on Thursday, August 27 at a ceremony in Monaco.

The 2026/27 UEFA Champions League league phase draw starts at 5pm BST.

The draw will arrange 36 teams to play eight match, as they face two teams from pots one, two, three and four.

Half of the matches will be at home, the other half away.

Sports.title: Emi Martinez keen to join Chelsea as Blues consider deal days after poor Robert Sanchez display
Sports.content:
Emi Martinez keen to join Chelsea as Blues consider deal days after poor Robert Sanchez display

Chelsea are in talks with Aston Villa over Emiliano Martinez, talkSPORT understands.

The Argentina goalkeeper, 33, is available for as little as £8.6million and has made it clear he wants the move.



2 Martinez has spent six years at Aston Villa Credit: Getty

Martinez was offered to Chelsea by intermediaries following the arrival of Zion Suzuki as the new No.1 at Villa Park.

The Blues had insisted earlier in the summer they were content with their current keepers, but Martinez has presented a late-window opportunity.

It comes just two days after the 3-2 victory at Fulham, which saw Chelsea's first-choice goalkeeper Robert Sanchez widely criticised for both goals conceded.



Which other clubs have been linked with a move for Emi Martinez?

Martinez was the subject of heavy interest from Juventus earlier this summer, but a deal collapsed and the Italian club opted for Guglielmo Vicario instead.

Villa had quoted Juventus €10million (£8.6m) for the Argentinian gloveman.



Martinez's mooted exit comes after Villa boss Unai Emery confirmed the 33-year-old had expressed his desire to leave the club this summer.

What has Unai Emery said about Emi Martinez's future?

“Martinez transmitted to us the possibility to have another challenge in his career, not just now and even last year, and he was thinking in case he had a possibility to change his challenges, but he stayed and performed fantastic," Emery said.



"This year, again, he transmitted to us for a new challenge, and we signed Suzuki to replace him."

Martinez agitated for a move to Manchester United last summer but it never eventuated, as the Red Devils opted to sign Senne Lammens instead.

Despite missing out on a move to Old Trafford, Martinez knuckled down and helped Villa enjoy a historic season.

2 Martinez is arguably Villa's best goalkeeper in the modern era Credit: Getty



Emery's side finished fourth in the Premier League last term, ensuring a return to the Champions League.

Villa also ended their 30-year wait for a trophy by defeating Freiburg 3-0 to win the Europa League.

Emi Martinez's Aston Villa career at a glance

The Europa League final was Martinez's 256th competitive appearance for Villa in all competitions, having joined from Arsenal in 2020.

Martinez's move to Birmingham proved transformative for his career, having gone on to win the World Cup with Argentina as their first choice goalkeeper.



The 33-year-old has also kept the second-most Premier League clean sheets for Villa (60), with only Mark Bosnich boasting more (64).

Martinez's exploits for club and country have helped him win the Yashin Trophy twice, an award given out during the Ballon d'Or ceremony to the best performing goalkeeper in the world.

Martinez was the first goalkeeper to have claimed the award multiple times.

Sports.title: Liverpool open surprise talks for new Premier League winger after Yankuba Minteh negotiations break down
Sports.content:
Liverpool open surprise talks for new Premier League winger after Yankuba Minteh negotiations break down

Crystal Palace have rejected Liverpool's approach for Ismaila Sarr, talkSPORT understands.

The Reds had sounded out Palace over a move for the 28-year-old, albeit without lodging an official bid.

2 Sarr could join a Premier League giant Credit: Getty

However, it is understood the Eagles indicated they were not willing to entertain a sale.

Liverpool's approach for Sarr comes after Brighton set a £80m asking price for winger Yankuba Minteh.

The Seagulls had already knocked back two bids from Liverpool for Minteh, with the latest being £60m.

Liverpool are not expected to return for a third bid unless Brighton's valuation drops.

Sarr has already been the subject of interest from elsewhere this summer, with Palace rejecting a bid from Turkish giants Galatasaray.

The 28-year-old did not feature in the Eagles' season opener, which ended in defeat away to Everton.

What has Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage said about Ismaila Sarr's future?

Prior to the contest, Palace boss Pierre Sage said Sarr would be available for the contest.

However, Sage later revealed Sarr had been ruled out due to a groin issue and reiterated he hoped to keep the winger at the club.

"We don't want him to leave, he is under contract with us for three years and he will be with us on Monday," Sage said.

"That's the most important information for me and you."

2 Sarr has given Premier League full-backs plenty of nightmares since he joined Palace Credit: Getty

Sarr has spent the last two seasons with Palace having joined in the summer of 2024 from Marseille.

The 28-year-old has gone on to score 33 goals and contribute 10 assists for the Eagles across 92 appearances across all competitions.

In that period, Sarr has helped the club win the FA Cup and the Conference League.

What is the latest on Liverpool's pursuit of a winger?

Liverpool's interest in Sarr comes as they remain active in the market for wide attackers.

The Reds are looking to recruit in the final third following Mohamed Salah's exit.

Paris Saint Germain's Bradley Barcola is Liverpool's top target, but the English club are yet to find a breakthrough in negotiations.

The European champions initially set the price for Barcola at £145m, but it has since dropped to £125m.

Sports.title: Police launch search for ex-Premier League star after he was reported missing
Sports.content:
Police launch search for ex-Premier League star after he was reported missing

Hungarian police have launched a search to find Akos Buzsaky after he was reported missing.

Local authorities have been searching for Buzsaky since August 18.

2 Buzsaky spent nearly a decade in English football Credit: Getty



Buzsaky's father, Akos Buzsaky Sr, was not even aware his son had been missing when contacted by Hungarian publication Blikk.

What has Akos Buzsaky's father said about the search?

"I didn’t know that the police were also looking for my son," Buzsaky Sr said.

“He basically spends a lot of time in Greece, where he works as a construction contractor.

“He spent almost the entire last year there.

“Since we don’t live under the same roof, it’s not surprising that we only speak less often.



“The last time I spoke to him was last week, when he was at home.”

QPR and Plymouth Argyle share messages of support for Akos Buzsaky

Buzsaky is remembered by English football supporters for his stints with Queens Park Rangers and Plymouth Argyle, with both clubs sharing messages on social media hoping for the midfielder is found safe.

"We are concerned to hear that Akos Buzsaky has been reported missing," Plymouth wrote.



"Everybody at Plymouth Argyle is hoping that Akos is found safe soon."

QPR said: "The club are concerned to learn that R's favourite Akos Buzsaky has been reported missing. We're all praying he's found safe and well."



2 The 44-year-old registered 37 goal contributions for the Hoops Credit: Getty

Akos Buzsaky's career at a glance

The 44-year-old began his career at MTK in Hungary before moving to Porto in 2002.

A loan spell at Portuguese side Academica followed, with Buzsaky then joining Plymouth on loan in 2004 after impressing in a behind-closed-doors friendly.

The Pilgrims turned Buzsaky's loan into a permanent deal after just one season.



He went to on make over 100 appearances for Plymouth before joining QPR on loan in October 2007.

The Hungarian then became a permanent member of QPR months later in January.

Buzsaky wasted little time in becoming a cult hero among the Hoops faithful, scoring 10 goals and providing six assists in his first season.

He later helped the club achieve promotion to the Premier League in 2011, going on to represent the Hoops 18 times in the top flight.



It proved to be Buzsaky's only Premier League campaign as he departed QPR at the end of this contract in July 2012.

Following his exit from the Hoops, Buzsaky moved to Portsmouth before returning to Hungary in September 2013 to join Ferencvaros.

Sports.title: Why Julian Alvarez is missing from Atletico Madrid training amid Arsenal transfer rumours
Sports.content:
Why Julian Alvarez is missing from Atletico Madrid training amid Arsenal transfer rumours

Julian Alvarez was absent from Atletico Madrid training on Wednesday as speculation grows surrounding his future.

The forward has expressed his desire to leave the Spanish giants this summer despite having four years remaining on his contract.

3 Alvarez missed Atletico training on Wednesday amid transfer interest from Arsenal Credit: Getty

Alvarez is desperate to secure a switch to Barcelona, whilst Real Madrid have also had a bid rejected this summer.

Although a move to Barca now appears unlikely, Arsenal could still complete the signing of the 26-year-old.

The Gunners are exploring a deal for Alvarez as revealed by talkSPORT at the weekend.

European football journalist Andy Brassell previously told talkSPORT Arsenal have a clear run at the signing with Barca out of the race.

It would take a bid matching Atletico's £150million asking price to make it happen, though.

However, Arsenal's interest is not the reason for his failure to train with his team-mates on Wednesday.

Why is Alvarez missing Atletico training?

According to Marca, Alvarez was absent from Atletico's latest training session due to illness.

Diego Simeone's players returned to training for the first time since their draw with Villarreal on Sunday.

It comes ahead of a trip to face Sevilla in LaLiga this coming weekend.

Alvarez had made a 24-minute cameo off the bench as his side were held at home.

3 Alvarez's absence from training has been put down to illness by reports in Spain Credit: Getty

The Argentina international had been left out of the squad for the season opener against Malaga.

Although Simeone later revealed the club have no plans to sell his future remains uncertain.

Alvarez's introduction against Villarreal was met with boos and jeers from the home supporters.

Atletico fans then sent him down the tunnel at full-time as they made their feelings known over his desire to leave the club.

His change of heart comes just two years on from signing a six-year deal in 2024.

Alvarez was signed from Manchester City for £81m, the second-most expensive signing in the club's history.

3 Alvarez has expressed his desire to leave Atletico for a 'dream' move to Barca Credit: Getty

He has since scored 49 goals in 107 appearances across all competitions for Atletico.

However, a move to Arsenal could still go through before Tuesday's 11pm transfer deadline for Premier League clubs.

Sports.title: Chelsea offered Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa - who Juventus bid just £6m for - to fix their goalkeeper problem after Robert Sanchez shocker
Sports.content:
Emiliano Martinez has been offered to Chelsea as Aston Villa seek a new club for their want-away goalkeeper.

After his move to Juventus collapsed earlier this month despite an initial £6million offer, Martinez is now one of three senior keepers in the Villa squad following the arrival of Zion Suzuki at Villa Park.

Martinez is also Villa's top earner following the departure of Youri Tielemans to Manchester United in July, and Unai Emery intends to press ahead with Suzuki and Marco Bizot.

Earlier in the summer, Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso indicated he was happy with keepers Robert Sanchez and Mike Penders.

But Sanchez's shaky display in Chelsea's 3-2 win at Fulham raised more question marks about the Spaniard.

Aston Villa have replaced Emiliano Martinez with Zion Suzuki and he is available for transfer

Asked about Sanchez on Wednesday, Alonso said: 'Normal conversations. We have talked more about the team thing, about what we did well and what we have to do better. It was more about understanding the context.

'Every game is going to be important because we are in this process that we still need to develop things, we need to make adjustments that are more team-related.'

Chelsea have brought 21-year-old Belgian Mike Penders into their squad after a successful loan at Strasbourg last season.

Alonso today suggested he is likely to start Thursday's Carabao Cup game against Luton Town. 'He's in the squad and will have an opportunity,' he said.

The Blues rate the former Genk youth shot-stopper, who has been likened to former Chelsea man Thibaut Courtois, very highly.

A move for Martinez, at 33 years old, would not be viewed as blocking Penders' progress.

The Argentina goalkeeper has been training with Villa since returning from the World Cup and his club say he is not injured.

Robert Sanchez's position as Chelsea No 1 is under threat after his recent errors

Emery confirmed he has once again asked to leave.

'We have signed Suzuki not for the future, but for now,' the Villa boss said. 'He has shown his capacity and that he can play at our level.

'Martinez transmitted to us the possibility to have another challenge in his career, not just now and even last year, and he was thinking in case he had a possibility to change his challenges, but he stayed and performed fantastic.

'This year, again, he transmitted to us for a new challenge, and we signed Suzuki to replace him. But the scenario we have is that we have two great goalkeepers.

'(Marco) Bizot as well, when we needed him, he responded fantastically. My ideal scenario with the goalkeeper is really fantastic, but maybe we can still change something.'

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Schlotterbeck to be made a Saint

Southampton have agreed a £3.8million deal with Augsburg for defender Keven Schlotterbeck. The 29-year old centre-back is undergoing a medical this afternoon.

Keven Schlotterbeck is set for sign for Southampton

Louza's a winner for Panathinaikos

Panathinaikos have agreed a deal to sign Watford midfielder Imran Louza. The fee for the 27-year-old Morocco international is worth £6.8m. Louza has travelled to Athens ahead of joining the Greek club.

Derby set to welcome Meister

Derby County are closing on Pisa striker Henrik Meister. The initial deal is a loan with an option to buy for £7.2m but the overall cost will be £8.5m if Meister joins Derby permanently.

Kabore completes Wrexham medical

Manchester City right-back Issa Kabore has completed a medical ahead of his £2m move to Wrexham. The Burkina Faso international has agreed a three-year deal.

Wrexham are also adding Angers left-back Jacques Ekomie who has completed a medical ahead of his £8m move.

Martinez offered to Chelsea

Emiliano Martinez has been offered to Chelsea as Aston Villa seek a new club for their wantaway goalkeeper.

After his move to Juventus collapsed earlier this month, Martinez is now one of three senior keepers in the squad following the arrival of Zion Suzuki at Villa Park.

For more on this story click HERE

Emiliano Martinez reached the World Cup final with Argentina in the summer

Liverpool check on Palace's Sarr

Liverpool have checked on a deal for Crystal Palace forward Ismaila Sarr, though any move looks unlikely as it stands.

The Anfield club have been assessing different opportunities in the market as they look to add two attacking players before Tuesday. They have not made an offer for Sarr as it stands.

For more on this story click HERE

Sunderland in for Brazilian winger Igor

Sunderland are in talks with Marseille for Brazilian winger Igor Paixao.

Leeds have previously checked on 26-year-old Paixao. Sunderland are understood to have made an offer earlier this week and talks are continuing. Marseille need to raise funds and Sunderland's priority is to add a winger.

They have also been in talks with Sporting Lisbon over Mozambique winger Geny Catamo.

Bees agree Malick Diouf deal

Brentford have agreed a deal with West Ham for left wing back El Hadji Malick Diouf worth £35m plus add-ons.

Daily Mail Sport reported Brentford's interest last month and the clubs have now come to an agreement.

The Senegal international joined last summer from Slavia Prague for £19m but had an indifferent season.

Brentford have agreed a deal for El Hadji Malick Diouf of West Ham

Disasi in at Palace

Crystal Palace have announced the arrival of Axel Disasi on a straight loan from Chelsea.

The 28-year-old centre-back replaces Maxence Lacroix, who went the other way in a £52million move earlier in the window.

Disasi provides experience in the centre of Palace’s back three, with the Frenchman expected to play in the middle of Chris Richards and Jaydee Canvot.

Palace remain in the market for another centre-back following Chadi Riad’s injury during last weekend’s 2-0 defeat to Everton.

BOBBY MANZI

Brighton's £3.5m Orozco deal

Brighton are working on a £3.5million deal to sign 18-year-old midfielder Matias Orozco from Colombian side Deportivo Cali.

Orozco, a defensive midfielder, has been watched by Liverpool and Manchester United among others.

He is due in the UK to complete formalities of the transfer and is expected be sent out on loan initially.

Man City complete ins and outs as they wait to go back in for Enzo

Manchester City's Omar Marmoush will sign a contract at Tottenham tomorrow after having his medical today, while Nico Gonzalez is finalising his move to Newcastle with the second part of his medical.

City are signing Palmeiras winger Allan Elias - who will fly in from Brazil to complete his move tomorrow - while a City bid is expected to go in for Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez.

City have confirmed the £85.6m signing of 18-year-old Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille. The Morocco midfielder said: 'Manchester City are, for me, the best club in the world.

'It’s a dream to be here and be able to call myself a City player. I have spent most of my life working hard to become the best player I can be and reach the top of the game.

'I’ve watched City for many years, and I love their style of play. City always try and play quality football and they have shown they are winners – this club feels like it’s built to win. The squad is world class and Enzo (Maresca) is a top manager.'

Ayyoub Bouaddi has joined Manchester City in a £85.6m deal from Lille

Aston Villa expect Saudis to meet £50m Watkins asking price

Aston Villa expect Al Hilal to hit their valuation of £50million for Ollie Watkins if they complete a deal for the England forward.

Watkins is keen to move to the Saudi Pro League club, who are offering a salary far higher than his current wages at Villa.

Villa have so far stuck to their position on Watkins and there is growing optimism Al Hilal, who have already had four bids turned down, will eventually meet the asking price.

Villa are also pursuing the £65million signing of Nicolas Jackson from Chelsea, who would effectively replace Watkins.

TOM COLLOMOSSE

Monaco join queue for Spurs star Matar Sarr

Monaco have joined the list of clubs showing interest in signing Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr.

Monaco are looking at the market for new midfielders in case they lose Lamine Camara who has attracted offers from Crystal Palace and interest from Chelsea.

All options open for Grealish as clock ticks down

Manchester City are leaving all options open to Jack Grealish as the window draws to a close.

The 30-year-old has returned to City's first-team fold, appearing as substitute in their first two games.

He was on loan at Everton last season and their chief executive Angus Kinnear says they have remained in contact.

City have not ruled out a permanent sale. Nor have they ruled out another loan or an option to stay, though that could be with potentially limited game time.

Coach Enzo Maresca has not ruled out a move either, saying after Sunday's win over Bournemouth: 'He is here and it is my duty to coach Jack and to try to get the best. 'Then it is one more week to go and we will see what happens. Not only with Jack but also other players.'

Jack Grealish is now back at Manchester City but all options are open as the window closes

Liverpool look elsewhere with Minteh fee too high

Liverpool are exploring alternative wing options with Brighton's valuation of Yankuba Minteh considered too high.

As Daily Mail Sport reported at the weekend, Brighton have been looking for a figure closer to £80million for the 22-year-old Gambian who is out until October with injury.

Liverpool had initially hoped to strike a deal around £50m.

Meanwhile, Celta Vigo are understood to be interested in midfielder Stefan Bajcetic but Liverpool have yet to receive a formal approach.

The 21-year-old started out at Vigo.

Yankuba Minteh is valued at around £80million by Brighton

Forest in talks over Celta defender

Nottingham Forest have opened talks with Celta Vigo for right-back Javi Rueda.

Forest are discussing an £8m offer for the 25-year-old who joined Celta from Real Madrid in 2024.

Tottenham have asked about Forest full-back Neco Williams but he is expected to stay at the City Ground.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport, Forest are also in talks over a £13.6m move including add ons for Corinthians midfielder Andre.

The 20-year-old only made his league debut a year ago but Corinthians are holding out for more.

Javi Rueda (left) in action in Celta Vigo's La Liga opener against Valencia at the weekend

Palacios set for £23.5m Ipswich deal

Ipswich are finalising a £23.5m deal for Bayer Leverkusen midfielder Exequiel Palacios. The 27-year-old has agreed a four-year contract. As Daily Mail Sport reported yesterday, Ipswich want £9m for midfielder Anis Mehmeti, who has offers from Wrexham, Birmingham and Derby.

Ezequiel Palacios is set to became the latest signing in a busy summer at Portman Road

Osmajic leaves Preston

Preston striker Milutin Osmajic has signed for Genoa.

Deepdale boss Paul Heckingbottom confirmed the move was on the cards at the weekend and added to BBC Radio Lancashire: 'The business we've done so far has been really good in terms of players we've brought in to replace, players who have gone out, but we've lost a lot of players. We've still got a lot to replace and now Milly is another one we've got to replace.'

Milutin Osmajic is heading to Genoa after three years at Preston North End

Sports.title: Fears as police launch search for ex-Premier League star who has been missing in Hungary for over a week
Sports.content:
Police in Hungary have launched a search for former Premier League star Akos Buzsaky, who has been missing for more than a week.

The 44-year-old, who played for QPR in the English top flight, has been missing from Budapest since August 18.

The midfielder earned 20 caps for Hungary as a midfielder and also played for Plymouth, Portsmouth and Barnsley before retiring in 2025. He made 18 Premier League appearances, contributing two goals and two assists.

The police have not said why they are looking for Buzsaky and his father, Akos Buzsaky Sr told Hungarian outlet Blikk: ‘I didn’t know that the police were also looking for my son.

Akos Buszaky played for QPR between 2007 and 2012, with one season in the top flight

Sports.title: Champions League draw's BANNED matches: Why Liverpool vs Real Madrid and Inter Milan vs Arsenal will be outlawed in first year of new UEFA rules
Sports.content:
Champions League draw's BANNED matches: Why Liverpool vs Real Madrid and Inter Milan vs Arsenal will be outlawed in first year of new UEFA rules

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Liverpool vs Real Madrid and Inter Milan vs Arsenal will not be allowed in this season's Champions League league phase due a little-known new rule introduced by UEFA.

The draw for the competition takes place tomorrow, with each team to face two sides from Pot 1, Pot 2, Pot 3 and Pot 4.

Liverpool, Real, Inter and Arsenal are all in Pot 1, and therefore in principle the Reds could be drawn against the Spanish giants at Anfield, and Inter could host the Gunners at the San Siro.

However, UEFA rules prevent this from happening because of recent history.

Liverpool have faced Real at home in the past two seasons, while Inter have also entertained Arsenal twice in the league phase over the same timeframe.

And, the European governing body have now brought in a ruling that is based around stopping the same fixture happening three years in a row.

Liverpool won't be able to draw Real Madrid at home in this season's Champions League league phase after UEFA introduced a new rule

The rule also applies to Inter Milan hosting Arsenal after the fixture took place in the last two years

A section of the Champions League regulations says: 'UEFA administration may determine alternative conditions for the draw in accordance with the principles set by the Club Competitions Committee and may adapt any of the conditions of the draw to avoid deadlock situations and/or take into account any relevant constraints in light of decisions taken by the UEFA Executive Committee.'

They added: 'The UEFA Club Competitions Committee has determined an additional condition that may be applicable to the UEFA Champions League draw for the 2026-27 season, deciding that any individual fixture between the same two teams may not be repeated in the same competition with the same home team for three consecutive seasons.

'This means that if any teams that already played against each other in the league phase of the UEFA Champions League in the 2024-25 season are again drawn against each other, with the same home team, in the league phase of the UEFA Champions League in this 2025-26 season, those teams will not be able to be drawn against each other with the same home team in the 2026-27 season.'

This does mean that the teams can be drawn against each other, but this would have to be with the match between Liverpool and Real at the Bernabeu, and at the Emirates for Inter vs Arsenal.

A fixture between Real and Liverpool would have plenty of spice due to their recent history, coupled with the fact that former Liverpool stars Trent Alexander-Arnold and Ibrahima Konate now play for the Spanish giants.

Both teams endured a disappointing time in Europe last season as they exited at the quarter-final stage.

Liverpool were beaten 4-0 on aggregate by eventual winners PSG, while Real lost 6-4 to Bayern Munich over two legs.

Meanwhile, Inter were shocked by Bodo/Glimt at the play-off stage, while Arsenal lost the final to PSG on penalties.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo is hauled off, mid-tantrum, at half-time by no-nonsense Ange Postecoglou - before team turn a 2-0 deficit into 3-2 win without him - in new challenge to his Saudi supremacy
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo's relationship with new Al Nassr boss Ange Postecoglou already appears to be under scrutiny just three matches into the season.

Al Nassr completed a remarkable comeback from two goals down to beat rivals Al Ettifaq 3-2 on Tuesday, but it was no thanks to Ronaldo, who earns an astronomical £488,000 a day, that the reigning champions claimed all three points.

The visitors appeared to be heading for defeat after enduring a disastrous first half which saw goalkeeper Bento sent off in the 12th minute for a challenge on former Fulham midfielder Mousa Dembele after rushing out of his box.

Al Ettifaq capitalised, with Ondrej Duda and Alvaro Medran finding the back of the net to take a two-goal lead into half-time.

Ronaldo, who was making his first start of the season following his return from the summer's World Cup, cut a frustrated figure as he headed towards the dressing room at the break.

The 41-year-old forward was seen angrily gesturing and removing his captain's armband as he walked down the tunnel.

Postecoglou then boldly opted to remove Ronaldo before the start of the second half in what turned out to be an inspired move.

Ronaldo couldn't help but hide his frustration after enduring a disastrous first half which saw the reigning champions trail by two goals and reduced to 10 men

He was seen angrily gesturing and removing his captain's armband as he walked down the tunnel at half-time

Postecoglou then boldly opted to remove Ronaldo before the start of the second half in what turned out to be an inspired move

Sadio Mane sparked the revival in the 74th minute before defender Abdulelah Al Amri levelled the match three minutes later. Mane then found the back of the net again in the 90th minute to complete the turnaround and seal victory.

Footage of the post-match celebrations showed no sign of Ronaldo celebrating the victory, while Postecoglou refused to indulge questions about his controversial call to drop the Portugal star after the match.

'I think there’s a bigger story today, and that is that ten men of Al Nassr were unbelievable. That's all you should write about today, everything else doesn't matter.

'It doesn't matter what team because if you see ten men in those conditions for so long, 2-0 down to come back, that's the only story today.'

Controversy appears to have followed Ronaldo since his move to the Middle East in January 2023, following his public fallout with Manchester United.

At the beginning of the year Ronaldo went on strike over what he felt was a lack of financial backing of his Al Nassr compared to their title rivals Al Hilal. Both clubs are majority owned by The Public Investment Fund, Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund.

Ronaldo was convinced that Al Hilal are getting preferential treatment, and he was particularly angry that they strengthened their squad by bringing in players such as his former Real Madrid teammate Karim Benzema during the January window.

Saudi officials, meanwhile, were surprised that Ronaldo was unhappy given he is earning nearly £500,000 a day.

Footage of the post-match celebrations showed no sign of Ronaldo celebrating the victory

Ange Postecoglou:



“I think there’s a bigger story today, and that’s that the ten Al Nassr players put in an incredible performance. That’s all you should be writing about today.”

pic.twitter.com/7jSMfBAtqp — Al Nassr Zone (@TheNassrZone) August 26, 2026

Although Ronaldo is the face of the Saudi Pro League (SPL), the league issued a statement firing back at the Portuguese star by reaffirming that he has no say on what happens at clubs outside of his own.

'The SPL is structured around a simple principle: every club operates independently under the same rules,' they said.

'Clubs have their own boards, their own executives and their own football leadership. Decisions on recruitment, spending and strategy sit with those clubs, within a financial framework designed to ensure sustainability and competitive balance. That framework applies equally across the league.

'Cristiano has been fully engaged with Al Nassr since his arrival and has played an important role in the club's growth and ambition. Like any elite competitor, he wants to win. But no individual - however significant - determines decisions beyond their own club.'

Ronaldo claimed his first league title with Al Nassr last season.

Sports.title: Newcastle Confidential: Why Matias Fernandez-Pardo deal is NOT dead, Joelinton injury REVEALED, what William Osula absence means for Yoane Wissa and the Yankuba Minteh sell-on clause
Sports.content:
Newcastle have NOT given up hope of signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo before Tuesday’s transfer deadline.

There were reports in France today of the Magpies walking away from a deal amid Lille’s £60m asking price. Newcastle Confidential understands that is not yet the case, although sporting director Ross Wilson will not sanction any deal that leads to future problems with Premier League and UEFA spending rules. Wilson and the hierarchy have solved those issues this summer and there is now a transfer framework within which they are operating.

Fernandez-Pardo is an ambitious target and the club’s interest was revealed in the final Confidential column of last season. It was thought then that the 21-year-old wanted Champions League football, but there has been encouragement in recent days of him being open to the move.

The £50million marquee signing of Nico Gonzalez from Manchester City has been a huge boost in terms of the optics around a club who have lost several stars this summer.

This comes on the back of confirmation of plans for a new £190million training ground development and the impressive showing in the season opener against Liverpool. There is a feeling inside St James' Park, and among the fanbase, of renewed positivity heading out of the summer.

Fernandez-Pardo, a Belgium international, is seen as a versatile forward who can play in any of the four attacking positions used by new boss Matthias Jaissle.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo is an ambitious target and Newcastle's interest was revealed in the final Confidential column of last season

Joelinton injury boost

Joelinton has a quad injury but the problem is not as serious as first feared, Confidential can reveal.

Mystery has surrounded the nature of the Brazilian’s issue since Jaissle told reporters 11 days ago that he would miss at least a ‘couple of weeks’ with an unspecified injury.

We now understand there were concerns that Joelinton could be set for a lengthy spell on the sidelines. He needed surgery on his thigh in 2024 and missed four months of the season. However, the 30-year-old does not require an operation this time and the news has been more positive in recent days. Indeed, once the symptoms subside, he will be free to return.

That exact date is still to be determined, but it is hoped that will be this side of the September international break.

Newcastle's Joelinton has a quad injury - but it is not as bad as first feared

Toon set for slice of Minteh fee

Newcastle DO have a sell-on clause in the deal that took Yankuba Minteh to Brighton two years ago.

Liverpool want to sign the 22-year-old and are willing to pay £65million to take him to Anfield. The Seagulls are holding out for closer to £80million and negotiations are ongoing.

Minteh joined Brighton for £30million from Newcastle in the summer of 2024 as the club scrambled to avoid a Premier League points deduction for breaching profit and sustainability rules. But we can reveal that, unlike the deal that took Elliot Anderson to Nottingham Forest on the same weekend, the package with Brighton does include a sell-on clause.

The value of this is thought to be around 10 per cent of the profit of any sale, meaning the Magpies could be set for a return of £4-5million should the winger move to Liverpool, a not-insignificant sum in a world of Squad Cost Ratio rules.

Yankuba Minteh could be heading for Liverpool from Brighton - which would land Newcastle a cut of the fee

No surgery for Burn

Dan Burn has damaged the deltoid ligaments in his ankle and is likely to be missing until mid-October, Confidential understands.

The good news is that the club captain does not need surgery and there is still an outside chance that he could return just before the September break. However, Burn will not be rushed and the expectation is that he will use that three-week period for international matches to build his fitness on Tyneside.

The protective boot he is wearing has given rise to fears of the problem being more serious, but that is standard practice for such an injury.

The deltoid ligament is a strong, triangle-shaped band of connective tissue on the inside of the ankle that stabilises the area and prevents outward rolling of the foot. Burn damaged his deltoid ligaments when his foot rolled in training last week.

Newcastle will not, as it stands, enter the market for a new centre-back. Sven Botman answered some of the concerns around him from pre-season with a strong display against Liverpool on Sunday.

Dan Burn in his protective boot on Sunday - but the good news is he won't require an operation

Osula blow a real pain

Finally, on injuries at least, William Osula has avoided a broken foot but will face a spell on the sidelines.

We understand the striker suffered the injury when he collided with Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson during the first half of Sunday’s 2-2 draw. Osula played on before succumbing to the pain 10 minutes after half-time.

While there is no significant damage, it looks like being an absence that is measured in weeks rather than days, with the pain needing to settle before a return date is set.

That is a blow given Osula was lively and helped set the tone against the Reds. It is likely that Yoane Wissa will revert to striker as opposed to Nick Woltemade, with Jacob Ramsey and Joe Willock vying for the No10 role at Tottenham on Saturday.

Woltemade’s future is uncertain and there could yet be movement in the final days of the window should an offer emerge, most likely from Germany.

Willock is wanted by Besiktas and Newcastle have a decision to make with the midfielder in the final year on his contract. Jaissle told us on Sunday that he wants to keep him.

William Osula was superb for Newcastle on Sunday and his injury is a real blow for Matthias Jaissle

Pope to stay

Nick Pope will be staying at Newcastle beyond the transfer window, as it stands.

We are told that the goalkeeping slots at viable suitors are all taken at this present time and, barring injury to those keepers or an unexpected approach over the weekend, the 34-year-old will remain at St James’ Park entering the final year of his contract.

Newcastle are still trying to find a solution given Pope has been told he would be third choice, but time is running out.

Toon kids shining

I went to watch the Under 21s on Monday night during their 3-1 defeat by Tottenham.

We should expect to see striker Sean Neave and defender Miodrag Pivas involved in tonight’s Carabao Cup tie against West Brom after they were taken off at half-time at Whitley Park, but Mason Miley played the full match.

Of those who caught the eye, Korean winger Park Seung-Soo was the pick, while scorer Vakhtang Salia clearly has ability.

I know those on the inside are excited about the 18-year-old Georgian, whose first year on Tyneside was disrupted by injury. He looks like a forward with scope for big improvement.

Sports.title: Liverpool check on Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr as they look to add two attacking players before deadline - with Yankuba Minteh pursuit stalling over Brighton's £80m asking price
Sports.content:
Liverpool have checked on a deal for Crystal Palace forward Ismaila Sarr, though any move looks unlikely as it stands.

Sports.title: Man United's kit clanger: Club's rule-breaking shirt falls foul of Premier League laws on first game of season
Sports.content:
Man United's kit clanger: Club's rule-breaking shirt falls foul of Premier League laws on first game of season

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United have fallen foul of Premier League kit rules after one game of the season.

The Old Trafford outfit went into the current campaign without a sleeve sponsor, following the expiration of a £20m per year deal with DXC Technology which dates back to 2022.

However, Premier League rules dictate that clubs without a sleeve sponsor should display the competition’s badge on both arms.

And eagle-eyed observers have pointed out that United did not comply during their opening day defeat at Hull City, with one sleeve left blank.

While both the Premier League and United declined to comment, Daily Mail Sport understands that the club was given a polite reminder of the rule.

Premier League rules dictate clubs without a sleeve sponsor should display the competition’s badge on both arms - but Manchester United did not

The Premier League badge was shown on the other arm of United's shirts

It is also understood that the top-flight badge will be on both sleeves when United return to action against Ipswich at Old Trafford on Sunday.

United are seeking a new shirt sleeve sponsor, having had one for the past eight seasons.

The rule-break came on a chaotic opening day for United and manager Michael Carrick, with the surprise defeat by Hull drawing plenty of criticism - including from captain Bruno Fernandes.

After the match, the United captain complained to the media that his side had made the 'same mistakes as we did last season (in away matches)'. The Portugal midfielder added: 'Every away game we give too much of the ball to them. In the first 20 minutes, the goalkeeper was the one with the most touches.

'We needed to press more, be more aggressive, and then again we need to work on set plays and not concede these types of goals. Against these types of teams, they are waiting for that moment.'

Club legend Paul Scholes, however, took issue with Fernandes' comments on his podcast The Good, The Bad & The Football.

'I'd be interested to know what he means by them. What mistakes were they giving away?' the 51-year-old former player said.

'Especially when you perform the way he did as well, I think it's probably best to keep your mouth shut. He didn't have his best performance either.'

Scholes and former United forward Dion Dublin went further, suggesting that Fernandes, alongside team-mate Luke Shaw, who also claimed after the match that United went into the fixture underprepared, had undermined manager Michael Carrick.

Bruno Fernandes - pictured without the Premier League logo - was left disappointed

Shaw had said after the match: 'It’s not us and we knew it was coming. I think as a whole, as a group, collectively, we could prepare better. Especially knowing how good they are at set plays and what their dangers are.'

Reacting to the left-back's comments, Scholes said: 'Luke Shaw always says something. And that's a slight on your staff. That's a slight on your manager. If one of your players is saying that you'd be like f***ing hell, you'd have them in on Monday morning.'

Dublin said: 'You want silence. If your skipper has to speak then he has to speak, but then you make sure he says the things that don't open a can of worms. You just don't give anyone any ammunition because the ammunition is there from your performance.'

Scholes added: 'Those comments are not so much about respect but you speak about fear of managers and the things they've said, they're a slight on the manager and staff. As a player if we did that about Sir Alex, "we weren't prepared", f***ing hell, you'd be right in and he'd probably single you out in front of the full team.'

Sports.title: Tyson Fury chooses replacement opponent for Anthony Joshua
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury chooses replacement opponent for Anthony Joshua

The 'Gypsy King' is prepared to move on should his all-British heavyweight showdown with Anthony Joshua fail to come to fruition

View Image Tyson Fury exchanges words with Anthony Joshua after his fight at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on April 11, 2026, in London, England. (Image: Getty)

‌



The heavyweight icons signed to fight each other just days after Fury's comeback win over Arslanbek Makhmudov back in April. Joshua and Fury then came through respective tune-up fights unscathed, as the latter forced Mariusz Wach to quit on his stool, while 'AJ' survived two knockdowns to stop Kristian Prenga in the second round last month.

‌



As of yet, an official date or venue is still yet to be decided. Joshua and Fury are currently contracted to fight in the UK later this year but broadcasters Netflix and the fight's Saudi backers want to move the fight to New York. Joshua and promoter Eddie Hearn have submitted their demands to shift the clash across the Atlantic but are yet to receive a response.

‌



Fury's brother Shane admits that the former world champion will be fighting at Madison Square Garden on November 20 with or without Joshua. Speaking to Boxing King Media, he said: “The more I’m watching it, the less I’m thinking that this fight’s gonna happen.

Sports.title: Moses Itauma responds to "deluded" claim from Filip Hrgovic
Sports.content:
Moses Itauma responds to "deluded" claim from Filip Hrgovic

Moses Itauma is not a fan of Filip Hrgovic's trash talk ahead of their mouthwatering heavyweight showdown for the IBF world title on Saturday night

View Image Moses Itauma ahead of his fight with Filip Hrgovic (Image: Queensberry)

Moses Itauma has brutally hit back at Filip Hrgovic's 'delusional' claim and admits that his upcoming rival is starting to get on his nerves.

‌



The 21-year-old is set for his first crack at a world title on Saturday night when he clashes with Hrgovic at the O2 Arena in London for the IBF heavyweight belt. A win could see the British sensation become the youngest heavyweight world champion since Mike Tyson - who achieved the incredible feat 40 years ago.

‌



As the fight edges closer, the pair are starting to go at each other's throats - which only makes for a rather explosive encounter. On Tuesday afternoon, Hrgovic branded his adversary as 'deluded.' And just hours later, it was the Brit's turn to bite back and have his say on the matter.

‌



“I tell myself there’s nothing that this Hrgovic guy can do to get in my head but he’s starting to wind me up,” Itauma told reporters during a media roundtable on Tuesday evening. “In an interview earlier, apparently he said I wake up and I just hug trees. He’s really starting to annoy me.

‌



Mike Tyson admits he could be banned from Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury READ MORE :

Moses Itauma on dark side of fame as heavyweight eyes world title READ MORE :

“In my mind if somebody’s trying to get one up on you, or trying to get in your head, it’s because they’re not confident in themselves. Obviously Hrgovic is a talker. Before fights, he’s always said certain things – like he did to [Daniel] Dubois when he said he sees big muscles but not big balls. Then you see Dubois, in his mind, is raging. So Hrgovic has always been a talker. It’s just because English ain’t his first language that people don’t pay attention.”

It comes after the Croatian boxing veteran had earlier stated that a win for Itauma could ultimately 'ruin' his soul. "I just think he's a kid. He's unexperienced. He's just a young man. I think for him, it would be the best to lose this fight because it's going to ruin him, winning the world title. He's already in the clouds, above the ground. He's already delusional. And I think it can ruin someone who's not ready for that kind of fame, that kind of money.

"It can ruin your soul, it can make you lose yourself and we've seen a lot of superstars and famous people who have lost themselves. They just lost in that crazy world of fame and money. I think he's not ready for that. I think for him, it would be the best to lose this fight, to be honest with you, to save his soul."

Article continues below

But Itauma believes there may be a method to his rival's madness, revealing: “Although it’s been annoying me, I hear that because I already know the level of success I’ve achieved and how I’m coping. I’ve always said I never wanted to be at Anthony Joshua or Tyson Fury level because I know how annoyed I get trying to be a normal person. Now I can’t imagine being at a level of Tyson Fury or Anthony Joshua. But, at the same time, if I’m going down this path, I don’t have a choice.”

That said, the 21-year-old star does not buy into Hrgovic's remark that a win would be bad for the youngster's soul. “I wouldn’t say he has a point but if I win this fight it might not be good for my soul. I can hear that. But that’s not the reason why I’m just gonna go in there and not win – for the sake of my soul. That’s not a good idea," he admitted.

Sports.title: 5 Premier League teams with the best fixtures for FPL Gameweek 2 as Newcastle lead the way
Sports.content:
5 Premier League teams with the best fixtures for FPL Gameweek 2 as Newcastle lead the way

The Premier League season is officially underway and several teams made massive statements in their opening fixtures

View 6 Images Newcastle United face an easier test in their second game of the season (Image: Getty)

The Premier League is back and the opening weekend threw up some surprises, with Manchester United losing on the road to Hull City and Leeds United picking up all three points at Nottingham Forest. So, which sides have the best fixtures over the next four gameweeks and which fantasy assets should we be stocking our squads with?

‌



If you've got off to a bad start, it's not too late! Get your FPL team rated for free by AI in seconds on Fantasy Football Hub and find out your recommended transfers.

‌



5th Place: Manchester City

Manchester City battled back against Bournemouth to secure three points in their opening home game under Enzo Maresca. A trip to Old Trafford in Gameweek 4 is their only tricky upcoming fixture, with Crystal Palace, promoted Coventry City and Sunderland also in their immediate schedule.

‌



View 6 Images Erling Haaland is the most expensive player in Fantasy Football (Image: Fantasy Football Hub)

Erling Haaland (£15.5m) is predicted to be the top-performing player in FPL across the next four gameweeks, according to Fantasy Football Hub's AI points predictions . He's the most owned player in the game, in 68.3% of teams, and the top captain pick for both Gameweek 3 and Gameweek 5.

Arsenal set to announce striker transfer as target sends farewell message READ MORE :

James Maddison suffers fractured shoulder in Tottenham defeat in fresh injury blow READ MORE :

Defenders Marc Guehi (£6.0m) and Josko Gvardiol (£5.5m) were their top performers against the Cherries, with a goal apiece. Nico O'Reilly (£6.5m) is a tempting alternative, though, having started that game out of position in the number 10 role, although his 63rd-minute substitution may deter investment.

‌



4th Place: Liverpool

Liverpool battled back twice against Newcastle to earn themselves a valuable point at St. James' Park, with Cody Gakpo (£7.0m) their star man. He was top among all players in Gameweek 1 for shots, with 6, getting his goal and also netting the two-point defensive contribution bonus.

It's Dominik Szoboszlai (£7.0m) who is capturing the attention of fantasy managers, though, with 150,000 transfers in taking his ownership above 40%. He scored the emphatic winner from the penalty spot, putting him above Alexander Isak (£9.0m) in the pecking order. He also took six corners and five free kicks, showing his dominance across set pieces.

View 6 Images Dominik Szoboszlai was all-action in Liverpool's 2-2 draw against Newcastle (Image: Fantasy Football Hub)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Liverpool now entertain Nottingham Forest, who are yet to score this season, which could spell clean sheet potential for Virgil Van Dijk (£6.5m). It's then a trip to promoted Ipswich Town, before facing Fulham and Bournemouth ahead of the international break.

3rd Place: Leeds United

Leeds United have begun the campaign in great form, beating Oliver Glasner's Nottingham Forest side 1-0 on the road on the opening weekend. They then backed that result up with a 2-0 win at the City Ground in midweek, the only all-Premier League clash in the League Cup second Round.

‌



View 6 Images Anton Stach and Harry Wilson could prove to be solid options (Image: Fantasy Football Hub)

They have three home games in their next four against Brentford, Newcastle and Glasner's former club, Crystal Palace. Harry Wilson (£6.5m) is taking a share of set-pieces along with Anton Stach (£6.0m), who got himself on the scoresheet and netted defensive contribution points. His routes to points give him the edge over striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin (£6.0m).

There are plenty of good defensive options in this Leeds United side, with their backline strengthened in the summer transfer window with the arrival of goalkeeper James Trafford and centre-back Tarik Muharemovic (£5.0m). It's Jaka Bijol (£5.0m) who looks to be the most intriguing pick, though, hitting the two-point defensive contribution bonus last time out.

‌



2nd Place: Spurs

Spurs didn't have the start to the campaign they desired, losing 3-0 on the road to Brentford. However, it's expected that their form will improve in the coming gameweeks, with three home games in their next four against Newcastle United, Everton and Aston Villa. It's an important run for Roberto De Zerbi's side heading into the international break.

New signing Marcos Senesi (£6.0m) demonstrated he could be as dominant on defensive contribution points in this Spurs side as he was last campaign for Bournemouth, with a tally of 16, ranking him third of all defenders in Gameweek 1. However, the Manchester City defenders are more appealing premiums, while team-mate Van Hecke (£5.0m) is cheaper.

View 6 Images Spurs host Newcastle in their next game (Image: Fantasy Football Hub)

‌



Spurs look to be strengthening their attack, with Savinho (£6.5m) among the new signings in the transfer window, which remains open until Tuesday, September 1. I think it's still a wait-and-see on their attackers, though, given they've yet to find the back of the net in this campaign.

1st Place: Newcastle United

Newcastle United top the Fantasy Football Hub's fixture analyser as the side with the best fixtures for the next four gameweeks of the season. It's Spurs up next, before taking on Bournemouth, Leeds United and Hull City. Many wrote them off for the start of this campaign, with their performance against Liverpool last weekend eye-opening.

View 6 Images Newcastle are still looking for their first win of the season (Image: Fantasy Football Hub)

Article continues below

Yoanne Wissa (£6.0m) managed just 517 minutes last season but made an immediate impact in this game, with an assist for the Magpies second goal. He looked to cause significant problems on the counter-attack, and had two big chances on goal. He could threaten Calvert-Lewin to dominate the cheap striker category.

There's plenty of options to consider from Newcastle United's defence, who are all capable of netting defensive contribution points. Malick Thiaw (£5.0m), Lewis Hall (£5.0m), and Sven Botman (£5.0m) all gained the two-point bonus against Liverpool. They are all differentials too, with Botman the pick of the bunch right now, sitting in just 0.2% of teams.

Sports.title: Alan Shearer makes Julian Alvarez transfer prediction as Arsenal target nowhere to be seen
Sports.content:
Alan Shearer makes Julian Alvarez transfer prediction as Arsenal target nowhere to be seen

Julian Alvarez remains the trending transfer topic at Arsenal with a new prediction made on the Atletico Madrid striker ahead of the summer window deadline

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez could join Arsenal from Atletico Madrid before the transfer window closes (Image: (Photo by Cesar Cebolla / Pressinphoto / Icon Sport))

Arsenal have been told by Alan Shearer they may have a transfer opportunity for Julian Alvarez after the Atletico Madrid star missed training on Wednesday. The Argentine returned to action following the World Cup last weekend and was booed by supporters as he actively seeks an exit.

‌



A move to Barcelona is Alvarez's dream but joining the Gunners is far more realistic given the stance of Atletico on selling to their domestic rivals. The summer window closes in less than a week with time running out for Alvarez to seal a move.

‌



He was due to take part in Atletico training on Wednesday but was not seen with his teammates due to illness, as per Spanish outlet Marca. The latest update on Alvarez has come from Shearer with the Premier League's record goal-scorer offering his thoughts on Arsenal's chances of signing him.

‌



"We've heard of a lot of pushing from Barcelona and the reluctance from Atletico," Shearer said on The Rest is Football podcast. "It seems like their thinking might be, 'if we have to sell, we're not selling to you [Barcelona]'.

"There's just maybe a small opportunity or a small window there for Arsenal to nab him, you would think. And if they do it's done by the way [the Premier League title race ]."

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Co-host Micah Richards also gave his verdict on the former Manchester City man, backing Alvarez to be prioritised above potential signings in other areas of the pitch.

He said: "I would actually go for a striker if I was Arsenal and we've all seen the situation with Alvarez at Atletico. He was booed by his own fans the other night and there are reports he wants to go to Barcelona. But are Atletico going to sell him to Barca?".

‌



View 2 Images Alan Shearer has made a Julian Alvarez to Arsenal transfer prediction (Image: Rest is Football podcast)

"It might be one for Arsenal to just sneak in there and offer a bid. He's clearly not happy... If Arsenal had Alvarez he would take them to the next level."

The asking price poses a significant obstacle, however, with Atletico demanding upwards of £100million. The Athletic reports they would entertain offers of €150m, equivalent to approximately £128m.

The 26-year-old returned to the pitch this past weekend in a 2-2 draw against Villarreal and was subjected to fierce jeering from his own fans before being ushered away by club officials while his teammates acknowledged the home crowd.
