As for the global flow of imports, the expected average, according to analysts at BCR/Rosgan, is 10 million tons, which would imply an increase of 2.7% compared to last year.

China, which reduced the pace of international beef purchases in 2021 to 950,000 tons compared to more than 1.1 million tons in 2020 will once again represent 32% of global consumption. According to BCR/Rosgan, China accounted for 13% of global meat demand in 2017.

At that time, Argentina was in the top five beef exporters, having previously been in the top three. But Argentina has dropped out of the top ten beef exporters in recent years, owing to government restrictions on beef exports with the purpose of supporting the domestic market and helping with lower prices.

Nevertheless the Brazilian and Argentine beef markets had an unusual year in 2021. Traditional animal protein producers, the two countries witnessed declines in their exports, particularly in the last months of the year. Overall compared to 2020, Brazil beef sales dropped 9,92% while Argentine exports decreased 13,84%.

The reduction experienced by Brazil can be explained by the beef embargo imposed by China. In effect on September 2021, Brazil voluntarily suspended exports to China after the identification of two cases of mad cow disease in the country.

The World Organization for Animal Health (OIE) recognized that these were atypical episodes and that the risk to the national herd was negligible. Despite this, China insisted in freezing Brazilian beef exports for over three months until December 15.

The drop in Argentine beef shipments were motivated by the high price of the product in the domestic market, and thus the government suspended all exports in May 2021. ” As a consequence of sustained increases in the price of beef cuts in the domestic market, the national government decided to implement a set of emergency measures to better organize the sector, restricting speculative practices, improving the traceability of exports and avoiding tax evasion,” said the decree issued at the time.

Further measures were implemented, and given the deteriorating economic situation of Argentina and its impact on inflation, the country’s export ban on certain beef cuts was extended until the end of 2023.

As a result of this situation, Mercosur junior member Uruguay strongly benefitted and saw beef shipments increase 35%. The same can be said of the other Mercosur member, Paraguay, that also experienced a record year of beef exports in 2021.

World.title: Unemployment in Chile almost back at 2019 levels
World.content:
Chilean authorities have reported Monday that unemployment nationwide had fallen in 2021 to 7.2% while in the same period of 2020 it had hit 10.3%. In the middle of the social uprisings of 2019 it had been recorded at 7.1%.

“It is the eighth consecutive annual decrease in the unemployment rate,” said Leonardo González of the National Institute of Statistics (INE), which also reported the unemployment rate for women stood at 7.4%, and for men at 7.1%.

In the quarter of the year, 119,930 jobs were created compared to the previous quarter. With seasonal adjustment, González specified, the number of jobs recovered quarterly reached 49,625.

Around 1,436,000 jobs have been recovered, which represented 77.5% of all jobs lost during the worst part of the COVID-19 pandemic, with 81.8% accounting for jobs held by men and 73.1% for those carried out by women.

The INE also said 80.1% of formal jobs and 94.5% of informal jobs had been recovered.

“If we continue at this rate, we estimate that we will soon be able to recover all the jobs that were lost in the worst moment of the pandemic,” González stressed. He warned, however, that “we have been consistently seeing these rates rise, but we are not yet seeing pre-pandemic levels.”

Employment ended 2021 at 54.3%, while the labor force participation rate ended at 58.5%, an 8.1% yoy increase, driven by women (11.7%) and men (5.7%).

Jobs were boosted by construction (22.2%), commerce (8.5%) and the hotels and restaurants (30.9%).

Economy Minister Lucas Palacios said that during “2021 we met the goal of strongly recovering economic activity and also employment.”

“We have recovered 80% of the jobs that the pandemic and recession destroyed. It was necessary to create health, operational security and certainty conditions to reactivate the economy and especially investment, which is the main source of opportunities,” Palacios said.

Palacios also highlighted joint efforts by the public and private sectors. “Incentives from the State can be very relevant to promote investment and employment,” the minister explained.

Labor Minister Patricio Melero agreed the unemployment figures meant “great news” and praised “the measures adopted by the government, both in economic and health matters,” which were yielding “results which are very positive for the country.”

(Source: ANSA)

World.title: Chile debates a state of emergency of up to eight months without congressional approval
World.content:
Chile debates a state of emergency of up to eight months without congressional approval

26th Wednesday, August 2026 - 08:42 UTC Full article

The main point of friction is parliamentary oversight

José Antonio Kast's government indicated on Tuesday it was willing to amend the constitutional security reform bill it submitted to the Senate on August 17, after the proposal drew objections both from the opposition and from parties within its own coalition.

The bill creates a constitutional state of public security emergency that the president could declare in the face of a serious and imminent threat to public order, or once public order has already been seriously affected. It would last up to 120 days, and the president could extend it once for an equal period without seeking parliamentary authorisation, adding up to 240 days. Only subsequent extensions would require congressional agreement. While in force, freedom of movement and the rights of assembly and association could be restricted, and communications intercepted.

The main point of friction is parliamentary oversight. The most severe states of emergency currently provided for in Chile's constitution — the state of siege, envisaged for civil war, and the state of assembly, for external war — require congressional approval within five days of being declared.

Senate president Paulina Núñez called for the measure to be removed from the bill and said her party, Renovación Nacional, would not support it. She argued a fifth constitutional state of emergency “is not necessary.” The president of the Unión Demócrata Independiente, deputy Guillermo Ramírez, said the executive had “gone a bit too far” and warned that “these rules always end up staying, and tomorrow there is another president.”

Interior Minister and government spokesman Claudio Alvarado said the government was prepared to listen to proposals. “Others may tell us: we find 120 days excessive, let's consider 30 days as under the other state of emergency and go to Congress for renewal. We are open to that,” he told Radio Bío-Bío. The executive has also indicated it would lower the legislative urgency, which set a fifteen-day deadline for debate.

The reform requires four-sevenths of sitting members of Congress and must clear the constitution, defence and public security committees. Senators from Renovación Nacional, Evópoli and unaligned groups have raised objections, leaving the government without an assured quorum within its own bloc.

A Cadem survey released on Sunday recorded 49% disagreement with the new state of emergency and 51% in favour of the government withdrawing the bill to adjust it. The text forms part of the Agenda against Organised Crime and Terrorism, comprising eight constitutional amendments and nineteen legislative initiatives, and includes the creation of an official registry of criminal organisations with constitutional rank.

World.title: Chevening Scholarship Falkland Islands; Deadline: 06-Oct-2026
World.content:
Chevening Scholarship Falkland Islands; Deadline: 06-Oct-2026

26th Wednesday, August 2026 - 08:35 UTC Full article

The Chevening crest

The Chevening Scholarship Falkland Islands offers exceptional future leaders from the Falkland Islands the opportunity to pursue a fully funded one-year master's degree at a UK university. The program supports individuals with leadership potential who want to develop their professional expertise and return home to contribute to positive social, economic, environmental, or community development.

What Is the Chevening Scholarship?

Chevening is the UK Government's flagship international scholarship program for emerging leaders from eligible countries and territories. The program enables talented professionals to study in the UK, build international networks, and develop the knowledge and skills needed to create positive change in their home communities.

Chevening scholars become part of a global network of leaders working on issues including:

- Climate action.

- Economic prosperity.

- Sustainable development.

- Public policy and governance.

- Community development.

- Conflict recovery recovery.

- International cooperation.

What Does the Scholarship Cover?

The Chevening Scholarship provides full financial support for an eligible one-year master's degree in the UK. The scholarship covers:

- Full UK university tuition fees.

- Monthly living allowance.

- Return airfare to the UK.

This financial support allows successful scholars to concentrate on their studies and professional development without having to fund the main costs of their UK education themselves.

Who Is Eligible?

Applicants must meet the core Chevening eligibility requirements. For the Falkland Islands opportunity, applicants must:

- Be a citizen of the Falkland Islands.

- Hold an undergraduate degree that qualifies them for a UK master's program.

- Have at least two years of work experience.

- Apply to three eligible UK university courses.

- Obtain an unconditional offer from at least one eligible course by the specified deadline.

- Commit to returning to the Falkland Islands for at least two years after completing the scholarship.

Applicants should also satisfy any additional requirements specified in the current Chevening application guidance.

Academic Requirements

Applicants must hold an undergraduate degree that meets the academic requirements for admission to their chosen UK master's program.

The selected master's course should be consistent with the applicant's academic background, professional experience, and long-term career objectives.

Because individual UK universities can have different admission standards, applicants should check the requirements of each selected course separately.

Work Experience Requirement

Applicants must have at least two years of work experience.

Professional experience should help demonstrate the applicant's development, achievements, leadership potential, and ability to contribute to their chosen field.

UK University Course Requirement

Chevening applicants must apply to three different eligible UK master's courses. The courses should be carefully selected based on:

- Academic background.

- Professional experience.

- Career objectives.

- Leadership ambitions.

- Intended contribution to the Falkland Islands.

Applicants must obtain an unconditional offer from at least one eligible course by the specified deadline.

Why the Chevening Scholarship Matters

Advanced Professional Skills. A UK master's degree can provide scholars with advanced knowledge and specialist expertise relevant to their professional goals.

Build International Networks. Chevening scholars become part of a global alumni and professional network, creating opportunities for international collaboration and knowledge exchange.

Strengthen Leadership. The program is intended for individuals with the potential to become future leaders and decision-makers.

Contribute to the Falkland Islands. Scholars are expected to return home after their studies and use their knowledge and experience to contribute to their communities and professions.

How to Apply

1. Confirm Your Eligibility. Check that you meet the citizenship, academic, work experience, university application, and return-home requirements.

2. Research UK Master's Courses. Identify three eligible UK master's programs that match your academic background and professional goals.

3. Apply to Three Universities. Submit applications to three different eligible UK courses.

4. Complete the Chevening Application. Prepare the required application information and demonstrate your:

- Leadership potential.

- Professional achievements.

- Career goals.

- Reasons for studying in the UK.

- Potential contribution to your home country.

5. Secure an Unconditional Offer. You must obtain an unconditional offer from at least one eligible UK university course by the specified deadline.

6. Return to the Falkland Islands. Successful scholars must commit to returning to the Falkland Islands for at least two years after completing their studies.

What Makes a Strong Candidate?

Applicants should be able to demonstrate more than academic qualifications.

A strong candidate should clearly communicate:

- Leadership experience or potential.

- Professional achievements.

- A clear career direction.

- The reason a UK master's degree is important to their development.

- How their proposed studies relate to their future work.

- How they intend to contribute to the Falkland Islands.

- Evidence of initiative, responsibility, and positive impact.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Applicants should avoid:

- Applying without meeting the citizenship requirement.

- Having less than the required two years of work experience.

- Selecting fewer than three eligible UK courses.

- Choosing courses that do not align with their career plans.

- Failing to check individual university admission requirements.

- Missing the deadline for obtaining an unconditional offer.

- Providing vague examples of leadership or professional impact.

- Failing to explain how their studies will benefit the Falkland Islands.

- Overlooking the two-year return requirement.

Tips for Applicants

Candidates can strengthen their preparation by:

- Starting university research early.

- Comparing master's programmes carefully.

- Preparing evidence of professional achievements.

- Identifying clear examples of leadership and initiative.

- Connecting their chosen degree with their career plans.

- Explaining how their knowledge could address priorities in the Falkland Islands.

- Tracking both Chevening and university deadlines.

- Reviewing the latest official Chevening eligibility requirements before applying.

Key Details at a Glance

- Scholarship: Chevening Scholarship

- Eligible applicants: Citizens of the Falkland Islands

- Study destination: United Kingdom

- Degree: One-year master's degree

- Funding: Fully funded

- Tuition: Covered

- Living allowance: Provided

- Travel: Return airfare to the UK

- Minimum work experience: Two years

- UK courses required: Three eligible courses

- University offer: Unconditional offer from at least one eligible course

- Post-study requirement: Return to the Falkland Islands for at least two years

Frequently Asked Questions

Who can apply for the Chevening Scholarship from the Falkland Islands? The opportunity is intended for citizens of the Falkland Islands who meet the Chevening academic, professional, work experience, and other eligibility requirements.

Is the Chevening Scholarship fully funded? Yes. The scholarship provides financial support for tuition fees, a monthly living allowance, and return airfare to the UK.

How long is the master's degree? Chevening supports a one-year master's degree at an eligible UK university.

How much work experience is required? Applicants must have at least two years of work experience.

How many UK university courses must applicants apply for? Applicants must apply to three different eligible UK master's courses.

Do applicants need an unconditional university offer? Yes. Applicants must secure an unconditional offer from at least one eligible UK course by the specified deadline.

Do scholars have to return to the Falkland Islands? Yes. Successful scholars must commit to returning to the Falkland Islands for at least two years after completing their studies.

Conclusion

The Chevening Scholarship Falkland Islands provides talented professionals with an opportunity to gain a fully funded UK master's degree while developing leadership skills and international connections. The program is particularly suited to candidates who can demonstrate professional experience, leadership potential, clear career ambitions, and a strong commitment to returning to the Falkland Islands and contributing to positive change in their communities.

For more information, visit Chevening.

World.title: PM Burnham on taxes, “I won't be unrealistic, and people need to understand that”
World.content:
PM Burnham on taxes, “I won't be unrealistic, and people need to understand that”

26th Wednesday, August 2026 - 08:25 UTC Full article

“I ran Greater Manchester for 10 years and we ran a very tight ship with rock solid finances,” Burnham said.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has suggested tax rises could be on the cards in the coming Autumn Budget, warning “I won’t be unrealistic” over the state of the public purse. The PM quickly pledged to give people “breathing space” and ease the cost of living after taking the keys to No.10 last month.

But in fresh comments during his visit to Ukraine, Burnham acknowledged the fiscal pressures facing the UK and said his spending packages would be fully funded.

When pressed on whether he would need to raise taxes to cover spending gaps, he said: “I won’t be unrealistic, and people really need to understand that.

“We are in a challenging position; whatever I do will be carefully thought through, it will be funded, and there will be no more to come as we go into the autumn.”

Top economists have already warned that Chancellor John Healey will have little capacity to announce fresh spending pledges after a spike in borrowing costs and the energy price shock triggered by the US-Iran war.

Burnham, however, has insisted he would “try to help” Brits in “whatever way” possible, adding that he wouldn’t “take risks” with people’s jobs or household finances.

“I will always take a careful approach to things. I ran Greater Manchester for 10 years and we ran a very tight ship with rock solid finances,” Burnham said.

Last week, official figures revealed Healey had overseen a surprise deficit in his first month as Chancellor. Government borrowing was recorded at £1.8bn in July, which overshot market expectations. Analysts had predicted there would be no difference between expenditure and receipts in July.

Analysis from Capital Economics has suggested that there would be “little scope” to raise borrowing in the Budget later this year. A maximum of about £15bn could be accepted, according to the consultancy, though tax rises are likely.

A separate note by senior economist Ashley Webb warned that the UK was on track to post a deficit of above four per cent of GDP for the seventh year in a row.

World.title: Bolivia deploys troops against blockades over a decree its own government wants repealed
World.content:
Bolivia deploys troops against blockades over a decree its own government wants repealed

26th Wednesday, August 2026 - 08:00 UTC Full article

At least ten organisations are defying the state of emergency

Bolivia's government deployed military and police units on Tuesday in the municipality of Yapacaní, in Santa Cruz department, ahead of announced road blockades called by farming organisations against the decree that raised the price of diesel for large consumers. Hours later, the deputy interior minister acknowledged that the same measure must be annulled.

“Faced with the public call to blockade in Yapacaní, a preventive deployment of the armed forces was ordered to assist the Bolivian Police. The mission is to prevent the blockade, protect the road and, above all, avoid clashes,” said Defence Minister Ernesto Justiniano. He specified that under the state of emergency in force people may “march, protest, meet and express disagreement,” but not block roads or impede free movement. The route remained clear throughout the day.

In parallel, deputy minister Hernán Paredes met leaders at the headquarters of the Intercultural Federation of Agricultural Producers and reached an agreement. “The supreme decree the government issued is indeed causing many problems in its application,” he said. “I have informed the cabinet, which has said it does want to repeal it, but it cannot stay as it is, because it has not met its objective.” He explained the aim was for large consumers to import their own fuel and for small producers to be guaranteed the subsidised supply, which did not happen. Farm leader Juan Cáceres said the executive had committed to seeking annulment within 48 hours and warned that otherwise the organisations would decide on further action.

Supreme Decree 5676, issued on August 17, set a reference price of 18 bolivianos per litre of diesel for industry, companies and large consumers, against the 9.80 that applies to public transport and to those consuming less than 5,000 litres a month. The increase amounts to 83.7%. Producers in Yapacaní say supplies have fallen by half.

The municipality is a sensitive point: its mayor, Juan Ramos, says it accounts for a large share of rice supply and connects the east and west of the country, meaning a closure would affect foreign trade and food distribution.

At least ten organisations are defying the state of emergency, among them mining cooperatives, transport workers, market traders and coca growers. Groups aligned with former president Evo Morales meet on Wednesday in the Trópico de Cochabamba to decide on measures. The state of emergency was declared on June 20 for 90 days, after seven weeks of protests demanding President Rodrigo Paz's resignation, and runs until September 20.

World.title: Argentine trips abroad fall 21.2% as Brazil and Uruguay lead arrivals
World.content:
Argentine trips abroad fall 21.2% as Brazil and Uruguay lead arrivals

25th Tuesday, August 2026 - 21:39 UTC Full article

Among tourists arriving in Argentina, 36.1% came from Brazil and 16% from Uruguay

The number of Argentine residents leaving the country in July fell 21.2% year on year, to 1.22 million people, according to the international tourism statistics report released on Tuesday by the National Institute of Statistics and Censuses. In the opposite direction, 830,200 foreign visitors entered the country, 17.9% more than a year earlier.

Of the residents who left, 697,200 were tourists and 531,100 were same-day travellers who did not spend a night abroad. Brazil accounted for 22% of outbound tourism and Paraguay for 15.2%.

Growth in inbound tourism is largely explained by same-day visitors. Of the 830,200 foreigners who entered the country, 466,200 were tourists, an increase of 9.1%, while 363,900 were same-day visitors, a category that jumped 31.5%. The latter are concentrated in border cities or on day trips to Buenos Aires and have a considerably smaller economic impact.

Among tourists arriving in Argentina, 36.1% came from Brazil and 16% from Uruguay. Third place went to the residual category “rest of the Americas”, with 10.8%, ahead of Chile, which in June had been the third largest source market with 12.8%.

The balance of exchanges remained unfavourable for Argentina: some 398,000 more residents left than visitors arrived. In the first half of the year the accumulated deficit was 3.49 million travellers, with 2.9 million foreign tourists against 6.38 million residents travelling abroad.

The fall in outbound tourism consolidates a sustained trend. In June the year-on-year decline was 22% and across the first half it was 13.2%. The shift reflects the relative rise in the cost of travelling abroad for Argentine residents following exchange rate movements, after two years in which an appreciated peso drove departures to record levels.

In monetary terms the imbalance also persists. During the second quarter foreign visitors spent 608.8 million dollars in Argentina, while residents spent 1,360.7 million abroad, leaving a negative balance of 751.9 million. Average daily spending was 87.3 dollars per person for foreign visitors and 105.8 for Argentines abroad.

Argentine tourism flows remain heavily concentrated within Mercosur: Brazil leads both arrivals and departures, and the top three origins and destinations correspond to countries in the bloc or neighbouring it.

World.title: Argentina acknowledges the Magellan treaties and seeks to defuse friction with Chile
World.content:
Argentina acknowledges the Magellan treaties and seeks to defuse friction with Chile

25th Tuesday, August 2026 - 21:28 UTC Full article

The 1881 treaty recognised Chilean sovereignty over the strait and established its perpetual neutralisation, with free navigation for vessels of all nations

Argentina's foreign ministry issued a statement on Tuesday reaffirming that its position on the Strait of Magellan is the one established by the 1881 Boundary Treaty and the 1984 Treaty of Peace and Friendship, a day after Chile announced it would send a note of protest over remarks by the head of the Argentine Air Force General Staff.

“Both instruments are fully in force and are considered definitive by the Argentine Republic,” says the text, titled “Argentina's position on the Strait of Magellan and cooperation with Chile in the South Atlantic and Antarctica.” The document, issued by the ministry headed by Pablo Quirno, makes no mention of Brigadier General Gustavo Javier Valverde, whose words triggered the episode.

Valverde said on Sunday, in an interview with a YouTube channel, that “Magellan, the south, the Drake, all of that is sovereignty” and that it was necessary to “maintain a presence” in the area because it constituted “a bioceanic key.” Chilean authorities interpreted his words as a challenge to their country's sovereignty over the southern passage.

The Argentine statement places the continent's southern extreme within the defence of its rights “in relation to the Malvinas Question, the South Atlantic and Antarctica,” areas of “growing centrality for their strategic natural resources, for their role in maritime routes and global supply chains.” It then reaffirms “the strategic value of cooperation with Chile” and lists mutual recognition of Antarctic rights, joint administration of protected zones, the Combined Antarctic Naval Patrol the two countries have maintained for more than twenty-five years, and a joint proposal for a marine protected area in the western Antarctic Peninsula.

The 1881 treaty recognised Chilean sovereignty over the strait and established its perpetual neutralisation, with free navigation for vessels of all nations. The 1984 treaty, signed at the Vatican after the 1978 Beagle Channel crisis, ratified the southern boundaries and settled the divergences over the passage's eastern mouth.

There is a recent formal precedent. Decree 457 of 2021, issued under Alberto Fernández's government, proposed strengthening the “exploration, study and joint control” of the strait and the Drake Sea. In March 2025, Javier Milei's government acknowledged in writing to Chile that this interpretation was an error under the treaties and undertook to replace it.

It is the first diplomatic friction between the governments of José Antonio Kast, who took office in March, and Milei, who maintain a close political relationship. The two countries share more than 5,000 kilometres of land border.

World.title: Chile protests to Argentina over a military chief's remarks on the Strait of Magellan
World.content:
Chile protests to Argentina over a military chief's remarks on the Strait of Magellan

25th Tuesday, August 2026 - 06:04 UTC Full article

He did not specify which country he was attributing that sovereignty to, but Chilean authorities and media interpreted his words as an Argentine claim over the southern passage

Chile's foreign ministry announced on Monday it will send a note of protest to the Argentine government over remarks by the head of the Argentine Air Force General Staff, Brigadier General Gustavo Javier Valverde, in which he mentioned the Strait of Magellan while referring to sovereignty matters.

Valverde spoke on Sunday in an interview with the YouTube channel La Fábrica del Podcast. “Magellan, the south, the Drake, all of that is sovereignty. We have to maintain a presence there, because that is a bioceanic key, Atlantic-Pacific, and that can alert you to a great many things,” he said. He did not specify which country he was attributing that sovereignty to, but Chilean authorities and media interpreted his words as an Argentine claim over the southern passage.

Chilean Foreign Minister Francisco Pérez Mackenna responded from Vietnam, where he was on an official visit. “Chile's sovereignty over the Strait of Magellan in its entirety is indisputable and is founded on the treaties of 1881 and 1984 signed by both countries,” he said, adding a “stern call to the authorities of other countries to be responsible with their statements and not confuse their citizens.” Interior Minister Claudio Alvarado said it was striking “that statements of this kind are raised from time to time, because there is nothing to discuss here.”

The announcement followed demands from lawmakers across the political spectrum. Socialist deputy Nelson Venegas argued that under international law, failing to protest such assertions may be construed as recognising foreign sovereignty over one's own territory. Alejandro Riquelme, a deputy for Magallanes, rejected the remarks and placed them within a series of earlier episodes.

The Strait of Magellan lies entirely under Chilean sovereignty under the 1881 Boundary Treaty and the 1984 Treaty of Peace and Friendship, the latter signed after the 1978 bilateral crisis over the Beagle Channel and mediation by the Holy See. The passage, together with the Drake — international waters between Cape Horn and Antarctica — is the main alternative to the Panama Canal for shipping between the Atlantic and the Pacific.

Valverde was appointed to head the Air Force General Staff in November 2024. He graduated from the Military Aviation School in 1989 and served as a fighter-bomber pilot.

Neither the Argentine government nor the Air Force had commented at the time of writing. The episode comes three weeks after Brazil downgraded its diplomatic relations with Buenos Aires to chargé d'affaires level.

World.title: The Pan-American Congress closes with a call for more equal north-south dialogue
World.content:
The Pan-American Congress closes with a call for more equal north-south dialogue

24th Monday, August 2026 - 21:55 UTC Full article

“It is necessary to reframe the dialogue between the north and south of the Americas in more equal terms,” said the meeting's coordinator, David Adler, at the closing session held at the Teatro Solís

The third Pan-American Congress concluded on Sunday in Montevideo with a call to reframe relations between the north and south of the Americas on more equal terms. The forum, which brought together some 150 lawmakers, governors and former heads of state from fifteen countries, will hold its next edition in Brazil in 2027.

“It is necessary to reframe the dialogue between the north and south of the Americas in more equal terms,” said the meeting's coordinator, David Adler, at the closing session held at the Teatro Solís. Conclusions were organised around regional integration, peace and security, care policies and welfare systems.

The congress was marked by one notable absence: former Colombian president Gustavo Petro, who promoted the first edition, held in Bogotá in 2024. Organisers cancelled his participation as a precaution to avoid exposure to sanctions, since Petro has been listed since October 2025 by the Office of Foreign Assets Control of the US Treasury Department, along with the then first lady, his eldest son and his interior minister. The designation, administrative rather than judicial in character, cited an alleged role in illicit drug trafficking. There has been no trial or conviction, and the Colombian government at the time described it as political persecution.

Among the subjects debated was the militarisation of public security in several countries in the region. Brazilian senator Humberto Costa warned that the inclusion of two organisations from his country on the US list of terrorist groups affects national sovereignty and could serve as an argument for military intervention under the justification of combating drug trafficking. He called for particular attention to Brazil ahead of October's presidential elections.

US lawmakers present referred to the midterm elections due in November in their country. Representative Jesús García called for prioritising the wellbeing of working people and respect for the sovereignty of Latin American nations.

The gathering, held from Friday to Sunday with both public sessions and closed-door debates, also included an address by Macarena Gelman, granddaughter of Argentine poet Juan Gelman, whose identity was taken from her at birth during Argentina's dictatorship and who was located years later by the Grandmothers of the Plaza de Mayo. The figure of the late Uruguayan president José Mujica was repeatedly invoked in speeches.

The forum began in Bogotá in 2024 and held its second edition in Mexico City in 2025. With Brazil chosen as host, the meeting moves to the region's largest country in the year following its presidential elections.

World.title: MND Local: Murals, an eclipse and aura farming in San Miguel de Allende
World.content:
The arroyo mural project is finally dedicated, a botanical sculptor reveals his latest project, a partial lunar eclipse is on its way, a spreading social phenomenon is coming to town and registration is open for the 2027 writers’ conference. Read on about some of the many community activities happening in and around San Miguel de Allende this month.

Mural project dedicated along the Las Cachinches Arroyo

A dozen new large-scale murals were dedicated Aug. 1 along 90 meters of the Las Cachinches Arroyo just west of Calzada de la Aurora and across from Fábrica La Aurora.

The mural corridor project, coordinated by Audubon de México, was designed to transform the previously neglected area into an open-air gallery celebrating the arroyo’s history, ecology and enduring presence.

“A lot of people don’t even know it’s there,” said Audubon de México President April Gaydos. “It will be a lovely green place for people to walk.”

Gaydos emphasized that the area is often “tagged” with graffiti, and that “murals are a deterrent for tagging.” She added, “There have been studies done on this. It’s educational as much as creating a place people want to visit.”

See the Audubon de México website for additional details about the project and the artists and sponsors who participated.

Regular cleanup efforts are also taking place along the Las Cachinches Arroyo. Volunteers have spent their Saturdays hauling out a large amount of garbage from between Calzada de la Aurora and Canción de India.

This work is being organized by Colectiva Ecología en la Montaña with coordination by Gabriel González and Juanita Nolasco. For more information or to donate to the arroyo cleanup project, email arroyocachinches@gmail.com.

Botanical sculptures combine wood, plants and metal

“Rooted in Rust” is former landscape designer Matt Wilson’s latest artistic project. The work combines reclaimed iron relics, wood and succulent plants in permanent botanical sculptures.

“For 1,000 years, you’ve seen a single plant in a pot,” Wilson told Mexico News Daily. “Mine is a single composition with color, with a filler plant, and everything that hangs out of the pot is called the spiller. Those make up the criteria, and they’re very attractive, and nobody else is doing that in San Miguel.”

Wilson hails from San Diego and lived in the San Francisco Bay Area for 40 years. He then moved to Costa Rica for four years and relocated to the Los López area south of San Miguel about 3.5 years ago. He started creating the Rooted in Rust sculptures last year.

“My girlfriend asked me, ‘Can you do something with this metal suitcase?’ and I laughed, and I said, ‘Of course, what do you want?’ So I came up with this succulent, which were unfamiliar to me, and there are thousands of succulents,” he said.

Wilson said the plants grew quickly, and in six months, the result was a “very nice” sculpture.

“I saw there was something there, and it really engaged my creative side,” he said. “I went out and bought an old rusted inner spring mattress, an old rusted tricycle with no rubber on the tires and an old Coca-Cola cooler. I put on an exhibition, and people said, ‘Oh, that’s great,’ and it just went from there.”

More images of Wilson’s work can be seen here.

Partial lunar eclipse coming later this week

The partial lunar eclipse starting Thursday night and ending early Friday morning is expected to be visible from San Miguel. The penumbral eclipse will begin about 7:23 p.m. Thursday in the east-southeast and reach maximum eclipse about 10:12 p.m., creating a reddish-orange effect known as an “almost blood moon.”

A lunar eclipse happens when the Earth moves directly between the sun and the moon, casting the Earth’s shadow onto the moon’s surface. They only occur during a full moon when the sun, the Earth and the moon all line up.

Close to 1 billion people in South and North America will be able to fully see the eclipse, while more than 3 billion should be able to view part of the five-hour event. According to NASA, a similar eclipse last occurred on Aug. 16, 2008, and the next one will be on Sept. 7, 2044.

Ready for an ‘Aura Farming Battle’ this Sunday?

It’s possible to observe the social phenomenon of “aura farming” on Sunday at 3 p.m. at Parque Juarez on the small basketball courts. The prize is 500 pesos.

Aura farming is a trend that started on TikTok and Instagram and consists of young participants silently making moves designed to appear confident and cool without seeming deliberate. The audience’s response decides who wins.

Aura farming battles have been spreading throughout Mexico, with recent ones occurring in Mexico City, Veracruz and Coahuila. Additional gatherings have been reported in Argentina, Brazil, Peru and Bolivia.

Writers’ Conference registration discount ending soon

The San Miguel Writers’ Conference and Literary Festival is offering $95 off its registration packages until Aug. 31. The regular prices go into effect Sept. 1.

Scheduled for Feb. 10-14, 2027, at the Hotel Real de Minas, the conference will feature keynotes by U.S. authors Amor Towles and Jennifer Finney Boylan, Canadian author Michelle Good and Mexican author Martha Bátiz, along with literary presentations, workshops and many other events.

More information, along with the 2027 conference schedule, bilingual programming and free community events, is available here.

Cathy Siegner is an independent journalist based in San Miguel and Montana. She has journalism degrees from the University of Oregon and Northwestern University.

World.title: México Canta and Spotify partner up to amplify young talent across Mexico-US border
World.content:
México Canta is turning up the volume for its second season, tapping the music streaming service Spotify to give the cross-border contest’s top singers even more exposure.

The partnership will give the 14 semifinalists from Mexico and the United States an official Spotify playlist and offer them a career-development master class, and the three winners will be invited to a Spotify flagship event for emerging artists, the Mexican government said in a press release.

México Canta (Mexico Sings) is a federal initiative led by the Culture Ministry in collaboration with the Mexican Music Council.

Open to Mexican and Mexican American artists ages 18 to 29, it is akin to “American Idol” with one overriding rule: It seeks songs promoting themes such as love, tradition and culture rather than glorifying violence, drugs, discrimination or misogyny.

Unlike last year’s inaugural contest — which staged semifinals in Chicago, Houston, Los Angeles, Tijuana, Oaxaca and Mexico City that blossomed into must-see TV — this year’s whittling-down process was left in the hands of the Mexican Music Council. It reviewed online auditions to determine the best of more than 16,000 entries (about 1,200 more than last year).

Of the 5,760 U.S.-based registrants, seven were chosen for the first semifinal, which was Sunday at the Orpheum Theatre in Los Angeles. It produced three finalists.

The second semifinal is scheduled for Sunday at the Ángela Peralta Theater in Mazatlán, where three more finalists will be selected, plus a wild-card from either semifinal. The contest drew 10,528 registrants from Mexico.

The finals are set for Sept. 13 at the Auditorio Nacional in Mexico City, where winners will be selected in three as-yet-unnamed categories. Last year’s titles were for best performer and best song, alongside a wild-card pick.

The agreement with Spotify comes during a boom in regional Mexican music.

Global listening to the genre on Spotify has risen 450% over the last five years, while consumption in Mexico increased 560%, the Ministry of Culture noted. Moreover, more than 70% of Spotify Mexico’s daily Top 50 is made up of Mexican artists compared to 10% a decade ago, the ministry added.

Also, for the first time, Mexico has entered the world’s 10 largest recorded-music markets, noted Spotify representative Karen Duque.

“A decade ago, it was quite difficult to imagine that Mexico would become one of the most important powers in the world of the music industry,” she said.

Following the finals in Mexico City, the three winners will be scheduled to perform during Mexican Independence Day celebrations on Sept. 15.

With reports from La Jornada and Informador

World.title: Mexico’s first solar panel recycling plant coming to Jalisco
World.content:
The western state of Jalisco will soon boast Mexico’s very first solar panel recycling plant, an installation with the capacity to recover up to 95% of the materials from equipment that reaches the end of its useful life.

The project evolved in response to the growth of photovoltaic generation in Jalisco, which has approximately 1.6 million installed solar panels, equivalent to about 50,000 tonnes of equipment.

Rafiqui — a non-profit civil organization dedicated to recycling and repurposing — is building the plant in Ciudad Guzmán, about 125 kilometers south of the state capital, Guadalajara.

In its initial phase, the recycling plant is expected to process up to 1,000 tonnes of “retired” solar panels annually, recovering core materials like silicon, aluminum and silver to be used in other production chains.

Rafiqui director Ximena Cantú said her company’s model “goes beyond recycling because we believe in the circular economy.”

Before sending any materials to the recycling plant, the decommissioned equipment will be evaluated to determine if it is still functional. Those that remain in suitable condition may be reused or donated to communities and non-profit organizations.

Manuel Gómez-Herrera Lasso, executive director of the Mexican Photovoltaic Industry Association, praised Jalisco as a pioneer in the adoption of solar energy. The first photovoltaic system interconnected to the national energy grid was installed in Jalisco in 2007.

The growth of the technology, however, presents a challenge for managing the waste generated by the replaced equipment.

The International Renewable Energy Agency estimates that 30,000 tonnes of solar panels in Mexico will be retired due to premature failure by 2030, while at the same time 6,500 tonnes will reach the end of their life cycle naturally.

As part of the strategy to address this, Rafiqui has established a collection center in a southern Guadalajara neighborhood to receive small volumes. It has also developed a collection scheme for larger quantities in different regions of the country.

Additionally, Rafiqui is holding discussions with municipalities and industrial associations to expand the alternatives for collecting solar panels in Jalisco.

With reports from Mexico Industry, Jalisco TV and El Financiero

World.title: Schneider Electric plans major Querétaro expansion to meet growing power demand
World.content:
Schneider Electric, a France-based multinational, plans to expand its manufacturing capacity in Querétaro state with 115,000 square meters of new industrial facilities that will support the creation of 4,000 direct jobs by the end of 2027, the company has announced.

The expansion includes two completed facilities and a third planned for a later growth phase, where the firm will manufacture solutions for electrical distribution, equipment for critical energy infrastructure, and specialized projects under custom “engineer-to-order” (ETO) models.

Schneider Senior Vice President of Power Systems and ETO Guillaume Le Gouic said that Querétaro, in Mexico’s Bajío region, provides the talent, industrial capacity, and strategic location required to advance the region’s electrification and digitalization processes.

“We are very pleased to continue growing in Querétaro, and very grateful for the support of the state government,” Schneider Mexico and Central America President Luis D’Acosta Anezin said. “The truth is, we feel right at home here, and this is the first of many investments to come, and we’re very happy and excited.”

According to the announcement, Schneider is now hiring between 200 and 250 workers a month and training engineers, technicians, and specialists in advanced manufacturing and energy infrastructure to support its operations.

Querétaro Governor Mauricio Kuri González met with Schneider Electric executives last Wednesday to discuss the project. While the company did not share an investment figure, Kuri González said he expects the total job creation from new facilities to reach 7,000 or 8,000 by 2028.

Schneider currently has production plants in Querétaro, Nuevo León, and Tlaxcala, supporting industrial demand in North America and Central America.

The firm aims to strengthen production for sectors with a higher demand for electrical infrastructure, such as data centers, industry and the digital economy.

In a 2025 interview with MND, the president and managing director of Schneider Electric Mexico & Central America, Jesús Carmona Colina, said that President Claudia Sheinbaum had “correctly recognized that more energy is needed in Mexico” to meet demand, including from the country’s growing industrial sector.

He noted an energy imbalance in Mexico, with sufficient electricity in some regions and a shortfall in others.

As part of its overarching economic strategy, Plan México, the government aims to increase electricity generation by 22,000 megawatts by 2030, investing US $12.3 billion over the next six years to build new power plants, $7.5 billion to strengthen transmission networks and $3.6 billion to improve distribution networks.

With reports from Mexico Industry, Mexico Now and TYT

World.title: Despite a Q2 dip, first-semester Foreign Direct Investment was Mexico’s highest ever
World.content:
Mexico attracted US $34.968 billion in Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) between January and June 2026, marking the highest amount ever recorded for a first semester, the Economy Ministry (SE) reported.

The figure represents a 2.1% year-on-year increase compared to the same period last year and confirms Mexico’s continued appeal as a destination for established international companies.

Going back further, foreign investment practically doubled, with an accumulated growth of 89.7%, compared to the first half of 2021, when Mexico attracted US$18.433 billion,

The 2026 advance lost momentum, however, during the second quarter, when revenues reached $10.464 billion, 3.5% less than the $10.848 billion originally recorded during the same period in 2025.

The SE attributed the contraction to last year’s high base of comparison and indicated that it does not represent a change in trend. Despite the year-on-year decline, the result for the second quarter of 2026 was the second highest in the last 16 years.

Who received the foreign investment?

The manufacturing industry was the primary recipient of the arriving resources, receiving $13.482 billion, equivalent to 38.6% of total FDI. The figure represents a 9.3% year-over-year increase for manufacturing.

Financial and insurance services ranked second, with $10.15 billion, followed by the transportation, postal, and warehousing sectors, which registered the strongest growth, attracting $2.65 billion.

Mexico City came in as the top destination for foreign investment, receiving $16.862 billion, or 48.2% of the national total. It was followed by Nuevo León, with $3.712 billion; México state, with $2.114 billion; Baja California, with $1.743 billion; and Jalisco, with $1.406 billion.

Together, these five states accounted for 73.9% of all FDI received during the first half of the year.

Where did the first semester FDI come from?

In the first half of 2026, the United States remained the leading source of FDI in Mexico, with a flow of $16.871 billion, equivalent to 48.2% of the total.

Spain ranked second with $4.954 billion, followed by Canada ($1.741 billion), Australia ($1.698 billion) and Germany ($1.647 billion).

According to the SE, the positive FDI numbers are attributed to the country’s macroeconomic and institutional fundamentals and the guidelines of Plan México, the government’s flagship economic and policy strategy.

Mexico News Daily

World.title: MND Local: Is the tourism outlook in Los Cabos improving?
World.content:
Spring was a poor season for tourism in Mexico. International air arrivals — the driver of 80% of all tourism revenue in the country, with two out of every three passengers hailing from the U.S. — were down nationwide in March, April and May.

That trend continued in June, as spring turned to summer, despite Mexico’s role as a host for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. But outside of the host cities, which received a boost from the event — albeit not to the extent expected — high-value tourism to traditional beach tourism destinations in Mexico like Los Cabos continued to plummet. International air arrivals fell 7.1% in Los Cabos in March, 9.7% in April, 10.5% in May and 14.2% in June, relative to the same months in 2025.

July was even worse, with international air arrivals falling by 16.6%. That means that in the first seven months of the year, international tourism fell by 7.2% in Los Cabos, with overall tourism declining by 5.4%. Unfortunately, things don’t look much better for the second half of the year, with U.S. air bookings for the next six months down 13% from 2025.

That said, there are some signs of a brightening outlook for Los Cabos.

Domestic tourism is beginning to improve

After seeing falling numbers for 10 straight months — from July 2025 to April 2026 — the domestic travel market has recently shown signs of life in Los Cabos. Domestic arrivals nosed into positive numbers in May and were up 7% in July, with nearly 20,000 more Mexican nationals visiting the destination relative to the same month in 2025.

Low season rates are part of the appeal. High season prices typically peak in April (US $470 per night for hotels in 2026), with summer seeing lower average hotel room rates in Cabo San Lucas (US $336 as of the most recent numbers from May) and San José del Cabo (US $339), as well as for the destination as a whole (US $414).

But since airline bookings for the next six months are up 5.4% domestically, with a better than 9% increase in passengers from Mexico City expected through the end of the year, it appears that this isn’t just a seasonal spike, but rather a welcome return to form for what has traditionally been an important market, accounting for over one-third of overall tourists to Los Cabos.

Tourism from Canada is on the uptick

The Canadian tourism market is not as robust as the U.S., at least not in Los Cabos. Last year, for example, over two million tourists from the U.S. visited Los Cabos, versus 215,000 from Canada. So even though tourism from Canada is up 8.8% in 2026, that doesn’t make up for U.S. tourism being down by more than 7%.

Still, it’s significant that numbers are up this year for visitors from Canada, as well as for visitors from Europe, the Caribbean, and Central and South America. This diversification is important to the local economy, especially if U.S. tourism to Mexico continues to slump.

Cruise tourism continues to boom

The reason international arrivals are considered “high-value” is because these tourists, on average, spend more than US $1,300 each. Cruise ship tourists, by contrast, traditionally spend less than US $100 per person. Every little bit helps, however, especially when it comes to keeping businesses alive in downtown Cabo San Lucas.

Last year, the Land’s End city set a record, surpassing one million cruise ship tourists for the first time. This year, that record will almost certainly be broken, as through June, cruise ship arrivals were up by 64.5% through June; 789,919 through the first six months of 2026, compared to 480,198 during the same timeframe in 2025.

If this pace continues, Cabo San Lucas will top 1.5 million cruise ship passengers for the year, cementing its position as the nation’s fourth largest cruise ship destination, behind only Cozumel, Mahahual and Ensenada.

New air routes added to replace those that have been lost

Airline capacity cuts due to rising jet fuel costs, combined with a declining demand for seats to Mexican beach destinations, have led to the cancelation of several Los Cabos-bound routes this year, including the loss of Southwest flights from Baltimore, Chicago and Indianapolis, and a Delta flight from Seattle.

Fortunately, though, new flights have been added this summer to make up for, or at least mitigate, previous tourist losses. Southwest added its first nonstop flight from Las Vegas to Los Cabos during the first week of June, the same week a new domestic route was added by Volaris connecting Puebla to Los Cabos.

Once high season returns this fall, expanded service to Los Cabos will also be offered by several airlines, including Volaris in Mexico; American, Southwest and United in the U.S.; and Air Transat, Porter and WestJet in Canada.

Chris Sands is a writer and editor for Mexico News Daily, and the former Cabo San Lucas local expert for the USA Today travel website 10 Best and writer of Fodor’s Los Cabos travel guidebook. He has also contributed to numerous other websites and publications, including The San Diego Union-Tribune, Marriott Bonvoy Traveler, Forbes Travel Guide, Porthole Cruise and Travel, and Cabo Living.

World.title: Former Sinaloa state official arrested in Utah with more than 100,000 fentanyl pills
World.content:
A former Sinaloa state official was arrested this month in a Utah hotel room with more than 100,000 fentanyl pills in his possession, U.S. authorities said.

Ricardo Verduzco Bernal, former head of the high-performance program at the Sinaloa Institute of Physical Culture and Sport, was detained in Salt Lake County on Aug. 12, according to an Aug. 20 statement released by the U.S. Attorney’s Office in the District of Utah. He is currently in preventive detention awaiting trial.

Over 200,000 Fentanyl Pills Taken Off Utah Streets During Two Separate Unrelated Seizures PRESS RELEASE: 🔗https://t.co/J4P7GFf1GC pic.twitter.com/m9luPFOsax — US Attorney Utah (@USAO_UT) August 20, 2026

In its statement, the U.S. Attorney’s Office said that “according to allegations contained in court documents, in August 2026, the FBI Wasatch Metro Drug Task Force initiated a criminal investigation on Bernal and co-conspirators, both known and unknown, associated with a drug trafficking organization believed to be distributing large quantities of fentanyl and other narcotics in the District of Utah.”

The suspect is referred to as Bernal throughout the statement, although his first surname is Verduzco.

The U.S. Attorney’s Office said that in August 2026, FBI agents “conducted a controlled purchase of fentanyl from Bernal.”

“As a result of the controlled purchase, agents obtained and executed a search warrant on a hotel room in Salt Lake County, Utah. On August 12, 2026, agents executed the search warrant, and Bernal was alone inside the room where agents located and seized approximately 11,160.65 grams of field-tested positive fentanyl,” the Attorney’s Office said.

“Agents estimated the fentanyl evidence to be approximately 111,000 fentanyl pills. According to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Bernal is in the United States on a visitor visa.”

At the start of its statement, the U.S. Attorney’s Office said that Bernal and another Mexican national “were indicted by a federal grand jury after they were arrested and charged in two separate and unrelated cases that led to the seizure of approximately 204,000 fentanyl pills in one week.”

“Jesus Alexis Cecena Cota, 22, of Mexico, residing illegally in West Jordan, Utah; and Ricardo Verduzco Bernal, 54, of West Valley City, Utah, were charged in two separate complaints August 13, 2026,” the statement said.

The U.S. Attorney’s Office said that “Bernal is scheduled for a jury trial on August 26, 2026, before a U.S. Magistrate Court Judge at the Orrin G. Hatch United States Courthouse in downtown Salt Lake City.” He is accused of “possession of fentanyl with intent to distribute.”

During a court appearance last Wednesday, the suspect maintained his innocence despite the discovery of the fentanyl in the hotel room where he was arrested.

Verduzco’s civil service career

Verduzco served as head of the high-performance program at the Sinaloa Institute of Physical Culture and Sport, a state government institute, during the governorship of Rubén Rocha Moya, who is also accused of drug trafficking by U.S. prosecutors. He left that position on July 31, according to the newspaper Milenio.

Verduzco previously served as the director of the Municipal Institute of Sport in Guasave, a city in Sinaloa around 150 kilometers northwest of the state capital, Culiacán. He occupied that position between 2022 and 2024. Before taking up that role, Verduzco was a manager with the Guasave water authority.

With reports from Milenio and Reforma

World.title: US issues security alert concerning area of Mexicali
World.content:
U.S. officials have expressed concern that a recent drug bust in the northern border city of Mexicali could result in retaliatory violence by the “Los Rusos” crime gang.

In a tersely worded alert issued on Monday, the U.S. Embassy in Mexico urged U.S. citizens to be aware of the potential threat, adding that all “U.S. government activities in, and travel to, Mexicali have been suspended on August 25.”

The statement encouraged U.S. citizens to be aware of their surroundings at all times, to avoid local government buildings in Mexicali and to “notify friends and family of your safety in the event of an incident.”

The U.S. Consulate in Tijuana — about 180 kilometers (112 miles) east of Mexicali — shared the warning, but did not provide any details about the supposed threat.

On Tuesday morning, President Claudia Sheinbaum said the alert was issued due to the possibility that a criminal group could pose a danger, though she said “there is no specific issue.”

The Baja California state government said it has reinforced security in the entire municipality of Mexicali with the cooperation of federal agents and members of the armed forces.

“Prevention, patrol and surveillance efforts continue on a permanent basis to protect the peace of mind of Mexicali families,” Baja California Governor Marina del Pilar said on social media.

She urged members of the public to call 911 in case of emergency, or to make an anonymous report by calling 089.

State Security Minister General Laureano Carrillo said that “rigorous, continuous and coordinated work” is being carried out by state and federal authorities “to prevent and contain any type of contingency in Mexicali.” Mexico’s federal security cabinet released a statement saying it had not identified evidence confirming “a specific or imminent risk to the public” at midday on Tuesday.

El Gabinete de Seguridad informa: pic.twitter.com/43Qwwxr7O1 — Gabinete de Seguridad de México (@GabSeguridadMX) August 25, 2026

Last week, Mexican authorities — with the help of the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) — seized 120 kilograms of fentanyl pills in a joint operation carried out in Mexicali by federal and state agents.

The raid occurred at a property linked to “Los Rusos” — a cell operating as part of the Los Mayos faction of the Sinaloa Cartel — and resulted in the seizure of approximately 4 million opioid doses.

According to reporting by Luis Chaparro, U.S. authorities decided to issue the security alert after the DEA intercepted at least one call in which alleged members of Los Rusos appeared to be planning an attack on the Municipal Police and the offices of the Federal Attorney General’s Office in Mexicali.

With reports from El Financiero, El País and La Jornada

World.content:
Gastronomy & Talent

Four Colombian chefs have secured places in the Latin America and Caribbean regional final of the S.Pellegrino Young Chef Academy Competition 2026/2027. It is the first time Colombia has placed this many finalists in the contest.

A Record Showing for Colombian Chefs

The selected chefs are Daniela Díaz Fuertes, Diana Pérez, Heisy Córdoba and Diego Ramírez. Their selection marks an unprecedented moment for Colombian gastronomy on this stage.

The competition is open to chefs aged 18 to 30. It aims to identify and promote the best young culinary talent in the world.

For Colombia, the result signals growing international recognition of its food scene. The country has steadily built a reputation for creative, ingredient-driven cooking.

How the Finalists Were Chosen

Why Colombia’s Food Scene Is Rising

Colombia’s culinary identity has deepened over the past decade. Chefs have drawn on the country’s biodiversity, from Pacific seafood to Andean tubers.

Cities like Bogotá, Medellín and Cartagena now host ambitious dining rooms. Young chefs are pushing beyond traditional recipes with modern technique.

Mexico City is about to host another round of its most playful viral competition. Young people will gather at major landmarks to pose, gesture and compete for something money cannot easily buy: aura.

What an Aura Battle Actually Is

An aura battle is a live, crowd-judged contest born from internet culture. Participants step forward and perform poses, facial expressions or short movements meant to project confidence and charisma.

The audience reacts, cheers or laughs, and the person who generates the strongest response wins. There is no official scoreboard or uniform rulebook across events.

The concept spread through short-form video platforms, where clips of winners and dramatic reactions travel quickly. In Mexico City, the trend has moved from screens to plazas.

The Main Mexico City Aura Battle at Monumento a la Revolución

The headline event is set for Saturday, 22 August 2026, at 1:00 p.m. It will take place at the Monumento a la Revolución, one of the capital’s most recognisable open spaces.

Islas Vlogs, a content creator known for organising public competitions, is behind this edition. The winner takes home 3,000 pesos (about US$150).

The monument’s wide esplanade offers plenty of room for a crowd. That matters because these events depend on audience energy as much as on the contestants themselves.

Other Aura Battle Venues Across the City

The Monumento a la Revolución is not the only stop. Bellas Artes hosts a battle on Thursday, 20 August, at 3:00 p.m., with prizes of 2,000, 1,000 and 500 pesos (about US$100, US$50 and US$25) for the top three.

Chabacano, near Line 9 of the metro, has an event on Saturday, 22 August, at 3:00 p.m. Parque México in Condesa follows on Sunday, 23 August, at 3:00 p.m., also with a 3,000-peso prize.

This spread across neighbourhoods shows how quickly the format has been adopted. Each organiser sets their own time, prize and crowd dynamic.

How to Join or Watch

Entry is generally open, but there is no single formal registration system. Most organisers coordinate through social media posts or simply invite people to show up.

Arriving early is the safest strategy, especially at high-profile spots like Bellas Artes or the Monumento. Crowds can grow quickly once a battle starts.

Spectators are just as important as participants. Their reactions effectively decide the winner, so even watching means taking part in the judging.

Why This Matters for the City

These battles turn public landmarks into low-cost entertainment hubs. They require no tickets, no infrastructure and no corporate sponsorship to draw a crowd.

For local businesses near venues, the foot traffic can be a small boost. For content creators, the events generate shareable moments that extend far beyond the plaza.

The trend also reflects how younger Mexicans are reclaiming public space. A monument built for political memory becomes, for an afternoon, a stage for performance and play.

What to Watch Next

Expect more dates to appear as organisers see the turnout. The format is cheap to run and easy to replicate, which makes it likely to spread to other cities.

For expats and visitors, these events offer a window into how digital culture shapes real-world gatherings in Mexico. They are free, public and entirely unpredictable.

The next test is whether the Monumento a la Revolución event draws the largest crowd yet. If it does, expect the aura battle calendar to keep filling through the autumn.

Italian singer Eros Ramazzotti has rescheduled his Mexico concerts to October 2027. The change affects shows in Monterrey and Mexico City, while the Guadalajara date has been canceled outright.

What Changed for Eros Ramazzotti Mexico Concerts

Ramazzotti will now perform at Arena Monterrey on 20 October 2027. The Mexico City show moves to Arena CDMX on 23 October 2027.

The Guadalajara concert has been removed from the schedule. No replacement date has been announced for that city.

Reports point to medical reasons behind the shift. The singer reportedly underwent vocal cord surgery and was advised to pause for rehabilitation.

Why the Dates Moved So Far Out

A vocal cord procedure is a serious matter for any touring artist. Recovery and vocal rehabilitation can take many months before a singer is cleared to perform again.

Pushing the dates to 2027 gives Ramazzotti a long runway to recover fully. It also avoids the risk of another postponement if healing takes longer than expected.

For fans, the wait is significant. But the alternative could have been a full cancellation of the entire Mexican leg.

What Ticket Holders Should Know

Tickets for the rescheduled Monterrey and Mexico City shows remain valid for the new dates. Fans who cannot attend have a refund option.

The refund window reportedly runs from 26 August to 30 October 2026. Anyone planning to request a refund should check their point of purchase for exact instructions.

Guadalajara ticket holders will need to seek refunds. Since that show is canceled, there is no new date to carry tickets over to.

The Business Impact on Mexico’s Live Music Market

Mexico is one of Latin America’s most important touring markets. Major international acts routinely sell out arenas in Monterrey, Mexico City and Guadalajara.

A postponement of this length creates ripple effects for promoters, venues and local vendors. Hotels, transport operators and hospitality businesses near the venues also feel the shift.

Still, keeping two of three shows alive preserves most of the tour’s economic value. The canceled Guadalajara date is the clearest financial loss for that city.

What It Means for Investors and the Events Sector

Live entertainment has been one of the strongest post-pandemic recovery stories across Latin America. International tours bring hard-currency revenue into local economies.

When a headline act reschedules, investors watch for signs of broader weakness. In this case, the cause is specific to one artist’s health, not a market downturn.

The long lead time to 2027 suggests promoters are being cautious. They are protecting the asset rather than rushing a return that could damage the artist’s voice permanently.

What to Watch Next

Fans should watch official channels for confirmation of the refund process. The reported window closes on 30 October 2026.

Any announcement about a replacement Guadalajara date would be significant. For now, that market is left out of the tour entirely.

Ramazzotti’s recovery timeline will also matter. If he returns to the stage earlier in other markets, confidence in the 2027 Mexico dates will grow.

The Roma Norte Setting

Roma Norte is one of Mexico City’s most vibrant neighbourhoods. It is known for its galleries, cafes, restaurants and strong creative energy.

Revuelta Queer House fits naturally into this landscape. Its location on Puebla 94 places it near other cultural spots that draw locals and visitors alike.

For expats and travellers, the area offers a walkable mix of daytime and nightlife options. The venue adds a distinctly LGBTQ+ community focus to that mix.

Why This Matters for Visitors and Expats

Community spaces like Revuelta Queer House help newcomers feel connected. They offer a place to meet people outside of work or tourist routines.

For LGBTQ+ expats, having a dedicated cultural venue matters. It signals that the neighbourhood supports diverse identities and creative expression.

Visitors can plan an afternoon gallery stop and stay for evening drinks. That makes the venue a practical and social destination in one trip.

What to Expect During a Visit

The gallery portion of Revuelta Queer House is open earlier in the day. The wine bar and rooftop come alive later, from late afternoon until midnight.

Because the venue is closed on Mondays and Tuesdays, plan your visit for the middle or end of the week. Weekends are likely to be busier given the neighbourhood’s popularity.

Bringing a small gift is optional but appreciated. It is a simple way to show respect for the space and the community it serves.

The Bigger Picture for Mexico City

Mexico City has long been a hub for LGBTQ+ culture in Latin America. Venues like Revuelta Queer House strengthen that reputation.

They also contribute to the local economy by attracting visitors who spend on art, food and drinks nearby. This supports small businesses across Roma Norte.

For investors watching urban cultural trends, spaces like this show how community venues can anchor a neighbourhood. They create foot traffic and a sense of place that benefits the wider area.
