World.title: President of Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council visits Iran
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The President of Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council, Faiq Zaidan, paid a high-profile, one-day official visit to Tehran on Tuesday to boost cross-border legal cooperation, develop bilateral judicial agreements, and address important security concerns.

Zaidan met with Iran’s senior executive, legislative, judicial, and security leaders, including the Iranian president, minister of justice, judiciary chief, speaker of the parliament, and secretary of the Supreme National Security Council.

The meetings focused on aligning judicial protocols and managing shared legal issues, strengthening legal relations, streamlining judicial procedures, activating cooperative security frameworks, reviewing legislative support for cross-border law enforcement, and addressing border stability and security measures.

Zaidan strongly opposed the foreign economic pressure against Iran, citing the latest US sanctions imposed under “Operation Economic Outcast.”

The Iraqi judicial chief indicated that Iraq will never forget Iran’s support during the US war against the country in 2003 and the war against ISIS terrorist groups.

Zaidan called for the full execution of existing bilateral legal and security agreements between Baghdad and Tehran.

The Iraqi official added that it is important to enhance intelligence cooperation, curb smuggling networks, streamline extradition protocols, and tackle the existence of anti-Iran groups along shared borders.

World.title: 30 Iraqi students join PetroChina Scholarship at China University of Petroleum
World.content:
Qingdao/ Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Thirty Iraqi university students are completing their preparatory semester at the China University of Petroleum (East China) in the coastal city of Qingdao, marking the inaugural cohort of the Pioneers of Excellence academic scholarship program.

The initiative represents the first time the Iraqi federal government has mobilized the state Training, Technology Transfer, and Scholarship Fund (TTSF) to sponsor undergraduate engineering scholars in China. Funded under the corporate social responsibility and capacity-building commitments of PetroChina Iraq – West Qurna 1, the program bridges bilateral energy development with engineering education.

The scholarship follows a customized “0.5 + 4” academic curriculum designed specifically by China University of Petroleum (East China):

Preparatory Foundation (6 Months): Intensive Mandarin Chinese language acquisition paired with foundation courses in advanced calculus, physics, and chemistry.

Undergraduate Degree (4 Years): Full Bachelor of Science degree tracks focusing on three core upstream disciplines: Petroleum Engineering: Reservoir management, well completion, and enhanced oil recovery (EOR). Mechanical Engineering: Industrial machinery design, refinery turbines, and pipeline hydraulics. Petroleum Geology: Geophysical seismic surveying, structural sedimentology, and basin modeling.



Selected through nationwide competitive examinations and panel interviews organized jointly by the Ministry of Oil and the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research, the students represent diverse Iraqi governorates.

Bilateral Diplomatic Patronage: During the program’s official inauguration ceremony in April, the Consul General of China in Basra, Chen Peizhong, and the Scientific and Educational Counselor at the Iraqi Embassy in Beijing, Dr. Mohanad Najah Jawad Al-Shorofi, addressed the cohort, highlighting the importance of developing native technical talent to lead Iraq’s domestic energy sector.

Student Commitment: Class representative Mohammed Al-Tawous reaffirmed the students’ commitment to mastering advanced engineering curricula to support the modernization of Iraq’s oil and gas infrastructure upon graduation.

Industrial Synergy: Since assuming the role of lead contractor at the giant West Qurna 1 oil field in 2024, PetroChina has prioritized local workforce upskilling, transitioning bilateral energy ties from traditional equipment procurement to joint human capital development.

Hydrocarbons form the foundation of Iraq’s national economy. By equipping domestic engineering talent with advanced training at premier international energy institutions, the Ministry of Oil aims to build a modern technical workforce capable of operating complex extraction assets, deploying artificial lift technologies, and managing next-generation energy infrastructure across southern oil fields.

World.title: Iraq and South Korea finalize financing for air defense missile system
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Minister of Finance Falih Sari met on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, with the South Korean Ambassador to Iraq, Lee Jae-myung, to finalize the financing mechanisms for the contracted air defense missile system between Iraq and South Korea.

The high-level meeting was attended by the Chief of Staff of the Iraqi Army, General Staff Officer Abdul Amir Rashid Yarallah, alongside the South Korean military attaché in Baghdad, according to an official statement issued by the Ministry of Finance and reported by the Iraqi News Agency (INA).

Key Financial & Operational Discussions

Contractual Financial Framework: The talks focused on operationalizing the payment schedules, legal frameworks, and treasury mechanisms required to fulfill bilateral contractual commitments without procedural delay.

Airspace Sovereignty Mandate: Minister Sari emphasized that securing Iraq’s airspace and modernizing territorial air defense capabilities remain national priorities to protect state sovereignty and critical infrastructure against external airborne threats.

High-Level Military Coordination: The presence of General Staff Officer Yarallah underscores operational synchronization between the Ministry of Defense’s procurement timetable and the Ministry of Finance’s budgetary disbursements.

Bilateral Commitment: Ambassador Lee Jae-myung and the South Korean defense attaché reaffirmed Seoul’s commitment to expediting technical execution and delivery timelines in line with agreed bilateral protocols.

The air defense procurement contract with South Korea represents a major technological leap for the Iraqi Air Defense Command.

By securing multi-tiered surface-to-air missile interception batteries, Baghdad aims to establish full sovereign control over its national airspace, replace legacy systems, and build an integrated radar and missile shield capable of intercepting advanced airborne threats, drones, and ballistic targets.

World.title: Chief Justice Zaidan and U.S. Envoy discuss post-coalition arms control
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The President of Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council, Judge Dr. Faiq Zaidan, received the Chargé d’Affaires of the U.S. Embassy in Baghdad, Joshua Harris, on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, to discuss judicial mechanisms and the enforcement of the rule of law following the scheduled conclusion of the International Coalition’s military mission.

According to an official statement issued by the Supreme Judicial Council and reported by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), the discussions focused on legal procedures regarding entities and individuals bearing arms in violation of the Iraqi Constitution and applicable laws, as well as institutional frameworks to enforce the rule of law universally across the country.

Key Discussion Pillars

Post-Coalition Legal Framework:Reviewing judicial and legal preparations ahead of the formal conclusion of the Global Coalition against Daesh/ISIS mission in Iraq on September 30, 2026.

Prosecution of Unregulated Arms:Outlining judicial measures against groups and individuals possessing, displaying, or utilizing unauthorized weapons outside the direct chain of command of state constitutional institutions.

Universal Rule of Law:Establishing judicial coordination mechanisms to ensure that legal statutes and constitutional provisions apply equally to all entities without exception.

The meeting comes as Iraq prepares for the transition of the U.S.-led international military mission into bilateral security partnerships.Restricting weapons exclusively to state custody remains a core pillar of the Iraqi government’s institutional program.

By coordinating judicial procedures alongside executive security measures, the Supreme Judicial Council aims to reinforce national sovereignty, enhance judicial oversight over armed actors, and solidify internal stability as the international military mandate concludes.

World.title: Iraq’s GCCE and Germany’s Sutco sign major waste-to-resource deal in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The General Company for Carbon Economics (GCCE Iraq) has finalized a bilateral Master Agreement with German waste treatment plant manufacturer Sutco® to construct a modern, integrated waste management and resource recovery facility in Baghdad.

The agreement, announced by GCCE Chairman Hayder Al Darraji, was signed under the joint patronage of the governments of the Republic of Iraq and the Federal Republic of Germany, marking a decisive shift toward circular economy infrastructure and sovereign carbon market integration.

The facility is engineered to process municipal solid waste at utility scale, converting daily refuse into certified agricultural inputs, renewable aviation fuel, and internationally tradeable environmental assets:

Daily Waste Intake: Processing capacity of approximately 6,000 tonnes of municipal waste per day.

Organic Fertilizer Yield: Annual output of 500,000 tonnes of high-grade organic fertilizer, produced in full compliance with German industrial quality standards to support domestic agricultural self-reliance.

Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF): Daily production of approximately 100 tonnes of SAF, providing low-carbon aviation fuel options and diversifying downstream energy products.

Industrial Recyclable Sorting: Comprehensive material recovery lines to extract plastics, metals, and inert recyclables for domestic industrial feedstocks.

Carbon Credit Generation:Estimated generation of up to 2 million tonnes of certified carbon offsets annually, positioning Iraq to enter international voluntary and compliance carbon credit markets under verified emissions reduction frameworks.

Cross-Sector Impact and Macroeconomic Value

Sector Core Contribution & Operational Outcome Environmental Protection Diverts 6,000 tonnes/day from open landfills, curbing methane emissions and groundwater contamination. Food & Agriculture Security Delivers 500,000 tonnes/year of organic fertilizer, reducing chemical fertilizer imports and restoring soil health. Clean Transportation Fuel Introduces domestic SAF production at 100 tonnes/day for cleaner aviation pathways. Climate Finance & Carbon Trade Unlocks 2M tonnes/year in carbon credits to mobilize sovereign climate capital under international standards. Industrial Circularity Reclaims secondary raw materials to feed local manufacturing and recycling clusters.

The partnership between GCCE and Sutco establishes a new benchmark for public-private environmental investment in Iraq.By coupling mechanical-biological waste treatment with advanced recycling, aviation bio-refining, and international carbon credit issuance, Baghdad is turning an acute municipal waste challenge into a high-yield green asset class.

World.title: Stocks edge higher as oil drops on fresh Mideast hopes
World.content:
Hong Kong – Most Asian stocks edged higher on Wednesday as oil prices extended a decline on receding concerns about another military flare-up between the United States and Iran, while traders were also nervously awaiting Nvidia’s earnings and key US inflation data.

Both main crude contracts have tumbled more than eight percent this week as Tehran and Oman edge towards a deal to partially reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while signs of fresh diplomacy to end the Middle East crisis added to the upbeat mood.

While US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the White House was declaring an “economic D-Day” against Iran and its trade partners, the measures were regarded as softer than many had feared.

Jason Wong at BNZ wrote: “The move could reflect market sentiment that the latest US strategy, ‘Operation Economic Outcast’, aimed at severing Iran’s remaining financial lifelines, could bring Iran back to the negotiating table and help resolve the conflict.”

The comments came as key Pakistani mediators reported positive talks with Iran’s president on Monday.

Pakistan’s Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi reported “a very positive and productive meeting”, saying on X he believes the “momentum will help pave the way for further progress and lasting peace in the region”.

Crude fell more than two percent on Wednesday, with Brent back well below $90 a barrel.

That has eased pressure on markets after last week’s spike fanned inflation fears and sent the yield on long-dated US Treasuries to their highest since 2007, just before the global financial crisis.

The cost of US borrowing easing and the prospect of more Middle East talks provided a much-needed boost to equities.

Tokyo, Hong Kong, Shanghai, Seoul, Wellington, Taipei, Bangkok and Jakarta all rose, though Sydney, Mumbai, Singapore and Manila fell.

Paris rose but London and Frankfurt edged down.

However, analysts said the simmering US-Canada trade row was causing some uncertainty, while the big event on the agenda this week is Nvidia’s second-quarter earnings on Wednesday.

The chipmaking titan has become a key marker of the reporting season as investors use it to judge the health of the AI boom that has sent markets to record highs over the past two years.

The figures come during rising angst about when the vast sums of cash pumped into AI software and hardware will see a meaningful return, if ever.

“Several analysts argue that the second-quarter number itself may end up mattering less than what management says about the quarter ahead,” said Axel Rudolph, a market analyst at IG.

“It’s entirely possible for the headline print to look solid and the stock to still sell off if the third-quarter guide comes in below what’s already embedded in current estimates.

“Conversely, even a modest second-quarter beat could support the stock if management raises the forward outlook and reiterates that supply, rather than softening customer demand, remains the binding constraint.”

Wednesday also sees the release of US personal consumption expenditure data, the Federal Reserve’s favoured gauge of inflation that could play a role in policymakers’ decision-making with regard to interest rates.

A soft reading could temper hike worries, but an outsized figure would likely ramp up bets on an increase in borrowing costs.

World.title: America unites in mourning for Dolly Parton
World.content:
Los Angeles – Americans of all stripes united to grieve the death of country music legend Dolly Parton, offering a rare moment of agreement as presidents of both parties joined entertainment and business giants in paying her tribute.

The singer, who was 80, was long heralded as one of the few celebrities that everybody loved.

President Donald Trump announced the lowering of flags across the United States for a week, calling Parton’s death a “true loss for millions of people.”

“Very sad to report that Dolly Parton, one of the greatest Country singers, and far beyond, EVER, has just passed away,” Trump posted on his Truth Social network. “There has never been anyone like her, and never will.”

His predecessor Joe Biden called Parton “an American original” who “treated everyone with kindness and respect.”

Republican George W. Bush praised “her work to promote literacy, advance health, and strengthen communities,” while Democratic former president Bill Clinton called her “one of a kind.”

New York’s mayor, Zohran Mamdani, praised Parton as “an irreplaceable champion of the working class.”

“We are a better country because of her,” he said.

– ‘Devastating day for humanity’ –

Singer Miley Cyrus took to X to mourn the passing of Parton, who was her godmother.

“So many evil people in this world and we had to lose a pure heart like Dolly Parton,” Cyrus said. “Devastating day for humanity.”

Popstar Taylor Swift, who got her start in country music, said a world without Parton “doesn’t feel possible, real, or right.”

“Her legacy will be an everlasting one,” Swift said in a statement shared with Variety and The Hollywood Reporter.

Beyonce, who collaborated with Parton for her Grammy-winning album “Cowboy Carter,” also paid tribute to the star.

“Bold and brilliant. Talented and tenacious. You taught so many lessons on how to be uniquely oneself,” Beyonce said on her website.

Rocker Jack White, who covered one of Parton’s most famous hits “Jolene,” called for her “instant sainthood” on Instagram.

Rapper Kid Rock, who worked with Parton, called her “quite simply” the greatest of all time.

“Thanks for the songs, the laughs, the humility and grace. Without a doubt a woman who God truly has his hands on.”

– ‘Magical and joyous’ –

Across the world of entertainment there was a palpable sense of loss, but also one of gratefulness for a person whose life was filled with joy and compassion.

Country music star Carrie Underwood said Parton “was probably the one person on planet Earth that everyone loved and could agree on”.

Popstar Sabrina Carpenter, who collaborated with Parton in 2024, recalled meeting Parton for the first time, describing her as “an angel walking the earth.”

“Your light will be something the world will search forever to find again,” Carpenter said on Instagram.

Actress Jane Fonda, who performed opposite Parton in “9 to 5” mourned Parton’s loss.

“Dolly will always be with us because she was so present, so powerful, so generous and playful that she is woven into all our lives and hearts forever,” Fonda said on Instagram.

Parton’s “Steel Magnolias” co-star Julia Roberts called her “a magical and joyous human.”

Country music star Jason Aldean said he was grateful to have been in Parton’s company a few times over the years.

“She was truly a bright light that shined just a little brighter than anyone else in the room,” he wrote on X.

– Apple, Amazon and a Beatle –

Beatle Paul McCartney posted on Instagram about meeting Parton early in her career, adding “she was so bubbly and full of life it is difficult to take in the news that she has passed.”

World.title: Meta and US states discuss settlement in landmark social media trial: report
World.content:
San Francisco – Social media giant Meta has been in discussions with multiple US states to settle a major child privacy and consumer protection case out of court, Bloomberg News reported on Tuesday.

With more than three billion users around the world, Meta is fending off accusations by a coalition of 29 states that it deliberately designed its products to hook children and gather their data while misleading the public.

The states are claiming that Meta violated both state-level and federal laws, though the exact allegations vary by state.

If Meta loses the case, the states could ask for around $200 billion in penalties, in addition to forcing the tech company to make changes to its products.

“Meta Platforms Inc. and state attorneys general have discussed a possible mid-trial settlement,” Bloomberg reported, citing anonymous sources familiar with the matter.

California, Colorado, New Jersey and Kentucky are leading the prosecution of Meta from a courtroom in Oakland, just a short drive from San Francisco.

Multiple state attorneys general sent out media advisories late Tuesday that they would hold press conferences on Wednesday regarding consumer protections and tech-related announcements.

Colorado said it would announce “a major update in a Big Tech case.”

Nevada, which is not involved with the trial in California, said it would make an announcement Wednesday regarding a “settlement” with “a leading technology company.”

Representatives for Meta and California Attorney General Rob Bonta did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Instagram boss Adam Mosseri took the stand on Tuesday as the trial entered its second week.

Mosseri admitted he touted newly launched safety tools for teens without disclosing low adoption rates from early testing several years ago.

Other witnesses have testified over the past week that Meta knew these tools were not effective and even that they were “designed to fail.”

Meta founder and chief executive Mark Zuckerberg was expected to testify at some point, as well.

World.title: Dasgaja from the sky: Why India and Nepal are deploying drones over no-man’s land
World.content:
Maintaining the Dasgaja buffer remains a challenge. Photo credit: ANI

What is Dasgaja?

Why India and Nepal are turning to drones to map a border where markers, rivers and land use have complicated boundary management.

An open but defined border

Cross-border occupation

What happens when a river moves but the border doesn't?

Missing boundary pillars and shifting river courses can make an already complex frontier harder to identify on the ground.

Most of the border is mapped

Why are boundary pillars a problem?

India and Nepal are using drone technology to survey parts of their open border where physical markers and changing landscapes create uncertainty.

Why use drones now?

Is this related to Kalapani and Lipulekh?

What this drone survey really means

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

India and Nepal are turning to drones to map a stretch of their border that, on paper, is supposed to remain empty.The area is known as Dasgaja, the no-man's-land or buffer zone along the India-Nepal boundary. But on the ground, parts of it have been cultivated, occupied or built upon. Rivers have changed course, while thousands of boundary pillars have gone missing or been damaged.Now, the two countries want to map that mismatch from the air.At the 13th meeting of the Survey Officials' Committee in Lucknow this month, India and Nepal agreed to use unmanned aerial vehicles to map cross-border occupation, including encroachments in Dasgaja. The joint survey is expected to begin after the monsoon, around September or October, and be completed within three years.The two sides will then jointly analyse the aerial imagery to establish how much land is being used by citizens on the other side of the recognised boundary.The move follows remarks by Nepal prime minister Balendra Shah in Parliament in May that India had encroached on Nepali land and that Nepal, too, had occupied Indian land in some places.Nepal's foreign ministry later clarified that Shah was referring to cross-border occupation and encroachment in Dasgaja, rather than making a new territorial claim against India.Dasgaja literally means "ten yards". It refers to the no-man's-land or buffer zone along the India-Nepal boundary.There is some variation in how its width is described. Indian reports generally refer to a 10-yard no-man's-land, while a study by Nepal's Institute of Foreign Affairs describes a 20-yard-wide buffer, with 10 yards extending from the boundary on either side.The principle is straightforward: the immediate area around the international boundary should remain free of occupation, making the border easier to identify, inspect and maintain.In practice, that is difficult along an open border stretching about 1,880 km. The boundary runs through farmland, settlements, forests, roads and river systems, while communities on both sides maintain deep social and economic links.Nepal's Institute of Foreign Affairs has documented people living in makeshift houses and tents within Dasgaja. Even when security forces remove such settlements, people can return.So, while Dasgaja is meant to function as a buffer on paper, parts of it have gradually become intertwined with everyday life and livelihoods along the border.India and Nepal share an open border. There is no continuous fence separating the two countries, and people routinely cross it for work, trade, family and other activities.An open border, however, does not mean an undefined border.The international boundary is established through boundary pillars, maps and geographic coordinates. Dasgaja provides an additional buffer around that line.Maintaining the physical markers has become a persistent challenge.According to Nepal's Department of Survey, 8,554 boundary pillars were installed along the border. Of these, 1,325 are missing and 1,956 are partially or completely damaged.A missing pillar does not automatically alter the international boundary. Its location can be reconstructed using survey records, coordinates and maps. But on the ground, the absence of a marker can make it far harder to establish where the boundary runs, particularly where fields, houses and roads are close to the line.The drone survey goes beyond Dasgaja. India and Nepal also want to map what officials describe as cross-border occupation.These are instances in which citizens of one country live on, cultivate or otherwise use land that falls on the other side of the legally recognised boundary.Nepal's foreign ministry said this was the issue Shah was referring to when he spoke about Nepal occupying Indian territory. It specifically linked the problem to the Fixed Boundary Principle used in riverine sections of the border.Several sections of the India-Nepal boundary run through or alongside rivers. Rivers naturally shift course through erosion, sediment deposition and the formation of new channels.That can create complicated situations when the legal boundary is tied to a position established in earlier surveys.Under the Fixed Boundary Principle, the boundary can remain fixed even when the river around it changes course.The result can be highly unusual: a farmer may continue cultivating land that a family has used for generations, only for a later survey to establish that the land now lies on the other side of the international boundary.Nepal's foreign ministry identified such riverine changes as one reason for cross-border occupation. Nepal's Kantipur has reported that decades of river-course changes have shifted thousands of hectares of land from one side of the border to the other.The new drone survey is not an attempt to redraw or rediscover the India-Nepal boundary.Technical boundary work dates back to 1981, when the Joint Technical Level Nepal-India Boundary Committee was established.After years of surveying, the committee prepared 182 strip maps covering about 98 per cent of the boundary. The maps were finalised in 2007 and excluded the unresolved areas of Kalapani and Susta.India's ministry of external affairs has also recorded that the strip maps covering 98 per cent of the boundary were authenticated in 2007.But the maps were never formally ratified by both countries as a final settlement.Nepal maintained that outstanding disputes had to be resolved, while India sought their endorsement.Even so, they remain an important technical reference.A boundary line on a map can be difficult to identify in a field without a physical marker.That is why India and Nepal maintain thousands of boundary pillars along the frontier. But many have been damaged, destroyed or lost, particularly in areas affected by rivers and erosion.The two countries have been working to restore them. At the seventh meeting of the Boundary Working Group in July 2025, India and Nepal agreed to jointly construct new pillars and repair damaged ones as part of their technical boundary work.Established in 2014, the Boundary Working Group deals with issues including the clearing of no-man's-land, construction and maintenance of boundary pillars, updating cross-border property records and other technical border matters.It does not cover the unresolved Kalapani and Susta disputes.The technical mechanism operates at three levels: the Boundary Working Group, the Survey Officials' Committee and Joint Field Survey Teams. Field teams conduct ground surveys, while the SOC and BWG examine the findings and determine the next technical steps.The immediate objective is simple: get a far more precise picture of what is happening on the ground.The UAVs will capture aerial images of areas where cross-border occupation is suspected. Indian and Nepali officials will then analyse the imagery jointly and compare it with existing maps, coordinates, boundary pillars and field records.Aerial imagery can show precisely where fields, houses, roads, rivers and other physical features sit in relation to the established boundary.But the most important element is not the drone. It is the joint verification.If both countries work from the same imagery and agree on the technical facts of a particular location, it becomes easier to determine what needs to happen next.The jointly verified record could eventually provide a basis for negotiating the removal of encroachments, restoration of land or, where necessary, compensation.The India-Nepal border has several separate disputes.Kalapani, Lipulekh and Limpiyadhura concern Nepal's territorial claims in the western sector and competing interpretations of historical maps, documents and the course of the Kali or Mahakali River.Susta is another separate dispute involving changes in the course of the Gandak or Narayani River.The current technical mechanism does not cover these unresolved areas. The 2025 BWG agreement specifically kept Susta and Kalapani-Lipulekh-Limpiyadhura outside its technical work.The Dasgaja exercise is narrower. It deals with no-man's-land, boundary infrastructure and cross-border occupation along the established boundary.At first glance, sending drones over Dasgaja may look like a relatively routine surveying exercise. It is anything but.The India-Nepal border is unusual: open to people, but fixed in law; socially intertwined, but internationally sovereign. Over decades, rivers have shifted, settlements have expanded, farms have crossed invisible lines and boundary markers have disappeared.That has created a gap between the border that exists on maps and the border experienced on the ground.The drones are an attempt to close that gap with evidence.They will not settle Kalapani. They will not redraw the map. And they will not, by themselves, resolve every dispute over land.But they could give India and Nepal something that has often been missing in sensitive border discussions: a shared, current and verifiable picture of what is actually happening on the ground.

World.title: Nepal flash flood unlikely to pose major threat to UP; 105 Indians among missing tourists
World.content:
The impact of the increased flow was expected to reach the barrage after around 8 pm on Wednesday.

Advisory by Nepal tourism board

LUCKNOW: The flash flood in Nepal on Wednesday is unlikely to cause major flooding in Uttar Pradesh, with the Gandak expected to remain below the danger level as the increased flow passes along Maharajganj and Kushinagar before moving into Bihar, a senior irrigation department official said.Speaking to TOI, Vikash Kumar Singh, Chief Engineer-II (Gandak), irrigation department, said there was no immediate reason to panic, though the local district administration and irrigation authorities had been put on alert and officials were deployed at vulnerable sites.âLast year, we successfully passed a discharge of around six lakh cusecs. There is no need to panic this time,â Singh said.Singh said the surge would reach the Valmiki Barrage near the Nepal-Bihar border and subsequently pass along Maharajganj and Kushinagar before proceeding into Bihar. Deoria will not fall in the path of this floodwater, he clarified.According to Singh, a sharp rise was recorded in the Trishuli river, a tributary of the Gandak, on Wednesday morning. At one stage, the water level was rising at around 20 cm per minute. However, the river subsequently began falling rapidly.The impact of the increased flow was expected to reach the barrage after around 8 pm on Wednesday. Singh said mountain rivers have steep gradients, resulting in both rapid rises and falls.As a precaution, canals have temporarily been closed because flash floods from the hills carry large quantities of silt. They will be reopened once the high-silt flow passes.Singh said officials currently do not expect the Gandak to cross the danger level or spill into agricultural fields in Uttar Pradesh. The affected river stretch along UP is roughly 30 km before the flow continues into Bihar.âThere is no need to panic. Everyone is prepared, and all our officials are working on the ground,â Singh said.Meanwhile, at least 105 Indian nationals were among hundreds of tourists reported missing following the flash flood in Nepal.According to a preliminary situation update issued by the Nepal Tourism Board on Wednesday, 384 travellers, including 291 foreign nationals and 93 Nepali nationals, were reported missing from the affected areas. The board said the information was preliminary and was being verified and cross-checked with travel agencies, guides, local authorities and security agencies.The list includes 59 Indians travelling with Samrat Tours & Travels and another 46 Indians with Leaf Holiday, taking the number of Indians identified in the preliminary missing list to 105. The nationalities of several other foreign travellers were yet to be confirmed.The Nepal Tourism Board said the flash flood struck the Bhote Koshi River in Rasuwa at around 8.30 am on Wednesday.

World.title: 'Highly malicious': India rejects with 'contempt' UN report on racial discrimination
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India has rejected concerns raised by a UN committee over alleged racial discrimination and rights violations by law enforcement agencies, calling references in the panel's report âpolitically motivatedâ and âhighly maliciousâ.

The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said the observations were made after the UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination (CERD) reviewed India's implementation of the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (ICERD) in Geneva on August 11-12.

The ministry said India had participated in the review in a spirit of constructive engagement and remained firmly committed to combating racial discrimination.

The MEA described the exercise as a routine treaty-body review in which India participated in the spirit of constructive engagement. It said India's commitment to combating racial discrimination remained unwavering, noting that India had played a leading role in negotiating and drafting the convention in the 1960s.

World.title: Centre sanctions ₹22 crore for 8th Khelo India Youth Games
World.content:
The Centre has sanctioned ₹22 crore for the 8th Khelo India Youth Games, which will be held in Hyderabad, Warangal, Karimnagar and Mahabubnagar in December this year in coordination with the Union Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. More than 6,000 athletes from across the country are expected to compete in 25 sporting disciplines, informed Union Minister of Coal & Mines G. Kishan Reddy on Wednesday.

Sports infrastructure worth nearly ₹30 crore has been created in Telangana under the Khelo India scheme. Of this, ₹11.5 crore was spent on developing facilities at Osmania University, including a synthetic athletics track, a synthetic tennis court and a dedicated swimming pool for women. Another ₹18.5 crore was utilised for creating sports infrastructure in various towns across the State, he said.

Around 33 Khelo India centres have been established across Telangana to nurture sporting talent at the grassroots level and in addition, around ₹8.5 crore has been allocated for sports development in the State through the National Sports Development Fund.

Highlighting the Centre’s investment in sports, he said the national sports budget has increased from ₹1,219 crore before 2014 to ₹3,794 crore in 2025-26. While 38 sports infrastructure projects worth ₹191 crore had been taken up across the country before 2014, as many as 350 projects worth ₹3,181 crore have been completed over the past 12 years, said a press release.

The sprawling campus of Kongu Engineering College at Perundurai, about 85 km from Coimbatore city, will soon be home to a 40 lakh sq. ft. research park called ‘Arivukoodam’.

The Kongu Vellalar Institute of Technology Trust, which runs six higher education institutions and a school at Perundurai, will develop the park at ₹100 crore. Vice-President of India C.P. Radhakrishnan will lay the foundation stone for the park on August 29.

C. Devarajan, president of the Trust, told The Hindu on Wednesday (August 26) that the park will be developed on the lines of the research park at IIT Madras. It will house the Technology Incubation Centre currently operational at the Kongu Engineering College, a tinkering lab, centres of excellence for various streams of engineering, and industrial research centres. Nearly ₹35 crore of the total investment will go towards purchasing the modern equipment to be used for research.

“We did a survey of over 100 industries of various sectors in the western districts of Tamil Nadu and got responses from more than 80. Based on their demands, we have decided to focus on five verticals at the research park, including 5G, electrification, and mobility. There will also be tie-ups with 10 industries, from Roots and Lotte India to Danfoss, who will have their satellite research and development centres at the Park,” he said.

Arivukoodam is expected to be operational by the end of next year or early 2028.

The aim of this project is to promote industry-driven research and development, bring deep tech solutions to the industries in the western districts, attract technology research experts to this region, and give students and faculty members real-time exposure to challenges of the industries in various sectors, Mr. Devarajan said.

“This is the actual industry-institute interaction that we have been advocating in various forums,” he added.

World.title: Tribal farmers demand joint probe into 64 acre land dispute in Chintapalli
World.content:
/PADERU

As many as 34 tribal farmers from Kandulagadi and Chinnagadda villages under Chintapalli panchayat in Alluri Sitharama Raju district, have urged the Tribal Welfare Department to conduct a district-level joint enquiry into a dispute over 64 acres of revenue lands claimed by both the farmers and the Forest Department.

In their representation, the farmers said they had been cultivating the lands for generations and possessed pattas and passbooks issued by the Revenue Department following surveys. They also claimed the lands inherited from their ancestors had been legally mutated in the names of family members.

According to the farmers, in January 2026, Forest department officials allegedly engaged contract workers to install cement boundary pillars in their agricultural fields. When questioned, the workers reportedly told them that the pillars were meant for telephone-related works. The farmers subsequently removed the pillars.

The Forest Department later claimed that the lands belong to it, leading to a dispute. The farmers alleged that cases were registered against some of them at the Chintapalli police station, following which the farmers subsequently lodged a complaint against forest officials.

The farmers submitted a representation to the district Collector on February 11, seeking intervention. Following this, the Chintapalli tahsildar initiated steps for a joint survey by the Revenue and Forest departments.

During the survey, Revenue officials reportedly examined revenue records, survey stones, village maps and other available records and informed the Forest officials that the disputed lands belonged to the tribal farmers.

“On March 20, the Forest Department issued notices to the farmers, allegedly without clearly specifying the extent of forest land they had allegedly encroached upon. The notices reportedly referred only to the removal of boundary stones and directed us to appear for an enquiry,” said tribal farmers K. Somalingam, Pangi Gurumurthy, in their representation to authorities in the Tribal Welfare Department.

The tribal farmers also stated that the dispute once again escalated recently when forest officials allegedly stopped borewell works being undertaken by the farmers for irrigation purpose and took some persons present at the site to the forest office.

Another survey was conducted at the mandal level on August 22, but the tribal farmers said it failed to resolve the issue or clearly establish the extent of rights over the disputed lands.

World.title: Nepal flash flood: 20 Tamil Nadu pilgrims from Tamil Nadu rescued, at least 37 still as landslips disrupt route
World.content:
A total of 57 persons from Thanjavur, Tiruvarur and Mayiladuthurai districts, who were on a tour to Nepal, were reportedly stranded at the Nepal-Tibet border following flash floods that took Nepal by surprise on August 26 morning.

Nepal flash floods live updates

Inquiries reveal that the tour was organised by a Kumbakonam-based tour operating company in a tie-up with a Nepal-based tour operating company. The tourists landed in Nepal a few days ago and were heading towards the Tibet border as part of their travel plan when the mishap took place.

Divided into three groups, they travelled in three buses to Tibet border, sources said.

Officials of the Tamil Nadu government have initiated action towards their rescue upon receiving the alert, official sources said.

As per the initial information, the pilgrims were on board three vehicles, and occupants of one of the vehicles have taken refuge in a Armed Police Force outpost at Timure, about 150 km north of Kathmandu, they said. The pilgrims were from various parts of Tamil Nadu, including Chennai, Puducherry, Chidambaram, Kumbakonam, Mayiladuthirai and Tiruchi. While a batch of 20 Indian tourists managed to get shelter at a Nepal border police outpost, the fate of others was yet to be ascertained, according to an official spokesperson of the travel company.

Nepal floods: PM Modi speaks to Balendra Shah, offers humanitarian assistance

“Along with them, two others from Maharashtra too joined them. The incident happened around 8 a.m. today. Occupants of one of the vehicles took refuge on top of a hill,” a source coordinating rescue efforts said, adding that it is not immediately known as to what happened to the occupants of the other two vehicles.

World.title: SC judge seeks transfer of Rajasthan HC Acting Chief Justice, asks why CJI ‘ignored’ appeals
World.content:
In three letters to Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, Supreme Court judge Justice Sandeep Mehta this month asked why his “fervent appeals” for the transfer of Rajasthan High Court Acting Chief Justice (ACJ) Sanjeev Prakash Sharma have been “ignored” despite there being “clear evidence of favouritism”.

In his first letter on August 2, 2026, Justice Mehta wrote to the CJI about the “grim and disturbing scenario” in his parent High Court in Rajasthan.

In the letter, he said the ACJ of the High Court, who is due to retire on September 26, displayed a total lack of leadership qualities and exhibited conduct unbecoming of a leader of the institution on more than one occasion. The Supreme Court judge reminded the CJI that he had been making repeated requests for the appointment of a regular Chief Justice to the High Court since the beginning of 2026.

“However, till date, the request to have a Chief Justice from another State in my parent High Court has met with no positive response,” Justice Mehta wrote.

He said there was maladministration and malpractices on both the judicial and administrative side of the High Court.

Cases were suddenly withdrawn and moved to the Bench of the Acting Chief Justice (ACJ) without any justifiable cause, Justice Mehta said. He said he was initially asked by the CJI to provide a list of these cases in writing, but was immediately thereafter assured that there was no need to place anything in writing and that suitable action would be taken.

The next letter, on August 10, noted that the CJI had asked Justice Sharma to respond to the shifting of cases, but said that no specific information was further available on the reply or facts of these cases.

Justice Mehta wrote that Justice Sharma called and humiliated judicial officers in Rajasthan to satisfy a “personal vendetta”. A full court meeting was held to designate a “large number of favoured advocates as seniors”, that too, on a working day, he said. He added that a “fanciful plan” was made for a multi-storied tower with almost 100 rooms to function as a guest house for the High Court, calling it a “sheer waste of public money”.

Justice Mehta also wrote that anguished judges of the High Court have said they were “frequently threatened” with retributive action, including transfer, by the ACJ, who claimed “closeness” with the CJI.

The Supreme Court judge noted that the CJI’s Bench had recently observed the growing trend of judges passing orders for extraneous considerations in the autumn days of their careers.

“It is indeed ironical that on one hand, the Chief Justice of India is flagging corrupt practices by judges in the eve [towards the end] of their careers, and here we have an ACJ indulging in these very activities with impunity,” one of the letters said.

In his last letter on August 17, Justice Mehta uses terms like “rampant nepotism and favouritism” to describe the ACJ’s actions.

‘Long rope'

He said it was “beyond comprehension” why “such a long rope” was given to a judge whose request for repatriation to the Rajasthan High Court was not accepted by the Supreme Court Collegium in March 2023.

Justice Sharma, who had served in Patna and then the Punjab and Haryana High Court, was finally recommended for repatriation to the Rajasthan High Court in a Supreme Court Collegium meeting on May 26, 2025. He was appointed Acting Chief Justice of Rajasthan in September last year, and has been holding the post for over 10 months.

“I have been repeatedly requesting you to take a decision for appointing a Chief Justice from another State to the Rajasthan High Court so that this unfortunate situation can be prevented. Continued ignorance of the request, in my opinion, is wholly against the interest of the institution,” Justice Mehta wrote to the CJI.

At one point, the Supreme Court judge also considered putting his letter in the public domain so that it might trigger an “inflow of information”. He has not heard from the CJI on the issue since August 17. A Supreme Court official said the CJI is currently on an official tour abroad.

World.title: TDP’s bond with BCs stronger than ever before, asserts Rajya Sabha member Vijay
World.content:
Rajya Sabha member Chintakayala Vijay on Wednesday said the foundation for TDP’s bond with the Backward Classes (BCs) had been laid with the provision of 34% reservation for those communities in the local bodies in 1987 by then Chief Minister N.T. Rama Rao.

The bond had since become stronger than ever before as the TDP went on to implement a slew of welfare schemes for the BCs, he added.

In contrast, the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) had reduced the quota for BCs in the local bodies from 34% to 23.14%, thereby robbing them of over 16,800 posts. This showed the YSRCP’s hollow claims to be supportive of the BCs, he argued.

Addressing the media at the TDP central office at Mangalagiri, Mr. Vijay said his own elevation to the Upper House of Parliament was a testament to the genuine commitment of Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and HRD Minister Nara Lokesh to the uplift of ordinary BC workers, and criticised the YSRCP and the Congress party for treating BCs as a vote bank.

He alleged that the YSRCP government had not allocated a single rupee and did not provide minimum facilities for the 50-plus BC Corporations. It had diverted the BC Sub-Plan funds and cut down on loans to the BC communities, he alleged.

The YSRCP was playing the BC card to divert attention from the ongoing Enforcement Directorate probes into their liquor scams and complicity of its leaders in various other scandals, Mr. Vijay said, warning the YSRCP of far worse plight in the 2029 elections if it did not change its ways.

‘Jagan spreading lies’

Meanwhile, Minister for Excise and Mines & Geology Kollu Ravindra condemned YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy for spreading blatant lies and fabricating stories about the prevailing weather in the State.

He pointed out that El Nino was not impacting Andhra Pradesh alone but the whole country, and to grapple with it, the government had drawn up its priorities with due focus on mitigating the damage to the agriculture and allied sectors.

Mr. Ravindra questioned why did the YSRCP MLAs stay away from the Legislative Assembly if they really cared about public issues, and what did Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy achieve for the people by holding press meets outside.

The government was providing ₹20,000 annual financial assistance to farmers and tenant farmers and taking various market intervention measures to solve the problems being faced by the farmers with due focus on protecting them from the fury of El Nino.

World.title: Abhimanyu bids adieu to Dasara duties with ceremonial farewell
World.content:
The iconic tusker Abhimanyu, who carried the golden howdah six times in a row during the Jamboo Savari and remained an integral part of Mysuru Dasara for over two decades, on Wednesday bid adieu to his Dasara responsibilities. He was accorded a ceremonial send-off during the Gajapayana at Veeranahosahalli, on the outskirts of the Nagarahole Tiger Reserve.

It was an emotional moment for Abhimanyu’s mahout and kavadi, Vasanth and Karthik, as well as forest staff and officials, who have witnessed the veteran tusker’s remarkable contribution to Dasara over the years. Abhimanyu is regarded as one of the celebrated members of the Dasara jumbo squad and the Forest Department.

Vasanth and Karthik also bid farewell to the tusker who will no longer be part of the Dasara festivities from this year.

All eyes were on Abhimanyu after the Forest Department announced that a ceremonial farewell would be accorded to him during the Gajapayana. A large number of people gathered to witness the special moment and captured it on their cameras. Crowds clapped and blew whistles to celebrate the veteran tusker’s contribution and selfless service to Mysuru Dasara.

Some Dasara elephants become part of the festival’s enduring legacy through their exceptional service and distinctive contributions. Abhimanyu now joins the illustrious list of elephants whose association with Dasara will be remembered for generations, having played a defining role in the festivities and carried the golden howdah with remarkable dignity and precision.

The emotional farewell to the veteran tusker was witnessed by elected representatives, senior officials and dignitaries, who joined forest staff and the public in acknowledging Abhimanyu’s invaluable contribution to the world-famous Mysuru Dasara.

World.title: 14 infants killed in fire at Pims' gynae ward in Islamabad
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Fourteen infants were killed in a fire that broke out in the gynaecology ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) early on Wednesday.

Footage showed rescue workers using ladders to reach broken windows to access the affected area and grief-stricken women sitting on the ground outside the hospital. An AFP reporter saw a woman in tears and a man clear glass from two broken windows, as security guards stood at the entrance to the medical facility.

Several witnesses, their hands and faces blackened from the smoke, told AFP they waited hours for help from the emergency services. They were forced to smash through windows to try and get to the neonatal intensive care unit.

Others said they came across locked doors and alleged guards prevented those inside the building from leaving as the fire raged.

In a statement, the Islamabad administration said that the fire broke out on the third floor of the Mother and Child Hospital’s ward. It said that rescue teams rushed to the scene, with six fire brigade vehicles and four ambulances taking part in the rescue operation.

“The fire was immediately brought under control and the children were immediately shifted to the intensive care unit,” it said, adding that 14 children “were completely burnt”.

Pims Spokesperson Dr Aneeza Jalil told Dawn that 15 babies were in the ward. “At least one baby was saved by a doctor,” she said.

Speaking to reporters in Islamabad in the afternoon, Health Minister Mustafa Kamal vowed that “no one responsible for negligence, including me, will be spared”.

Noting that he arrived in the federal capital from Karachi at 3:30pm, Kamal said he will present himself to his superiors for accountability.

Providing details of the incident, he said: “At 6:38am, it can be seen in the CCTV footage that there was a spark in the AC, then a fireball could be seen erupting out of it and landing on the floor of the ward. In one minute, at 6:39am, four people, including two nurses and two doctors, could be seen rushing for help and around the same time, the whole room was engulfed in flames”.

The health minister said the incident was being investigated by “experts, different institutions including us”, adding that “nothing will remain hidden and all facts will be unearthed”.

He continued: “Apparently, it seems that 14 out of the 15 infants were connected to oxygen tubes and it was that oxygen which caught flame.”

Kamal reiterated that the “heart-wrenching” incident will be investigated and warned that “if there was any negligence, then as I said, we will not spare them, including myself”.

The minister further said that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had instructed him “not to speak about certain issues”. He said he would be meeting the premier and that the two had been in touch.

“Everyone is on board, and the findings will be presented,” he said.

On being asked if he was going to tender his resignation, the health minister said, “As I have said before, whoever is responsible [..] they will not be spared. I have said what I can, and I wish I could say more, but the prime minister is my boss, and whatever his orders will be, I can only say that.”

The federal minister was also questioned about fire safety standards at Pims, with a reporter pointing out that the hospital had been issued notices for the past eight years.

Kamal claimed that the hospital had ensured compliance each time a notice had been issued in the past, pointing out that the blaze was contained with “26 fire extinguishers available in the building”.

When a reporter asked about his early morning statement over the lack of adequate facilities at Pims and “why in his 2-2.5 years as a health minister, no improvement had been made”, the minister, getting visibly frustrated, said, “If it has been 2-2.5 years, then feel free to shoot me” and clarified that he had only been at his position for one year and two months.

“What I said in the morning has to be seen within a certain parameter. I was saying that even if this did not happen, there are still challenges at the hospital. It has a capacity of 200-300 OPDs, and today, it has a footfall of over 9,000 people”.

He maintained that he was merely presenting facts. “I am not saying that everything is ideal.”

When pointed out that it was his responsibility to upgrade the facility, Kamal acknowledged his role and said, “We have to do it, but things cannot be ideal given the current scenario, but if we go into that, the conversation will take a different turn”.

The minister reiterated that every responsible person will be held accountable. “If I am willing to present myself for accountability, then no one else is left.

“Wherever there has been negligence, we will fix it,” he said. Noting that such an incident should not have happened, he said: “Will get to its root cause and ensure prevention in the future.”

The minister was also asked about reports that the door of the ward was locked, to which he said that access to the ward was limited and guarded due to “instances of people stealing newborn babies a couple of years back”.

“You would not see that anywhere else in the world, but we have the issue, so the door had to be manned with a guard,” Kamal explained.

During his media talk, the minister got into a verbal altercation with an individual who asked when action would be taken against those responsible. As the individual got louder, the minister repeatedly gestured to him to come forward and said, “Sir, come here and talk to me.”

‘Give me my child back’

Malik Israr, whose niece was admitted to the gynae ward, told Dawn that it was unfortunate the nursery was housed in a building in which repair and renovation work was ongoing.

“After the fire erupted, they told patients to vacate the building. Women who had just given birth had to rush down the stairs from the second floor,” he said.

A worker removes broken pieces of a glass window after a fire broke out at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in Islamabad on Aug 26, 2026. — Reuters

Khurram Mehmood, 40, told AFP he lost his three-day-old daughter in the blaze and that rescuers took hours to arrive.

“I lost my daughter. She was only three days old,” he said. “My wife was in the ward. They took everyone out. We were sitting on the road waiting for help.”

He added, “The fire erupted at 6am, rescue and authorities reached at 9am; people were helping themselves.”

“Give me my child back,” Jaweria, who lost her newborn, said outside the hospital. “I want justice.”

She told AFP: “Rescue teams arrived too late. Police arrived after four hours and said they are here to investigate. To hell with you, rescue team and police. Babies burnt to death there, but nobody could save them.”

Jaweria (2nd R), who said she lost her child in the fire, reacts following the blaze at the Mother and Child Health (MCH) ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) in Islamabad on Aug 26, 2026. — AFP

“For two hours I kept crying and wailing,” the mother said, questioning the action taken by hospital staff and emergency responders.

“Why did the doctors leave the children there? One nurse, one doctor, one gynaecologist, one paediatrician — there was nobody in the entire ward. Why were they not there?”

Mudasir, another parent who also lost his child, said all doors of the ward, except one, were shut and that there was “no fire security” in the ward.

A mother with black residue from the smoke on her hands stood crying outside the hospital as she held her 10-day-old baby in her arms.

“People were screaming. There was black smoke. We ran for our lives. Thank god my baby is safe,” Shagufta Parveen told AFP.

A man consoles a grieving father (C) as his child’s coffin is carried after a fire outside the Mother and Child Health (MCH) ward at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) hospital in Islamabad on Aug 26, 2026. — AFP

Ali Abbas, 20, was with his sister who was a patient in the ward.

“There was a short circuit in the nursery, in the children’s ward,” he said. “It was full of smoke.”

Eyewitness Abdul Ghafoor told AFP that there was “thick black smoke inside and patients were trapped”.

“I barged in to try to save as many people as I could, but we could not reach the ward where the patients were.

“The fire was in the nursing room, and we could not see anything. Some of us broke the windows to help people get out.”

Among the victims were the twin daughters of Bahadur Khan, a vegetable seller, The New York Times reported. He had left them with their mother to get some rest at home. Bahadur said his wife was recovering in Pims’ intensive care unit and was not aware of the deaths of their three-day-old daughters.

Alam Zaib, the father of a newborn child who was in another ward and remained safe, was quoted as saying that he tried to enter the ward where the fire broke out, but the door was locked.

Pims, established in 1985, is Islamabad’s biggest public sector hospital. It is one of the oldest health facilities in the federal capital and comprises several hospitals and teaching institutes.

Fires in large buildings are frequent in Pakistan, often due to poor safety laws and building codes as well as lax enforcement.

Federal health secretary removed

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif took notice of the incident and directed the relevant authorities to investigate it. According to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), he expressed deep sorrow and grief at the incident and offered his condolences to the bereaved families.

“Such a situation involving children is unbearable,” the statement quoted him as saying.

“The circumstances that led to the incident should be thoroughly reviewed, those responsible should be identified, and the strictest possible action should be taken,” he said.

In a second statement, the PMO said the prime minister had suspended and removed federal Health Secretary Muhammad Aslam Ghauri.

The premier chaired a high-level meeting on the incident, where he expressed his anger and issued directives for “strict action”, the PMO said in another statement.

It also stated that the prime minister suspended the federal health secretary and asked him to leave the meeting.

The statement quoted the prime minister as saying: “I am heartbroken at this tragic incident and share the parents’ grief.”

Subsequently, Captain (retired) Muhammad Mahmood, a BS-21 officer of the Pakistan Administrative Service (PAS), was appointed to the post of health secretary for three months “or till the posting of a regular incumbent,” a notification issued by the Cabinet Secretariat said.

According to the PMO, a high-level inquiry committee, headed by former interior secretary Shahid Khan, has launched an investigation.

State-run APP reported that Establishment Division Secretary Dr Barrister Nabeel Awan was also included in the committee.

Further, a notification issued by the Islamabad district magistrate said that a fact-finding committee, headed by the additional deputy commissioner general (ADCG), had been formed to determine the facts behind the fire.

The members of the committee included the CES director general, the City police station superintendent, the assistant commissioner (Industrial Area), the director general of Capital Development Authority’s (CDA) Electrical and Mechanical wing, along with representatives from Pims and Islamabad Electric Supply Company.

The committee was tasked with determining the exact cause of the fire, assessing whether adequate and functional fire-safety measures were in place, and evaluating the response time and effectiveness of the rescue and fire-fighting operations.

The notification said that a report would be furnished within 24 hours.

Ambulances are parked outside a mortuary following a deadly fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in Islamabad on August 26, 2026. — AFP

Minister of State for Law Barrister Aqeel Malik assured in a post on X that a “complete, transparent, and impartial investigation of the incident will be conducted to determine the true causes of this catastrophe and any possible negligence”.

“In the event that negligence or failure is proven at any level, strict action will be taken against the responsible individuals in accordance with the law,” he added, extending his condolences to the bereaved families and expressing grief over the incident.

Meanwhile, PPP leader Nayyar Hussain Bokhari, who reached Pims along with Senator Sherry Rehman and others, demanded that the head of the MCH be removed.

Bokhari said it was not just negligence but rather criminal negligence and should not be ignored.

Rehman said the Pims’ executive director must “answer why the system here keeps being akin to gross negligence”.

“The health ministry now has no justification for taking public funds. It should be dissolved or devolved to the provinces,” she was quoted as saying by her party.

She insisted they were not visiting “to play politics” but were sent by the party leadership to raise questions on behalf of the public.

In a post on her X account, Rehman also shared a video of her visiting the ward.

“Totally gutted. People had to break windows and jump out. Emergency gate was closed, fire equipment not working, medical staff not present,” she wrote.

“Honestly, I would have resigned on the spot,” Rehman added later.

Tallal Chaudhry defends district administration

Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry insisted that there had not been any delay in the arrival of rescue teams and defended the district administration.

“After receiving information in the control room, they reached the hospital within six minutes,” the state minister said while speaking to the media in Islamabad.

He added that once the rescue teams assessed the situation, 19 people were rescued, including seven children, 1o mothers and two men.

He also said that administration officials “from the assistant commissioner to commissioner to the Islamabad IG” reached the hospital to monitor the situation. “Not only did they monitor but also assisted in the rescue operation,” he said.

Reiterating that rescue teams reached the site within six minutes, the state minister said, “There appears to be no negligence on the part of rescue services.”

However, he added, only the hospital administration could answer for the arrangements present within the hospital.

Chaudhry said that the bodies of all 14 infants had been handed over to their families.

He added that a report of the incident had been sent to the prime minister and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, who he said had been monitoring the situation.

On being asked if Pims met the CDA’s fire safety protocols, with a journalist also pointing out that his ministry had been issuing notices to the hospital for the past seven years, he acknowledged that notices had been issued.

“It is a huge institution, and notices were issued […] but what was complied with and what was not — as there are multiple buildings; we cannot conclude anything today, and an inquiry committee has been formed”.

Asked why the administration had not been active on the fire safety issue before, he said, “If there has been any negligence, the inquiry committee will find out.”

An inquiry committee has been formed for a “high-powered” investigation into the incident, Chaudhry noted. He said the committee will collect evidence — CCTV footage, presence of flammable equipment, why the door was locked, the number of doctors and nurses present — and present its findings.

In its update on the incident, CDA said fire and rescue teams reached the site within seven minutes after a call was received at 6:54am.

Fire tenders, rescue teams, ambulances of the Capital Emergency Services (CES) and the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) administration were part of the deployed resources.

Nation expresses grief

President Asif Ali Zardari expressed heartfelt condolences and sympathy to the bereaved families. In a statement, the president said that the loss of lives was “heartbreaking and an irreparable loss”.

“Responsibility for the incident should be determined and action should be taken in accordance with the law,” he said.

Effective fire safety and emergency arrangements must be ensured in hospitals for the protection of patients, especially newborn babies, the president urged.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said he was deeply saddened by the incident.

“My deepest condolences to the bereaved parents and families. No words can ease the pain of losing an innocent child. May Allah Almighty grant the families strength and sabr in this unimaginably difficult hour,” he said.

As per the prime minister’s orders an immediate and thorough investigation will establish the causes of this tragic incident to ensure that those found responsible face the strictest action. The safety of our children must remain paramount,” he said.

PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari wrote on X: “Mothers do not keep their children in the womb for nine months just so that, due to someone’s negligence, they burn alive as soon as they are born.

“The deaths of 14 newborns in the federal capital are one of the most horrific tragedies in human history. The helpless fathers, whose lamps of hope were extinguished the very instant they were lit, are seeking justice.”

In a statement earlier in the day, he described the incident as an “unbearable tragedy for the entire nation”. He called for an impartial investigation into the incident and said the nation be informed how such a tragedy occurred at a major hospital.

“Those responsible for negligence or failing to ensure the safety of patients must be held accountable,” he added, stressing that the federal government must ensure the safety of patients and medical staff at all hospitals under its administration.

First Lady and MNA Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari also expressed “profound grief and sorrow over the tragic loss of newborn babies” and conveyed her “deepest sympathies to the bereaved families”.

“The loss of innocent newborn lives is heartbreaking and deeply distressing,” a statement by the Presidency quoted her as saying.

She called for a “thorough, swift and transparent investigation” into the incident.

PML-N President Nawaz Sharif said he was “deeply grieved” to hear about the deaths. He urged the government to take strict action against those responsible and ensure measures were put in place to prevent such incidents in the future.

Senate Chairman Syed Yousuf Raza Gilani expressed deep grief and sorrow over the tragic incident. In a statement, he offered his condolences to the families affected.

He said effective safety measures, fire safety systems and all necessary arrangements to deal with emergencies must be ensured in hospitals to prevent such incidents.

“Any negligence in safety measures is unacceptable,” he said. Gilani urged the relevant authorities to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the incident and take effective and practical steps to prevent such tragedies in the future.

National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq also expressed profound grief and sorrow over the deaths of the infants.

In a statement, he said he was “heartbroken” over the incident and shared equally in the pain and grief of the bereaved parents.

United Nations International Children’s Emergency Fund (Unicef) called for an urgent review as it expressed grief over the incident.

“Unicef is deeply saddened by the tragic loss of at least 14 newborn lives following a fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in Islamabad today.

“We extend our deepest condolences to the bereaved families and all those affected by this devastating incident,” it said in a statement.

The UN agency added, “ Every newborn deserves a safe start to life, and every mother and child should be able to receive care in a safe, secure health facility.

It called for the urgent review and strengthening of fire prevention and safety standards across health facilities.

The British High Commission in Pakistan termed the incident “heartbreaking news”.

“Our deepest condolences and thoughts are with the parents and families at this unimaginably difficult time,” it said.

Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Ministry also expressed “deepest condolences and sincere sympathy” to the families of the infants and to the people and the government of Pakistan.

“The kingdom expresses its solidarity with the families of the victims and stands with the government and people of Pakistan in the face of this great tragedy, wishing the Islamic Republic of Pakistan and its brotherly people security and peace,” the statement read.

The Turkish embassy said it was “deeply saddened by the tragic loss of newborn lives”,

“We extend our heartfelt condolences and deepest sympathies to the bereaved families. Our thoughts and prayers are with them at this profoundly painful time. May Allah grant them strength, patience and solace,” it said on X.

Spain’s embassy also extended heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families. “Our thoughts are with all those affected by this heartbreaking tragedy.”

The French embassy shared the sentiment, describing the incident as “deeply distressing”.

“Our hearts go out to the families who lost their newborn children in the tragic fire at Pims in Islamabad. Loss of innocent lives is heartbreaking and deeply distressing. Embassy of France extends its deepest sympathies to bereaved families and everyone affected by this tragedy,” it said in its message on X.

The Pakistan Medical Association (PMA) said in a statement that it was in “deep mourning” over the incident.

“The association reiterates that healthcare facilities are designed to protect and restore human lives, yet administrative failure and regulatory oversight lapses have turned these institutions into danger zones,” it said.

It demanded action against officials “whose failure to uphold safety codes resulted in this catastrophe”. It also demanded enforcing strict consequences so that “systemic failure serves as a decisive warning, preventing future lapses across both public and private medical facilities”.

It further said that there should be immediate restructuring and public accountability of health regulatory authorities responsible for enforcing safety protocols, building codes and emergency infrastructure in hospitals.

The PMA also called for “full institutional backing for the grieving parents, ensuring they receive complete legal, financial, and emotional justice”.

Search for Justice (SFJ) and Children Advocacy Network (CAN) Pakistan, a collective platform of local civil society organisations working for the protection and rights of children, also expressed their deep sorrow.

“The death of newborn children in a place entrusted with their treatment and care is deeply distressing and raises serious questions about safety and emergency preparedness,” said Rashida Qureshi, programme manager at SFJ and spokesperson for CAN Pakistan.

In its statement, the Islamabad Citizens Network (ICN) said, “This is not merely an unfortunate accident; it is a national tragedy in which innocent newborns, entirely dependent on the hospital system, its staff and state-provided arrangements for their safety and survival, lost their lives.”

It contended that an inquiry committee headed by an ADC was “neither adequate nor appropriate given the gravity of the tragedy and the need to determine possible administrative, criminal and institutional responsibility”.

ICN demanded an immediate judicial inquiry and an independent investigation into allegations by parents regarding the absence of staff, emergency exits and other administrative lapses.

It recalled that similar tragic incidents had occurred in Lahore’s Services Hospital in June 2012, the National Institute of Child Health (NICH) in Karachi in January 2020, and the nursery of Sahiwal Teaching Hospital in June 2024.

Civil Society Network Pakistan (CSNP) called upon Federal Constitution Court’s (FCC) Chief Justice Aminuddin Khan to take immediate notice on a suo motu basis or initiate appropriate constitutional proceedings on serious human rights violations arising out of the babies’ deaths.

CSNP President Advocate Abdullah Malik told Dawn that he has also requested the FCC chief justice to consider constituting a high-level, independent and transparent inquiry to determine the exact cause and circumstances of the fire at Pims.

Additional input from AFP, Reuters and Nasir Iqbal

World.title: Search team reaches suspected location of Pakistani climber Asma Mushtaq's body on Spantik, says minister
World.content:
A recovery team reached the spot where the body of deceased Pakistani climber Asma Mushtaq was suspected to be buried under the snow on Gilgit-Baltistan’s Spantik Peak, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said on Wednesday.

He added that the operation to retrieve the body was under way.

The 34-year-old climber died on Aug 20 while descending from the mountain, also known as Golden Peak, after suffering from high-altitude sickness. Her body was said to be at Camp 3, which is located at a height of approximately 6,250 metres.

Efforts to retrieve her body were earlier disrupted due to severe weather.

In an update posted to social media, Tarar said that the search team had reached the place where the body was suspected to be. “However, because the place is very large and due to heavy snowfall over the past two days, the body is now completely covered under the snow, making it difficult to locate,” he added.

According to the information minister, the rescue team’s search operation had been ongoing for two hours as of around 4pm and was continuing.

Alpine Club of Pakistan General Secretary Ayaz Shigri told Dawn that the six-member local team was making efforts to locate Mushtaq’s body.

“As the peak received fresh snowfall, it is feared that her body might be covered under snow.”

Highlighting that the team consists of highly professional climbers, Shigri said it would continue its efforts to locate the body.

He said Pakistan Army helicopters were expected to airlift Mushtaq’s body to Skardu after its arrival at the base camp.

The team had resumed its search operation on Tuesday once weather conditions improved, after heavy snowfall had halted the retrieval efforts on Sunday.

During her ascent, Mushtaq had successfully reached the 7,027-metre summit of Spantik and was in good health at the time, the ACP said in statements issued on Thursday.

However, she developed a serious high-altitude medical emergency at an elevation of about 6,400 metres during the descent.

High-altitude sickness encompasses a range of pulmonary and cerebral conditions caused by hypoxia, or oxygen deprivation, due to rapid ascent and inadequate acclimatisation to high altitudes.

Shigri earlier told Dawn that Mushtaq was part of a five-member Pakistani women’s expedition team that summited Spantik, which included climbers Zoni Aslam, Zaba Shigri, Shama and Sohana.

Climate change-induced shifts in weather patterns have worsened conditions on the peaks of the Karakoram Range in GB, creating serious difficulties for mountaineers.

Additional input from Jamil Nagri

World.title: Massive flood near Tibet border kills at least 95 in Nepal: police
World.content:
At least 95 people were killed in Nepal on Wednesday after a massive flood tore through the border region with Tibet, a police spokesman told AFP.

“So far, 95 deaths have been reported,” spokesman Abi Narayan Kafle said, adding that some 28 police personnel were also missing.

Hundreds of tourists were still out of contact hours after the disaster hit.

A torrent of mud and debris burst from the banks of a river between China and Nepal, burying buildings and triggering a frantic search for survivors.

Chinese state media reported “major casualties” from a mudslide at a Tibet trade hub on China’s side of its border with Nepal, and President Xi Jinping ordered an “all-out” rescue effort.

“I got a call from [my brother-in-law] this morning, and they were crying and said their entire house had been swept away. Three family members were rescued, but his brother is still missing,” said 56-year-old Raju Bhadel.

Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah urged the Himalayan nation to stand united after devastating flood.
